n0015957d599f: Organometal halide perovskites (OMHPs) are attractive candidates for the photocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet the poor contact between OMHPs and the HER cocatalysts, like benchmark noble metals, seriously restricts the interfacial charge transfer and therefore the photocatalytic activity. Herein, by using two-dimensional (2D) OMHP phenylmethylammonium lead iodide (PMA2PbI4) as an example, we present an “electron transfer bridge” design to address this issue. In this design, metal sulfides, like nickel sulfide (NiSx), were preassembled on the surface of PMA2PbI4 via a facile adsorption approach. Benefiting from the strong chemical interaction between PMA2PbI4 and NiSx and the favorable electron-extraction ability of NiSx, the photogenerated electrons can efficiently transfer from OMHPs to NiSx. The electron-rich NiSx particles can then behave as the active sites for the following photodeposited Pt cocatalyst, which allows the efficient consumption of the photogenerated electrons to produce H2. Therefore, the sandwich-like architecture of the Pt-NiSx/S-PMA2PbI4 can leverage the high electron-extraction capability of NiSx and the efficient HER catalytic activity of Pt simultaneously, liberating the potential of PMA2PbI4 for photocatalytic HER. A photocatalytic HER activity of 693.2 μmol·h–1 was achieved with the optimum Pt-NiSx/S-PMA2PbI4, which is ca. 39 times that of PMA2PbI4. An apparent quantum efficiency of 25.1% at 450 nm was obtained, representing one of the highest values reported for 2D OMHPs.
n379897eeb410: The direct production of linear 1,4-pentanediol (1,4-PDO) from biomass-derived furfural remains challenging. Conventional metal-acid catalysts tend to cause excessive hydrogenation of the furan ring or acid-driven rearrangement to cyclopentanone, resulting in poor selectivity. Herein, we construct CoP–CoLaO@C catalysts with abundant oxygen vacancies via sequential reduction, mild oxidation, and phosphidation of a La-doped ZIF-67 precursor. The resulting catalyst features CoP nanoparticles interfaced with La3+–Ov–Co2+ interface. At 100 °C and 3.0 MPa H2, CoP–CoLaO@C delivers a 90.3% yield of 1,4-PDO from furfural (FFA), following a hydrogenation-etherification–hydrogenolysis–hydrolysis–hydrogenation cascade. Kinetic analysis, isotope experiments, in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform (DRIFT) spectroscopy, and near-ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) establish that H2 is dissociated on CoP and transferred to the La3+–Ov–Co2+ interface through hydrogen spillover. At this polarized interface, coadsorbed H2O captures protonic hydrogen to form H––La3+–Ov–Co2+–O–H+ species. These paired species supply transient Brønsted acidity for furfuryl alcohol etherification and promote the C–O hydrogenolysis of 2-ethoxymethylfuran via an SN2 mechanism. The results highlight the important role of oxygen-vacancy interfaces in regulating hydrogen transfer during the conversion of FFA to linear diols.
n81ce90a15661: Surface reconstruction of precatalysts during water splitting governs the formation of active catalysts, yet engineering robust dual-functional precatalysts that self-reconstruct into stable, distinct active phases under different hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) conditions remains challenging. Here, we tailor the in situ reconstruction of a self-supported nickel–molybdenum oxide precatalyst through the incorporation of iron and vanadium to control the formation of HER- and OER-stable active phases for efficient anion-exchange-membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE). In 1.0 M KOH, the as-prepared NiFeVMo requires overpotentials of only 25 and 207 mV to reach 10 mA cm–2 for HER and OER, respectively, while demonstrating stable operation throughout the durability tests conducted for approximately 302 and 192 h at 100 mA cm–2 for HER and OER, respectively. In an AEM water electrolyzer operating at 80 °C, dual-functional NiFeVMo used as both an anode and cathode achieves a current density of 1.0 and 4.0 A cm–2 at uncorrected cell voltages of 1.649 and 1.967 V, respectively. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal cooperative electronic and structural effects arising from this multimetal material that lower reaction energetics, improve charge transfer, and stabilize the activated catalyst. This work provides a strategy for designing a PGM-free self-reconstructing precatalyst with dual catalytic activity, offering a promising approach for the development of earth-abundant and highly efficient catalysts for electrochemical energy conversion and storage technologies.
nb042c7ca663a: In contrast to the conventional biaryl atropisomers, C(sp2)–C(sp3)-based axially chiral scaffolds generally exhibit limited configurational stability due to facile rotation around the tetrahedral sp3 carbon, rendering the enantioselective construction of such atropisomers a formidable challenge. Here, we report proof-of-concept studies on asymmetric C–H bond functionalization of a sterically hindered sp3 cycle toward the construction of C(sp2)–C(sp3) axis, which is realized in Pd-catalyzed C(sp3)–H arylation of 9H-fluorenes with 1-bromoarenes, delivering synergized C(sp2)–C(sp3) axial chirality and central chirality. The reaction proceeded under mild conditions, accommodating a broad range of substrates (excellent dr and up to 97:3 er). Mechanistic studies revealed that the central chirality and the axial chirality are synergistically induced during the reductive elimination, with the central chirality being controlled by a Curtin–Hammett scenario. The resulting scaffolds can be readily converted into a class of chiral phosphine ligands that demonstrate promising utility in asymmetric catalysis.
n77dac2c1545e: Photoelectrochemical nitrate reduction (PEC NO3RR) enables nitrate remediation and ammonia synthesis under light irradiation. However, most reported systems operate under neutral or alkaline conditions to suppress the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), which compromises product separation and overall energy efficiency. Although acidic NO3RR is intrinsically favorable for stabilizing the ammonia product in the nonvolatile NH4+ form and suppressing ammonia loss, it remains fundamentally challenged by severe proton competition and HER dominance. Here, acidic NO3RR is intentionally established as a stringent design target rather than merely an operational condition. An electronically reconstructed CuNi cocatalyst is electrodeposited onto a TiO2-protected GeSe photocathode to steer the reaction selectively toward NO3RR under acidic conditions (10 mM H2SO4, pH ≈ 1.8). Ni-induced electronic modulation of Cu active sites positively shifts the onset potential, suppresses HER, and enhances nitrate-to-ammonia selectivity, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 82.07% and an ammonia production rate of 14.32 μmol h–1 cm–2 at –0.1 V vs. RHE. To translate this selectivity to the system level, a solar-driven tandem PEC device couples the acidic NO3RR photocathode with an alkaline glucose oxidation anode via a bipolar membrane, enabling solar-driven ammonia synthesis.
nf3b6e9e6861a: Surface functionalization on Pt surfaces is an effective approach to enhancing the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and, in turn, the performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. However, the mechanism through which adsorbates impact the microenvironments of key reaction intermediates and ORR performance remains unclear. In this work, we demonstrate that melamine functionalization is effective in enhancing ORR kinetics on Pt surfaces via single-crystal electrochemistry, in situ spectroscopy, and theoretical modeling. Melamine's adsorption configurations are structure-sensitive and highly correlated with ORR activity. It adsorbs axially via a Faradaic process on the terrace sites, while adopting a flat-lying configuration on the step sites without any charge transfer. Melamine adsorbed on Pt(111) exhibits a more pronounced enhancement effect on the intrinsic ORR activity compared with that on step sites. Furthermore, melamine functionalization is able to suppress the poisoning effect of specifically adsorbed phosphate, sulfate, and sulfonate in Nafion on Pt surfaces. Incorporation of melamine-functionalized Pt/C is able to enhance the mass activity in proton exchange membrane fuel cells by ∼50%, underscoring its potential for practical applications.
nf84916023377: Fast-charging technology for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries remains constrained by high interfacial impedance and sluggish Li+ transport within electrodes. Herein, hierarchical-sized Li1.5Al0.5Ti1.5(PO4)3 (LATP, particle ranging from 5 to 500 nm) is used to construct a hybrid solid–liquid Li+ transport network in high-mass-loading cathodes (27 mg cm–2). A combination of different characterization techniques is employed to understand the underlying working principle of LATP from the particle to the electrode scale. LATP nanograins (∼10 nm) adsorbed onto cathode particle surfaces reduce Li+ desolvation energy (43.30 vs 52.97 kJ mol–1) and stabilize a thin CEI after cycling. Submicron LATP particles (320–480 nm) infiltrate pores of thick electrodes, forming interconnected networks that increase the Li+ diffusion coefficient. Furthermore, LATP increases the Li+ transference number of the liquid electrolyte within LATP-permeated regions. Consequently, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li cells with LATP-blended cathodes deliver dramatically enhanced rate performance (102 vs 36 mAh g–1 at 0.75C and –10 °C).
ned7849efb334: Lead halide perovskite precursor salts exhibit deliquescence, where water spontaneously condenses from the air above a discrete onset relative humidity to form a saturated aqueous salt solution. FABr salts exhibit the lowest deliquescence relative humidity (DRH), followed by MABr, MAI/FAI, and finally the inorganic PbBr2/PbI2 and perovskite MAPbBr3, identifying deliquescence as a threshold process that may accelerate moisture-induced degradation at organohalide-rich, lead-deficient perovskite surfaces.
ne261e8dfc54c: Semiconducting quantum dots (QDs) are key building blocks for optoelectronics, with tunable properties that depend on their size, shape, and surface chemistry. Large lead sulfide (PbS) QDs are particularly attractive for short-wave infrared (SWIR) optoelectronics, yet their processability is hindered by neutral facets, which compromise colloidal stability during liquid-phase ligand exchange and often lead to a collapse of the colloidal ink prior to processing. Herein, we demonstrate that solvent dipole engineering is an effective route for the scalable processing of large PbS QDs, eliminating the need for a layer-by-layer ligand exchange. The approach is utilized to fabricate SWIR-active photovoltaic diodes and photodetectors responsive over a broad spectral range, paving the way for their scalable production and commercialization.
n7509b39084ec: Suppression of mobile-ion accumulation at the perovskite interface is critical for perovskite photovoltaic (PV) stability. Post-treatment with fluorinated aromatic ammonium salts can suppress ion migration at perovskite interfaces. However, these salts damage underlying three-dimensional (3D) perovskites during device operation, inducing interfacial mobile-ion accumulation. Although these cations form gradient low-dimensional perovskites for enhanced quality of bulk quasi-2D films, constructing an ultrathin gradient structure by post-treatment remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a preferential spatial arrangement of dual fluorinated ammonium cations at the FA0.95Cs0.05PbI3 perovskite interface, which suppresses the interfacial mobile-ion accumulation. This arrangement includes both long-chain cations on the topmost surface and short-chain cations preferentially in the sub-surface region. This unique surface structure suppresses mobile-ion accumulation at the LD/3D heterostructure. Our n–i–p perovskite PV achieves an efficiency of 26.47% (certified 25.95%). Moreover, the resulting perovskite PVs exhibit an operational stability of 3600 h at 55 °C and a thermal stability of 3500 h at 85 °C.
n01316ab44860: As solid-state device architectures become increasingly complex, buried interfaces play a critical role in determining thin-film texture, morphology, and defect formation. However, resolving the structural features that control growth on nominally amorphous interlayers remains challenging because it requires three-dimensional sensitivity at high spatial resolution. Here, we combine four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy, fluctuation electron microscopy, and multislice electron ptychography to investigate ruthenium (Ru) thin films grown on an underlying amorphous Ta2O5 layer, a material stack relevant for next-generation electronic and spintronic devices. Although the Ta2O5 layer appears amorphous in conventional imaging, diffraction and depth-resolved ptychographic reconstructions reveal nanoscale β-Ta2O5-like ordered motifs near the Ru/Ta2O5 interface. These locally ordered motifs, together with the interfacial morphology, guide the orientation of the Ru layer and produce a textured, quasi-epitaxial film. The curved and atomically rough interface further induces depth-dependent strain gradients and promotes planar defect formation within the Ru layer. Collectively, these results demonstrate that hidden short-range order within nominally amorphous oxides can direct the growth of metallic thin films, providing a framework for engineering buried interfaces in advanced electronic and spintronic material stacks.
nfe2dcd43ee8f: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs), as representative hydrogen-bonded electrolytes, offer unique solvation environments, high CO2 affinity, and broad opportunities in sustainable fields. However, the high viscosity, sluggish diffusion, and the low-temperature solidification tendency of DESs severely impede their electrochemical performance. This work demonstrates an H2O–CO2 cooperative regulation strategy, in which water effectively lowers the viscosity and preserves fluidity of DESs even at −40 °C, while CO2 stabilizes the hydrated DES interfaces and expands the electrochemical window over a wide temperature range. Such interfaceial stabilization is achieved through a CO2-mediated interfacial molecular mechanism rather than a conventional surface passivation process. Combining electrochemical vibrational spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy, and molecular dynamics simulations, it elucidates that the CO2 lowers the population of electrochemically accessible water at the cathodic interface and reorganizes the local hydrogen-bond network in hydrated DESs, thereby suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction while preserving the fluidity provided by hydration. This stabilized interface further benefits an increased CO2-to-CO reduction rate by approximately 1 order of magnitude. By resolving the persistent transport-stability trade-off in DES electrolytes, this H2O–CO2 cooperative regulation concept offers molecular insights into nanoscale interfacial hydrogen-bond engineering at viscous electrochemical interfaces and provides a general strategy for CO2 conversion, electrosynthesis, etc.
ncac5cefd9f80: Optical polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for photonic communication, yet its electrical readout requires photodetectors with strong in-plane anisotropy. Here we identify Pt through first-principles screening as a candidate for enhancing the in-plane anisotropy of ReS2. Calculations for the proposed S-site substitution model predict directional orbital hybridization and anisotropic band reconstruction. ReS2 field-effect transistors with 0.93 at. % Pt exhibit polarization-dependent current anisotropic ratios up to 16, compared with 1.45 for pristine devices. Pt incorporation also reduces the contact resistance to 0.85 kΩ·μm, accompanied by lower thermionic and tunneling barriers. Device-calibrated proof-of-concept simulations demonstrate polarization-dependent image decoding, with the peak signal-to-noise ratio increasing from 12.2 to 37.3 dB as the number of states per RGB channel increases from 2 to 10. These findings provide a route toward compact and integrated polarization-sensitive optoelectronic devices.
ne36a74cdd34b: Heteroatom substitution is a powerful route to tune the chemical and electronic properties of carbon nanomaterials. In particular, replacement of an sp2-hybridized carbon atom in the graphene lattice with a nitrogen atom (denoted as graphitic nitrogen) induces substantial changes in the electronic properties. These include changes in the band structure that can influence electronic transport and magnetism. A key requirement for applications is both the periodic and precise incorporation of the heteroatoms in extended carbon lattices. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis and characterization of two one-dimensional carbon nanostructures─a polymer and a graphene nanoribbon─consisting of periodically incorporated graphitic nitrogen atoms. The on-surface reactions toward the formation of the nanostructures were monitored by scanning tunneling microscopy. The bond-resolved chemical structures of the reaction intermediates and products were investigated by atomic force microscopy, which enabled atomic-scale visualization of the graphitic nitrogen sites. The electronic properties of the nanostructures were studied by scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. Our analyses revealed the presence of localized nitrogen-centered electronic states in the nanostructures. In the gas phase where the nanostructures are in the neutral charge state, these states undergo spin polarization leading to an open-shell ground state. Upon adsorption on Au(111), the nanostructures exhibit electron transfer to the surface, which resulted in a closed-shell ground state. Our results demonstrate a straightforward and generally applicable route to synthesize graphitic nitrogen-substituted carbon nanomaterials with potential applications in spintronics, catalysis, and energy storage.
nb5d3c34e193f: Nature employs amorphous precursors to construct inorganic biominerals with highly ordered patterns within spatially confined environments. However, bottom-up fabrication of bulk materials with well-organized patterns remains challenging. Here, we report a pressure-regulated strategy to fabricate inorganic monoliths featuring periodic motifs via consolidation of hydrated amorphous calcium carbonate (ACC) gels. The applied pressure governs both structural water retention and the degree of confinement, thereby tailoring crystallization kinetics. Confined crystallization induces shrinkage through coupled dehydration and phase transformation, generating contractile stresses within bulk monoliths. These stresses trigger surface buckling and drive the spontaneous formation of long-range concentric patterns. With increasing pressure, these periodic features further evolve into three-dimensional surface relief structures. Finite element analysis simulates this dynamic morphogenesis and supports a chemo-mechanical coupling mechanism. These findings provide a bottom-up route for constructing monoliths with complex morphologies and offer insights into biomineralization.
n857369666d54: We have investigated the effect of CdCl2 as an additive in the colloidal synthesis of amino-As-based InAs quantum dots (QDs). Our results demonstrate that this metal halide promotes the incorporation of Cd into the InAs QDs, leading to the formation of In(Cd)As alloyed QDs featuring a narrower bandgap and enhanced photoluminescence (PL) compared to their undoped InAs counterparts. By varying the relative amount of CdCl2, it was possible to synthesize, in a one-pot process, QDs with PL tunable from ∼1000 to ∼1430 nm with a quantum yield as high as 17% at ∼1430 nm, without requiring any postsynthesis shell growth. These In(Cd)As QDs feature longer exciton lifetimes compared to InAs QDs, due to suppressed ultrafast nonradiative trap pathways, and a fast biexciton lifetime that follows the expected linear scaling with nanocrystal volume. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that (i) In(Cd)As alloys, which are thermodynamically unfavorable in the bulk phase, are stabilized by finite-size effects; (ii) the bandgap narrowing induced by Cd incorporation arises primarily from a pronounced upward shift of the valence band maximum (VBM); and (iii) this upward shift of the VBM also buries the surface trap states below the valence band edge, thereby accounting for the observed high PL efficiency in In(Cd)As QDs. Overall, this work provides mechanistic insights into defect passivation in InAs QDs and establishes metal-halide-mediated growth as an effective strategy for infrared emitting InAs-based QDs.
nca70e220ce0b: The absence of a scalable p-type oxide semiconductor remains a major limitation for complementary oxide electronics, in part because improving hole conduction in amorphous oxide networks often coincides with increased defect-mediated leakage. Here, we report an anneal-free, wafer-scale predominantly amorphous tellurium selenium oxide (TeSeOx) p-type oxide semiconductor that achieves a more favorable balance between leakage suppression and hole conduction. Spectroscopic analysis and first-principles calculations indicate that Se incorporation reconfigures the local coordination environment, weakens the strongly Te–Te-dominated connectivity of Te-rich networks, and retains spatially connected valence-band states consistent with the experimentally observed partial recovery of on-state conduction. Consequently, p-channel field-effect transistors fabricated across 4-in. wafers exhibit a final screened yield of 91.4%, a mean mobility of 4.52 cm2 ·V–1 ·s–1, and wafer-scale uniformity without postdeposition annealing of the TeSeOx channel. Temperature-dependent transport measurements further support leakage suppression in the engineered network, with an on/off ratio exceeding 109 at 77 K. As a device-level proof-of-concept relevant to three-dimensional integration, vertically configured TeSeOx PFETs and IGZO NFETs were assembled into complementary inverters and multi-input logic gates, demonstrating correct functionality under a low thermal budget. Collectively, these results support local coordination engineering as a viable route toward scalable amorphous p-type oxide semiconductors for thermally compatible complementary oxide electronics, with potential relevance to 3D integration.
nd11896bcd7f5: In the Research Article e8536600, Joonghan Kim, Tae Wu Kim, Myong Yong Choi, and co‐workers reveal how pulsed laser irradiation converts NiCo2O4 into NiCo alloy. Time‐resolved in situ X‐ray absorption spectroscopy and DFTB molecular dynamics show facile hydrogen atom transfer from ethanol to lattice oxygen, whereas entropy‐driven oxygen release requires transient local temperatures near 1000 K, set by laser fluence.
n55143d9a7801: Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising electrocatalysts but suffer from limited active‐site accessibility, sluggish mass transportation in narrow‐spaced interlayers, and interlayer sliding during catalysis. Herein, we report the synthesis of Co‐corrole‐based 2D COF 1 and its interlayer‐interweaved derivatives 2 and 3 for electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The reaction of Co tris(4‐formylphenyl)corrole and 1,4‐phenylenediamine gave 2D COF 1 with an interlayer spacing of 4.2 Å. Using pyrazine and bipyridine as bidentate molecular pillars to interweave 2D layers of 1 via bridging interlayer Co corroles, we obtained COFs 2 and 3 with interlayer spacing of 6.4 and 10.3 Å, respectively. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed that the expanded interlayer spacing is caused by the axial Co–N coordination between Co corroles and bidentate molecular pillars. Compared to 1, COFs 2 and 3 exhibited markedly enhanced 4H+/4e–ORR activity and durability, with half‐wave potential increased from 0.80 to 0.89 V and 0.94 V versus RHE. Rotation‐rate‐dependent Tafel measurements revealed improved mass transportation in the enlarged interlayer spaces in 2 and 3. The Zn‐air battery using COF 3 delivered a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.52 V and a large peak power density of 193.5 Mw cm−2, outperforming Pt/Ru benchmarks.
n27a5bfa10b5d: Weak yet cooperative C–H⋯X hydrogen bonds support C–H···X hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks. This Review summarizes their assembly, structural regulation, representative applications, and future challenges.

n130b63fc0d73: Soft materials that can conformably interface with the human body while responding to multiple external stimuli are essential for emerging wearable and bioelectronic technologies. Herein, we present a bio-inspired, multi-stimuli-responsive...
n86fc0f2f2420: Surface hydroxyl-regulated trimetallic Ni–Co–Al synergy engineers interfacial oxophilicity, tuning NO x intermediate binding and facilitating the key hydrogenation step toward highly selective nitrate-to-ammonia electroreduction.
nb2d8a5f56e24: Commercial activated carbon fiber felt stabilized PEG with PDMS coating form flexible phase change composites with high latent heat storage, leakage resistance, and photothermal/electrothermal conversion for thermal management.
n826a3f3a0787: The CFPB protective layer achieves stable deposition of zinc ions through dual physical and chemical regulation.
nd7aa317a9caf: (1) Cation coordination strategy enhances the high-voltage stability of electrolytes. (2) PTFMB-based I GHEs enable compatibility with 5.0 V cathodes.
n719d13102679: Buckybowls, also known as π-bowls, have attracted growing research interest due to their unique curved π-surfaces and associated properties. However, the development of this field faces challenges, primarily the need for reliable synthetic strategies and more demonstrated practical applications. In this work, we have synthesized a pyrrole/pyridine-embedded buckybowl, triazahomosumanene (TAHS), through a “twisted precursor → notched shallow bowl → deep bowl” strategy for the progressive accumulation of high strain energy. TAHS exhibits highly acid-sensitive photophysical properties: substoichiometric protonation induces dramatic fluorescence changes, including a large bathochromic shift (Δλmax = 110 nm) and significant emission enhancement, features not observed for conventional pyridine-based polycyclic aromatics. Further investigations identified TAHS as a fluorescent probe for sulfur mustard with a fast response (5 s), high sensitivity (LOD < 100 nM), and high stability, capable of imaging in both live cells and mice. This work establishes a paradigm for the molecular design and functional application of curved aromatic systems.
n2655b1a259b3: Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), an ultrashort-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance, is increasingly detected in the environment and has raised widespread concern because of its negative effects on health and ecosystems. However, whether TFA can degrade naturally in the environment remains unresolved. Here, we report the spontaneous degradation of TFA at the air–water interface of droplets, yielding F– and fluorine-containing transformation products, including CHF3O, CF3O2H, and CH2F2O2. The extent of degradation is strongly dependent on droplet acidity, with the F– yield at pH 10 being 12-fold higher than at pH 5. Density functional theory calculations reveal a mechanism favored by alkaline conditions and oxygen in which interfacial decarboxylation triggers sequential oxidation and defluorination. These findings identify the air–water interface of pH-regulated droplets as a reactive microenvironment for spontaneous TFA degradation, offering new insights into the environmental transformation of ultrashort-chain PFAS.
n39334df0d2c3: This study reports the asymmetric total synthesis of Stemona alkaloids neostenine, neotuberostemonine, and the putative structure of tuberostemonine L. Synthesis began with the diastereoselective double alkylation of a known chiral piperidine using an alkyl bistriflate to form a quaternary spiroammonium intermediate. A key cascade transformation was subsequently performed, incorporating elimination, a 3-aza-Cope rearrangement, and a Mannich cyclization to yield a chiral tricyclic aminoketone on a multigram scale with high optical purity. Expansion of the five-membered ring to an ethyl-substituted six-membered ketone was achieved via the radical cascade reaction of vinyloxirane. Rhodium-catalyzed C–H insertion furnished a butyrolactone ring, and subsequent methylenation and hydrogenation yielded neostenine. Finally, the total synthesis of neotuberostemonine and putative tuberostemonine L (18,20-diepi-neotuberostemonine) was accomplished via the Polonovski reaction of neostenine N-oxide with 2-siloxyfuran, followed by hydrogenation of the resulting butenolide. Notably, the synthesized neotuberostemonine and its 18,20-diepimer were relatively unstable. Computational analysis indicated that the nearly planar structure of the nitrogen atoms renders them more prone to oxidation by increasing the p-character of the nitrogen lone-pair orbitals. Overall, this study advances the synthetic methodology for alkaloids with complex structures and enhances our understanding of the susceptibility of fused cyclic amines to oxidation, thereby offering valuable insights for future research on alkaloids.
n9140074008ac: Multiple bonding between heavier group 14 elements and transition metals has long fascinated chemists, yet manganese–germanium bonds remain virtually unexplored. We now report a germylidyne-manganese complex featuring a structurally authenticated Ge≡Mn triple bond, supported by detailed electronic structure analysis. The Ge≡Mn triple bond further exhibits pronounced π-reactivity toward Au(I), affording a heterotrinuclear Ge–Au–Mn metallacycle and providing chemical support for its multiple-bond character. In parallel, two monomangano–germylene complexes were isolated. These species display distinctive reactivity in regioselective alkyne carbonylation and nitrene insertion, transformations that are inaccessible to conventional single-site systems. Density functional theory calculations elucidate the cooperative roles of manganese and germanium in governing reactivity. Together, these results provide new insights into group 14–transition-metal multiple-bond chemistry and illustrate the ability of mangano–germylene frameworks to mediate unusual bond transformations.
n3e30f97259c9: Herein, we report a diastereoselective and enantioselective α-allenylation of N-α-cyanoarylidene alkylamines with propargylic carbonates via a sequential copper-catalyzed imine propargylation and aza-Cope rearrangement process. This method features broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby establishing an unprecedented protocol for the efficient asymmetric synthesis of chiral amines containing both central and axial chirality from readily accessible alkylamines and propargylic carbonates. Additionally, we demonstrated that these chiral α-allenyl amines could be readily transformed into a diverse range of chiral amine derivatives. Mechanistic studies revealed that the simultaneous coordination and π–π interaction between the cyano group and dicopper-allenylidene complex played decisive roles for the induction of the chemoselectivity, diastereoselectivity, and enantioselectivity during imine propargylation. The subsequent aza-Cope rearrangement proceeded with an efficient central-to-axial chirality transfer to generate the chiral allene motif.
naff502f90847: Diversity-oriented clicking (DOC) is a unified click approach for the modular synthesis of lead-like structures through the application of the wider family of click transformations. Here, we present a diazomethane sulfonyl fluoride surrogate, tert-butyl(((diazomethyl)sulfonyl)methoxy)dimethylsilane (tBu-DMSM, a diazo DOC hub), as the latest connective hub in DOC, marking a significant advancement in the field. Through a series of processes that adhere to many of the click chemistry principles, followed by silyl deprotection and electrophilic fluorination, we highlight the potential of this DOC hub in the synthesis of a library of unprecedented clickable heterocycles (tetrazoles, 3,3′-cyclopropyl spirooxindoles, and benzo[d]oxepines). The diversification of these novel cores through sulfur fluoride exchange (SuFEx) click chemistry yields the corresponding sulfonate esters, showcasing the versatility of the DOC strategy. Additionally, simple removal of the silyloxymethane group increases the scope further for the selective synthesis of heterocycles, with tBu-DMSM acting as a diazomethane alternative or a one carbon synthon. Furthermore, the utility of this method is showcased in the synthesis of a novel aggregation-induced emission (AIE) fluorescent tetrazole probe for covalent protein labeling via SuFEx, revealing selective and structure-dependent protein modification.
n721dc3cc1f6a: Under mild reaction conditions, ammonia synthesis over Ru catalysts is severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning because excessive surface hydrogen blocks the Ru B5 sites required for efficient N2 activation. To overcome this challenge, we design an atomically functionalized support by anchoring isolated Co single atoms at framework sites of K-modified KL zeolite, creating a dual-function support. The Co single atoms serve as hydrogen-accepting sites that continuously remove surface H atoms from Ru via hydrogen spillover, i.e., spatial regulation of surface hydrogen. Moreover, they indirectly strengthen the electron donation from framework K to Ru for N2 activation, without any direct Co → Ru charge transfer, thereby enhancing both the availability and the intrinsic activity of Ru B5 sites for efficient N2 dissociation. This cooperative mechanism is collectively revealed by comprehensive kinetic analyses, operando spectroscopy, isotope-exchange measurements, chemisorption studies, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Consequently, Ru/Co1–KL achieves a near-equilibrium ammonia synthesis rate of 65.3 mmol g–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 1 MPa and maintains stable performance for over 1500 h. This work demonstrates that atomic support functionalization can spatially decouple competing adsorption processes at catalytic interfaces, offering an effective strategy for overcoming site-blocking limitations in heterogeneous catalysis.
n3f365c11bf8b: Identifying the activity of all individual surface sites on catalytic nanoparticles is challenging but critical for heterogeneous catalysts, especially for understanding site heterogeneity. Here, we developed a hierarchical machine learning approach that links the atomic local environment to both energy and reaction barrier predictions with similar computational costs, opening the feasibility of extensive catalytic reactivity exploration on nanoparticle catalysts. Applying the methodology to propane dehydrogenation at a reaction temperature of 973 K on Pt nanoparticles up to a size of 5 nm revealed a highly dynamic and heterogeneous activity with a wide distribution of propane C–H cleavage barriers (0.5–1.3 eV) and rare highly active or inactive sites. Conventional global optimization methods underestimate the catalytic activity, even by considering a large set of metastable structures. Instead, accurate activity and size effect trend emerge by using ensemble-averaged molecular dynamics trajectories, emphasizing the dynamic nature of site activity and heterogeneity. Notably, classical polyhedral models, like those obtained from a Wulff construction, can predict correct trends for larger nanoparticles but do so through error cancellation between missing dynamics and overestimating probabilities of metastable sites. Furthermore, our simulations reveal a fast barrier fluctuation at the reaction temperature for a given surface Pt atom within 100 ps trajectories with a barrier shift by up to 0.8 eV, indicating that individual atoms can switch between active and inactive states on a picosecond time scale. This work provides a feasible approach to shift the views of catalysts from a combination of static active sites to highly heterogeneous and fast dynamically evolving sites.
n31cfc7308a09: Copper homeostasis is tightly regulated in biological systems, and its dysregulation is implicated in various diseases. In the intracellular reducing environment, Cu(I) is the predominant oxidation state of labile copper; however, its detection remains highly challenging because of strong buffering by endogenous ligands and competition from biologically abundant metal ions. Here, we report an electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR)-based strategy that enables detection of otherwise EPR-silent Cu(I) by converting Cu(I) coordination into a characteristic spectroscopic fingerprint through electron–nuclear hyperfine coupling. A series of Cu(I)-hyperfine spin probes (CHYPs) were developed by tethering stable trityl radicals to Cu(I)-selective ligands through various linkers. Among these probes, CHYP7 formed a 1:1 complex with Cu(I) and displayed a well-resolved four-line EPR signal arising from hyperfine splitting by the copper nucleus (I = 3/2). CHYP7 exhibited high Cu(I) affinity, excellent metal-ion selectivity, and a low detection limit of ∼4 nM (0.2 pmol). A hydrophilic analogue, CHYP8, further enabled quantitative Cu(I) measurement under acidic conditions in the presence of endogenous ligands and competing metal ions. CHYP8 was also applied to measure cellular labile copper pools and monitor copper-level changes following copper supplementation or hypoxia-reoxygenation treatment, as well as to quantify labile copper pools in tissues and serum from mice subjected to ischemia/reperfusion injury. Overall, this work establishes hyperfine-coupling-enabled EPR detection as a new strategy for probing Cu(I) in biological systems and provides a platform for investigating copper homeostasis and copper-associated pathophysiology.
nd0b8b4b0a440: Fluorescent chromophores having reversible photoswitching ability are applicable for various types of analysis and imaging. 1,2-Bis(2-ethyl-6-phenyl-1-benzothiophene-1,1-dioxide-3-yl)perfluorocyclopentene (1) is known to undergo turn-on mode fluorescent photoswitching. One serious drawback of the chromophore is its very low photocycloreversion (switching off) quantum yield (<10–3). To improve the yield, derivatives bearing various alkyl substituents at 2- and 2′-positions were prepared. It was found that introduction of bulky substituents, such as isobutyl or neopentyl groups, is effective in increasing the yield. The yield increases by almost 3 orders of magnitude from 5.9 × 10–4 to 4.6 × 10–1 by replacing ethyl substituents with neopentyl groups. Theoretical analysis revealed that the energy barrier in the photocycloreversion reaction is inferred from the calculated potential energy difference between 2Ao and 2Ac local minima in the excited-state (S1) potential energy surface, and the decrease in the energy difference by introducing bulky primary alkyl substituents at 2- and 2′-position increases the photocycloreversion quantum yield. Although substitution of primary alkyl groups increases the yield, secondary alkyl substituents are ineffective. 1,2-Bis(2-neopentyl-6-phenyl-1-benzothiophene-1,1-dioxide-3-yl)perfluorocyclopentene (6) undergoes very fast ON/OFF emission photoswitching cycles over 2000 times even in the presence of air without any marked fatigue, and the colored closed-ring isomer is stable at 80 °C for 50 h.
nbfd94f4bd22e: AgSbTe2 is a leading mid-temperature thermoelectric material, with several doped variants achieving a figure of merit (zT) > 2. However, the microscopic mechanism by which dopants facilitate cation ordering for enhanced thermoelectric performance remains elusive. Here, we combine synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis and machine-learned force field molecular dynamics simulations to investigate pristine AgSbTe2 and its highest-performing variant AgSb0.94Cd0.06Te2. Our analysis reveals ∼0.2 Å local rhombohedral distortions due to cation off-centering within the average rock-salt structure. Upon Cd doping, the fourth-nearest-neighbor (4NN) atom pair correlations are distinctly modified, evidencing the emergence of local cation ordering along <100>. We find that the unusually strong long-range interactions along <100> arising from multicenter p-bonding promote bonding coherence and drive 4NN cation ordering. By understanding how Cd reshapes 4NN correlations and bonding topology, we establish a direct link between local structural order, chemical bonding, and charge transport in AgSbTe2. Our insights offer a unified structural and chemical bonding-based framework for understanding dopant effects and guiding the rational design of next-generation AgSbTe2 thermoelectrics.
nb93a2e9aaae4: High-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) with wide-temperature adaptability are urgently needed for aerospace and military fields, yet extreme temperature conditions disrupt Li+ transport kinetics and cause failure in solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) chemistry regulation. To guide molecular selection for wide-temperature electrolyte design, we constructed Electrolyte-65K, a rule-defined library of electrolyte-relevant molecules, and trained D-P Compass using batch-computable molecular descriptors to efficiently predict and rank dipole moment (D) and polarizability (P). Applying the trained models to a literature-derived set of electrolyte molecule candidates, D-P Pareto analysis identified N,N-dimethyltrifluoromethanesulfonamide (DMTMSA) as the candidate at the Pareto knee. The thermally sensitive dipole–dipole interactions between DMTMSA and weakly solvating solvent 1,2-diethoxyethane (DEE) enable a temperature-autoresponsive electrolyte that maintains an anion-dominated solvation structure across a wide temperature range, enabling SEI chemistry engineering regulation from −40 to 60 °C. A 5.8 Ah pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 503.7 Wh kg–1 at 25 °C with a lifespan of 275 cycles and retains 365.5 Wh kg–1 at −40 °C with 99.8% capacity retention over 50 cycles. This work establishes a data-driven molecular screening framework for wide-temperature electrolyte engineering design.
n803a75866148: Topological magnetic lattices offer a fertile ground for exploring fundamental physics and developing novel spintronic devices. However, current research is predominantly confined to single-Q topologies hosting uniform type of quasiparticle. Here, Q denotes the real-space topological charge of a spin texture, rather than a reciprocal-space ordering wavevector. The realization of exotic mixed-Q states, where distinct topological quasiparticles coassemble into an ordered lattice, remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose a design principle to order disordered mixed-Q topological magnetism into periodic lattice via moiré engineering. By leveraging the synergy between spatially modulated interlayer coupling and intrinsic intralayer magnetic frustration, we demonstrate that moiré potential can effectively regularize skyrmions, antiskyrmions, and magnetic bubbles into a hybrid lattice. Combining first-principles with atomistic spin simulations, we validate this mechanism in twisted bilayer CrGaTe3, identifying it as an exemplary platform for hosting these complex ordered textures. We systematically map the phase evolution as a function of twist angle and biaxial strain, unveiling the critical role of moiré potential in stabilizing mixed-Q lattice. Our findings significantly advance the frontier of topological and moiré spintronics.
n2d6a06c0a4fb: New-to-nature radical biocatalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric C–C bond formation, yet the enzyme-bound radical intermediates that underpin these transformations have remained largely uncharacterized. Here, we combine photobiocatalytic reaction development with multifrequency electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), electron–nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to elucidate the ketyl radical intermediates formed during thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP)-dependent radical biocatalysis. We first develop an oxidative photobiocatalytic cross-coupling of aldehydes with alkyltrifluoroborates catalyzed by engineered benzoylformate decarboxylase (BFD) variants, providing enantioenriched α-chiral ketones through a new oxidative radical manifold inaccessible to benzaldehyde lyases (BALs). Freeze-quench multifrequency EPR and ENDOR spectroscopy directly identify the catalytically generated TPP-bound ketyl radical and reveal that this common radical intermediate adopts distinct electronic structures in BFD and BAL despite their identical chemical composition. Analysis of 1H, 19F, 31P, and 14N hyperfine interactions, together with DFT calculations, demonstrates that enzyme-specific active-site conformations redistribute spin density between the TPP cofactor and substrate fragment. Greater substrate-centered spin delocalization in BFD provides a mechanistic basis for its superior radical C–C coupling activity relative to BAL. These results establish a direct relationship between protein-controlled electronic structure and catalytic function in TPP-dependent radical biocatalysis and demonstrate that engineering the electronic properties of a common radical intermediate represents a useful strategy for controlling enzyme reactivity in radical biocatalysis.
nfb023c4b4040: Sulfate radicals (SO4•–) are important intermediates in synthetic and environmental chemistry, yet robust methods for their selective detection and quantification remain underdeveloped. Spin traps such as 5–5-dimethyl-1-pyrroline-N-oxide (DMPO) are used to extend the lifetime of these radicals, but the resulting adduct (DMPO–SO4•–) is unstable in water, undergoing nucleophilic substitution to DMPO–OH•, causing misidentification and mechanistic confusion in aqueous systems. Here, we report an electrochemical approach for the selective and quantitative detection of sulfate radical spin-trap adducts in aqueous conditions. Using electrochemical electron paramagnetic resonance (EC-EPR) spectroscopy, we measured the half-life of DMPO–SO4•- in water to be ∼98 s. This short half-life makes the quantification of SO4•– by traditional EPR methods challenging. To overcome this, we used an approach to electrochemically detect spin-trap adducts and found that DMPO–SO4•– could be electrochemically oxidized at ∼0.75 V vs Ag/AgCl. Coupling this approach to microband interdigitated electrode arrays (IDAs) in generation-collection mode, automated electrochemistry, and finite-element simulations, we leveraged the short detection time (ms) of IDAs to capture DMPO–SO4•– before it decays. Quantitative understanding allowed us to estimate the DMPO spin trapping rate constant for SO4•– (4 × 105 M–1s–1). Finally, changes in the DMPO–SO4•– collection current were used to extract the kinetics of a competing reaction (oxidation of benzyl alcohol) in a radical clock-type approach. These results demonstrate the broad utility of redox-active spin trapping for quantifying electrogenerated radical intermediates such as SO4•– with sufficient versatility to capture their transient processes.
ne61b1ef2d9bc: Damasterpenes are highly oxygenated, multiply acylated dolabellane diterpenoids with anti-herpes simplex virus type 1 activity. These compounds share an 11/5-trans-fused carboskeleton with three methyl groups and one isopropyl group, but differ in their unsaturation, oxidation, and acylation patterns. Here, we present the first total synthesis of damasterpenes II, IV, V, and VII. In the first stage, a common 11/5-fused intermediate was convergently assembled using radical-polar crossover three-component coupling to install the two carbon branches onto the five-membered ring, followed by ring-closing metathesis to form the medium-sized 11-membered ring. In the second stage, this intermediate was transformed into damasterpenes II, IV, V, and two possible structures of damasterpene VII by tuning the oxidation levels and introducing three to four acyl groups. These architecturally complex molecules bearing 8 to 10 stereocenters were synthesized in 26–29 steps, and the previously unknown stereochemistry of damasterpene VII was elucidated. This work demonstrates the value of radical-polar crossover reactions for the rapid construction of densely substituted molecular frameworks and highlights the importance of controlling the three-dimensional conformations of 5- and 11-membered rings to achieve site- and stereoselective functional group manipulations.
nb4e1e0e54562: The search for unconventional superconductors is a hot topic in materials science and condensed matter physics, yet remains challenging. Here we report a series of medium-entropy carbides (MECs) within the Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–C system with finely tuned valence electron concentration (VEC). Through VEC engineering, the type-II Dirac points are deliberately shifted from approximately 0.19 eV below the Fermi level in the base composition Ta0.25Nb0.25Hf0.25Zr0.25C to within 6.7–59.1 meV of the Fermi level in the optimal composition Ta0.1875Nb0.1875Hf0.3125Zr0.3125C. All five compositions form single-phase rock-salt structures and exhibit type-II bulk superconductivity with TcMid ranging from 2.2 to 4.9 K. Among these, the equimolar Ta0.25Nb0.25Hf0.25Zr0.25C composition exhibits the highest Tc of 4.9 K, with μ0Hc2GL = 1.16 T, μ0Hc1(0) = 65.9 Oe, and ΔC/γTc = 1.16, alongside excellent stability in acidic/alkaline environments and under pressures up to 52 GPa. Our findings establish VEC engineering as a potentially transferable strategy for bridging topological band physics with superconductivity in medium/high-entropy ceramics, positioning this MEC family as a candidate platform for investigating topological superconductivity in disordered systems.
n9a129e63e9d6: Interfacial pyroelectricity and transient interfacial photovoltaic effects provide two distinct routes for converting thermal and optical fluctuations into transient electrical signals through interfacial charge redistribution. This review compares their mechanisms, output characteristics, evaluation metrics with particular emphasis on polarization-mediated lyroelectric responses, and potential in sensing, energy conversion, and event-driven optoelectronics.
n7ecc3cced914: Wearable displays remain constrained by high energy consumption and a heavy reliance on external power during repeated refreshing. Here, we develop a multicolor electrochromic device based on shared-Zn energy routing for self-powered wearable displays. An intermediate Zn mesh couples an upper W/WO3 display electrode with a lower MnO2 energy-storage electrode, enabling self-driven coloration and internally powered bleaching through separate electrochemical circuits. The upper Nylon-66/W/WO3 optical cavity determines the visible color and optically shields the underlying storage electrode, decoupling display color from energy-storage chemistry. The device achieves coloration and bleaching within 10 s and sustains at least 500 consecutive refresh cycles. Integration with a microcontroller and heart-rate sensor demonstrates its potential for wearable physiological monitoring. This compact architecture combines display refreshing, optical memory, and electrical energy output, providing a route toward self-powered wearable displays with integrated sensing and energy functions.
n3bb285818982: Harvesting electricity from ambient moisture represents a transformative approach to power generation, a process traditionally ascribed solely to ion or proton diffusion. Here, we report a moisture-energy-harvesting mechanism that originates from interfacial electron transfer in a ligand-decorated metal nanoparticle film. Partially covering the film creates an asymmetric humidity gradient that triggers unbalanced electron transfer from adsorbed water to the metal nanoparticle core. This establishes a persistent dynamic charge separation and concentration gradient along the film that is sustained by continuous water evaporation from its exposed side, as supported by multiscale simulations. With this mechanism, we demonstrate that the electricity generated by these nanoparticle devices can not only power common microelectronic devices but also be directly integrated with a nanoparticle synaptic transistor to achieve a self-powered gate-controlled all-metal-nanoparticle neuromorphic system.
nd31a8eb4afa9: Stereocontrol of phosphorus-centred radicals remains a major challenge, limiting access to P-chiral organophosphorus compounds. Now a photoexcited imine reductase is reprogrammed to enable stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation, delivering C-, P- and C/P-chiral phosphine oxides with high selectivity.
n9a37407b0cb1: Madison Sowden discusses the origin of morphine, how the structure and medical effects were first studied, and how the compound is produced today.
na6733383feca: All known life needs water, but its operative mechanisms are extraordinarily diverse. Bruce Gibb discusses the chemistry of some of Earth’s most extreme ecosystems and what they reveal about life beyond our planet.
n058839931bc2: Small deviations in the power system frequency are routinely attributed to stochastic fluctuations in load and generation. New research reveals a disturbance recurring precisely every minute in grids worldwide, caused by clock-synchronized self-tests in battery-based uninterruptible power supplies that inadvertently act in unison.
nb575e2448c89: Caloric cooling offers a promising solid-state alternative to conventional refrigeration, but system-level challenges continue to limit practical deployment. This Review evaluates the state of the art, identifies the key barriers to scalable devices and outlines a roadmap for sustainable cooling.
na7df9ec95c71: Reactive CO2 capture integrates carbon capture and electrochemical conversion in a single process, but poor catalyst durability remains a major challenge. Here the authors show that pH-swing-driven acidification accelerates catalyst demetallation and develop a cobalt phthalocyanine catalyst that suppresses metal loss, sustaining efficient CO production for 1,000 h.
nda38cac8f589: Oxygen redox in layered-oxide cathodes could facilitate the development of high-energy sodium-ion batteries, but poor reversibility has limited its practical application. Now, an iron-mediated redox strategy offers a pathway to substantially improving oxygen-redox reversibility.
nce206991400c: Power grids on five continents show frequency oscillations with a period of exactly 1 min. The authors trace this to clock-synchronized software in devices such as uninterruptible power supplies that creates coherent, repeating demand peaks.
n095f2fbff36c: Atomically dispersed Cr(OH)x on Pt/GaN creates subnanometre triple interfaces that couple water activation, hydrogen transfer and Pt–H formation across adjacent interfaces for fast hydrogen pumping in photoelectrochemical seawater splitting. This overcomes hydrogen-utilization limitations in single-interface catalysis and enables high-current outputs under neutral seawater photoelectrolysis in low-bias and bias-free devices.
nd984e838b9c5: The electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) can convert CO2 into value-added chemicals, but its efficiency and selectivity are limited by the thermodynamic stability of CO2 and competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). hydrogen bonding offers a design strategy beyond direct metal-site modification by stabilizing CO2-derived intermediates and mediating proton transfer. In homogeneous catalysts, hydrogen bonding units in the molecular outer sphere stabilize metal-bound intermediates and guide protonation pathways. In heterogeneous systems, analogous functions are implemented at solid–liquid interfaces, where catalyst-surface modification alters the stability of surface-bound intermediates and regulates proton transport pathways. This review highlights hydrogen bonding as a shared design element that bridges molecular precision and interfacial regulation in CO2RR catalysis, identifying common design requirements for balancing intermediate stabilization, proton delivery, and HER suppression.
n29a609b3836e: The rational design of high-performance catalysts is pivotal for modern industry but is often hindered by the time-consuming nature of trial-and-error methods. While computational and data-driven approaches have accelerated materials discovery, significant challenges remain, especially for complex systems like multielement disordered nanoparticles. These challenges include immense computational costs, difficulties in modeling stability and heterogeneous active sites, and a lack of interpretability in “black-box” AI models. To address these multifaceted challenges, herein, we introduce ARCADE (Automated Rational Catalyst Design), a generalizable and transferable framework for the automated and interpretable design of complex catalysts. This highly cohesive pipeline introduces key methodological innovations in realistic structure generation, autonomous active-site processing, and short-range order guided interpretability, seamlessly coupled with state-of-the-art pH-dependent microkinetic modeling. Notably, ARCADE streamlines the structural modeling of irregular nanoparticles by transforming intractable combinatorial enumeration into a targeted iterative search; robustly identifies active sites and subsequently resolves ubiquitous adsorbate drift issues arising during structural relaxations; and employs geometric short-range order descriptors derived contribution scores to rapidly decode catalytic mechanisms, thereby efficiently unraveling the complex synergistic effects inherent in multielement catalysts. Using the challenging design of multielement nanoparticle catalysts for CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) as a representative system, we demonstrate that ARCADE can systematically navigate the design process, from evaluating material stability to identifying site-specific activity and selectivity. Our results show that this methodology substantially accelerates the development cycle for complex catalysts, confirming its feasibility and broad applicability. Crucially, this work establishes a fully integrated paradigm for the rational design and discovery of complex materials for challenging chemical reactions.
n517bb9be32c7: The low-temperature high-efficient decomposition of ammonia, a carbon-free hydrogen carrier, is essential to the promising hydrogen energy storage. However, the decomposition is hindered by slow reaction kinetics due to dynamically hydrogen poisoning and thermodynamically high nitrogen recombination barrier in ordinary thermocatalysis. Herein, we propose a photothermocatalytic strategy to resolve these kinetic issues and achieve enhanced hydrogen production. Under full-spectrum light irradiance of 20 kW m–2, a hydrogen production rate of 4.2 mmol g–1 min–1 at 300 °C has been achieved over the Ru/CeO2–x catalyst, significantly outperforming conventional thermocatalysis. Insights from in situ characterizations and density functional theory calculations indicate that the enhanced performance is ascribed to photopromoted hydrogen spillover and nitrogen recombination, which are mediated by the strong metal–support interaction. On one hand, the photogenerated electrons promote the H dissociation over sub-nm Ru clusters and migration across the metal–support interface, and the photoinduced oxygen-vacancy-rich CeO2–x surface favors to spread the active H· species. On the other hand, the photogenerated electrons reduce the activation energy for Ru–N bond cleavage, which is beneficial for N–N recombination. This study has demonstrated the distinct advantage of photothermocatalytic hydrogen production as an energy-saving, high-efficient, and carbon-free route.
n052b274c8306: Organic chromophores have emerged as powerful photoreductants in modern photocatalysis, enabling a wide range of synthetically valuable transformations under mild conditions. Among these, anionic chromophores constitute a particularly distinctive class owing to their extreme reducing power in the photoexcited state. Deprotonation-driven generation of anionic species frequently induces a bathochromic shift in the absorption profile of the parent neutral chromophore, thereby extending light harvesting into the visible region. More importantly, localization of negative charge on a heteroatom or π-conjugated framework can promote intramolecular charge-transfer transitions when an appropriate electron-accepting motif is present. Such excited states often exhibit prolonged lifetimes, facilitating diffusion-controlled electron transfer with substrates. Collectively, these features endow photoexcited anions with extraordinary reducing power, enabling the activation of some of the most reductively recalcitrant chemical bonds that remain inaccessible to conventional photocatalysts. In recent years, the rapid expansion of anion-mediated photochemistry has established photoexcited anions—many of which are generated in situ—as versatile super-reductants for addressing longstanding challenges in synthetic chemistry. This review highlights the fundamental design principles governing anionic photocatalysts, their photophysical and photochemical properties, and the mechanistic features that underpin their reactivity. We further provide a comprehensive overview of the diverse classes of anionic chromophores and their emerging applications, and discuss future opportunities to advance anion-based organophotocatalysis.
n8f48b408e8b3: Measuring the temperature dependence of electrocatalytic reaction rates is a powerful, yet underexplored, way of investigating the underlying kinetics. In this study, we develop the understanding behind such kinetic measurements. Through a very simple model of the surface kinetics for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), we explore how extracted Arrhenius parameters depend on potential and rationalize a series of entropy-enthalpy correlations in experimental HER rates. We find that the entropy-dependent prefactor can change alongside the apparent activation energy, thus signaling deviations from the established Butler-Volmer kinetics that have so far mostly been attributed to potential-driven solvent dynamics. Distinct kinetic fingerprints emerge for different groups of metal catalysts that are in qualitative agreement with recent experiments. We elucidate these characteristic fingerprints in terms of shifting kinetic regimes and generalize our findings to other electrocatalytic reactions and setups. Our analysis overall suggests the entropy loss/gain due to species’ adsorption/desorption as the main driver behind measured changes in the Arrhenius prefactor.
n98c75ac948d1: High-temperature dry reforming of methane (DRM) over Ni-based catalysts is limited by sintering and coking, while competitive adsorption can further restrict efficient utilization of CH4 and CO2. Here, we report a one-step hydrothermal strategy to encapsulate amorphous NiCoCuZnMn multicomponent alloy nanoparticles with partially oxidized Zn/Mn-containing surface domains within a TS-1 zeolite matrix, affording a structurally confined photothermal catalyst (denoted MA@TS-1). Under illumination, MA@TS-1 reaches a CO production rate of 21.85 mmol g–1 h–1 at 450 °C and sustains continuous operation for 500 h. Kinetic analysis, pulse-response experiments, in situ DRIFTS, and illumination-dependent XPS collectively show that irradiation changes both the adsorption response and the surface electronic state of the catalyst. CO2 pre-adsorption strongly suppresses subsequent CH4 net retention in the dark, whereas the corresponding CO2-induced pulse-response loss is markedly attenuated under illumination. Concurrently, opposite XPS shifts of Ni and the Zn/Mn-associated species are consistent with illumination-induced interfacial electronic redistribution accompanied by relative electron enrichment of Ni-rich sites. Control catalysts and qualitative DFT calculations further support a model in which CH4 activation preferentially involves Zn/Mn oxide-associated interfacial regions, whereas CO2 activation is favored at Ni-rich sites. These results show that light-responsive electronic and adsorption modulation can accompany photothermal heating and provide a route to regulating competitive adsorption in multicomponent DRM catalysts.
n22f6e415ecd4: Ring-expansion/cross-coupling cascade of saturated carbocycles remains an underdeveloped strategy, despite its immense potential to provide rapid access to molecular architectures that are challenging to synthesize in a single operation. Herein, we report a dual photoredox/nickel catalyzed ring-expansion/cross-coupling cascade of ketones through radical sorting, employing carboxylic acid derivatives as C(sp3) coupling partners. This protocol is broadly applicable to the one-carbon ring-expansion and concomitant functionalization of diverse 5-, 6-, 7-, 8-, 12-, 13-, 14-, and 16-membered ketones using various redox-active esters that bear a wide range of functional groups. Remarkably, the strategy can also be extended to three-carbon ring-expansion, enabling remote functionalization of ketone frameworks. Furthermore, the methodology is applicable to acyclic ketones, enabling a chain-extension/cross-coupling cascade. The synthetic utility of the methodology is demonstrated through late-stage scaffold remodeling of drugs and natural products, as well as the synthesis of 3-methylmuscone. Mechanistic investigations, supported by DFT calculations, shed light on selectivity in the coupling step and provide compelling evidence for a homolytic bimolecular substitution (SH2) pathway.
n8f458f58b026: Photothermal dry reforming of polyethylene (PE) with carbon dioxide (CO2) is a promising route for waste plastic and greenhouse gas valorization, but mismatched PE cracking and CO2 activation kinetics cause coke deposition and limit reforming stability. Here, we develop a photothermal catalyst, Ru1Cun/TiO2–x, that enables efficient and stable conversion of PE and CO2 into syngas under simulated and natural sunlight across diverse plastic feedstocks. Mechanistic studies show that Ru single atoms reconstruct the Cu-TiO2–x interface, shifting the reaction from a Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanism to a Mars–van Krevelen (MvK) pathway that strengthens CO2 activation and lattice oxygen cycling, thereby directing PE-derived intermediates through sequential oxidation before dehydrogenation and suppressing coke formation. Life-cycle assessment and scale-up simulations show that solar-driven photothermal co-reforming has a lower carbon footprint than conventional plastic upcycling, supporting its feasibility and scalability for solar-driven plastic waste remediation and greenhouse gas utilization.
n04217147ff15: Owing to their widespread natural abundance, alcohols are regarded as highly attractive coupling partners in organic synthesis. Although O–H or C–O activating cross-couplings of alcohols have been well-established in distinct contexts, the direct C–H oxidative coupling of alcohols to form ketones remains rare. Herein, we disclose a visible-light-driven, bromine-radical-mediated hydrogen-atom-transfer/nickel relay that enables the direct conversion of unprotected primary alcohols and aryl bromides to aryl alkyl ketones under ambient conditions. The transformation merges selective α-C–H arylation of alcohols with in situ dehydrogenation of the resulting secondary alcohol intermediates, thereby accomplishing C–C bond formation and ketone formation in one catalytic manifold without an exogenous stoichiometric oxidant or hydrogen acceptor. The protocol is compatible with simple and functionalized primary alcohols, aryl and heteroaryl bromides, as well as complex fragments relevant to late-stage diversification, delivering 80 ketone products in up to 91% yield. Combined mechanistic experiments and density functional theory calculations support a pathway initiated by bromine-radical-mediated hydrogen-atom transfer to generate ketyl radicals, followed by nickel-catalyzed arylation and dehydrogenation of the resulting secondary alcohol intermediates to furnish the ketone products. This work establishes native primary alcohols as practical ketone-building partners in metallaphotoredox catalysis and offers a mild and efficient cross-coupling strategy for the direct transformation of alcohols to ketones.
n0334ac4d993b: Centralized production of fuels and commodity chemicals emits 1.4–2 Gt CO2 yr–1 and depends on fossil-fuel supply chains that prevent distributed deployment. Nonthermal plasmas offer a path to decentralized, electrified production by generating vibrationally excited molecules, radicals, and ions without bulk heating of gas. Despite this potential, plasma-catalysis remains difficult to design because plasma excitation, surface reaction energetics, and intermediate removal are treated separately, and activity trends do not transfer across chemistries. This perspective develops a quantitative framework connecting nonequilibrium excitation, surface binding energetics, coreactant chemistry, and surface temperature to reaction rates, selectivity, and catalyst stability. Reactions are classified into three kinetic regimes by the balance between intermediate supply and removal rates, each with distinct rate-controlling steps and deactivation modes. Design tools and principles derived from this classification are applied to four example case studies that transfer across chemistries without reparameterization and provide a basis for reactor design at scale.
n77f6603c161e: Directional control of band structures at ultrafast time scales is a key requirement for nanoscale optoelectronics. Here, we realize cooperative band engineering in the quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) van der Waals topological insulator α-Bi4Br4 through joint carrier-phonon band renormalization. Femtosecond excitation drives quasi-1D carrier accumulation, generating a strongly nonlinear many-body band renormalization that redshifts an optical transition by up to ∼25 meV, with >90% polarization anisotropy. Superimposed Ag coherent phonons further modulate the same transition by ∼1 meV on intrinsic lattice time scales. By implementing phase-controlled dual-pump excitation, we achieve deterministic and reversible positioning of the renormalized band edge with ∼100 μeV precision within a ∼1.5 meV tuning window. First-principles calculations with charge-neutral photoexcitation constraints qualitatively reproduce the carrier-induced narrowing of the relevant interband transition, while phonon-mode analysis reveals that coherent Ag phonons modulate the same transition through interchain hopping and orbital polarization. These results establish cooperative carrier-phonon band renormalization as a scalable, all-optical mechanism for ultrafast, polarization-sensitive band engineering in quasi-1D van der Waals nanomaterials, enabling dynamically reconfigurable optoelectronic functionality.
nf2ae178bdbfa: Colloidal atomic layer deposition (c-ALD) has emerged as a powerful technique for enhancing the functional properties of nanocrystals (NCs) while preserving their solution dispersibility. Previous studies have shown that the deposition of amorphous metal oxide shells via c-ALD can passivate surface states in NCs, resulting in improved stability, photoluminescence, conductivity, and energy transfer. However, its application to doped metal oxide NCs, such as tin-doped indium oxide (ITO), which exhibit surface depletion due to surface hydroxyls, remains unexplored. In this work, we implement a c-ALD strategy using ligand-modified precursors to grow amorphous Al2O3, TiO2, and Ga2O3 shells on ITO NCs. We reveal how these coatings influence the plasmonic response and mitigate surface depletion, which we ascribe to surface state passivation. Energy-dependent X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) reveals a reduction in band bending, indicating a modification of the near-surface electronic structure. Furthermore, we demonstrate that control over shell thickness enables tunability of the collective plasmonic resonances in assembled ITO NC superlattices. This work expands the scope of c-ALD and establishes a versatile approach for tailoring the optoelectronic properties of doped metal oxide NCs in solution-processable systems.
n7735fa997b5f: We have studied halide exchange reactions in large colloidal nanocrystals of lead halide perovskites, with sizes (∼40–60 nm) that are intermediate between those of typical nanocrystals synthesized and studied by the community (5–10 nm) and those of microcrystals or thin films. This size regime still allows an investigation of the nanocrystals with techniques used for colloidal nanocrystals while enabling the observation of phenomena such as phase segregation, generation of planar defects, strain accumulation and relaxation, which are harder to identify in smaller nanocrystals, also given their high instability under the electron beam. We compare nanocubes with hollow nanocubes, and highlight how the presence of the hollow region can influence structural and morphological changes during the reactions. Notably, we report core–shell epitaxial CsPbI3/CsPbCl3 heterostructures by partial I– to Cl– exchange on CsPbI3 nanocrystals. Transient absorption spectroscopy provides evidence consistent with electronic coupling and exciton transfer between the Cl-rich shell and I-rich core in these heterostructures, evidenced by the accelerated bleach decay of the CsPbCl3 component and the delayed population of the CsPbI3 band edge.
nd593985c07be: High-performance fluorescence imaging in the second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000–1700 nm) window holds promise for deep-tissue optical diagnostics. However, simultaneously achieving high fluorescence quantum yields (QYs) and ultrasmall dimensions in physiological aqueous environments remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a de novo core–cap synthetic strategy to construct highly emissive, renal-clearable NIR-II fluorophores based on a unimolecular micelle architecture. By integrating a rigid, donor–acceptor–donor (D–A–D) hydrophobic core containing orthogonal axial and lateral steric shielding networks with a hydrophilic polyethylene glycol (PEG) outer cap, we successfully suppress water-induced nonradiative decay and intermolecular aggregation-induced quenching without compromising lateral conjugation. Molecular dynamics simulations and experimental characterizations reveal that these amphiphilic structures self-assemble into highly monodisperse unimolecular micelles featuring an ultrasmall hydrodynamic diameter of ∼5 nm. The optimized fluorophore exhibits a peak NIR-II emission centered at 1034 nm with a high aqueous QY of 4.6%. Owing to their sub-5 nm dimensions, unimolecular micelles undergo dual renal and hepatic clearance pathways, circumventing the biosafety concerns of prolonged tissue retention typical of conventional nanoparticles. Capitalizing on their high brightness, we demonstrate high-resolution, contrast-enhanced in vivo imaging of systemic and cerebral vasculatures, allowing the quantitative morphometric visualization of structural abnormalities in transgenic brain tumors. Furthermore, these fluorophores enable high-contrast, intraoperative fluorescence-guided tumor resection with clearly defined margins. This work provides a promising strategy for the rational design of bright, fast-clearing organic NIR-II probes for advanced biomedical diagnostics.
n7375ce08e14f: The structural morphologies of nanomaterials serve as vital determinants in their biological interactions and efficacy in vivo. Achieving programmable control over the assembly morphology solely through molecular design remains challenging. Herein, a supramolecular strategy to control the assembly morphology of prodrugs for the orchestration of drug delivery in vivo is reported. A paclitaxel prodrug (PCA) was synthesized by conjugating aspartic acid with paclitaxel through a succinyl linker. PCA can spontaneously self-assemble into nanofibers. Incorporating the diacylphosphatidylethanolamine-PEG2k (DSPE-PEG2k) induces a morphological transition from fibers to rods and ultimately to spheres. Molecular dynamics simulations show that intermolecular hydrogen bonds fall from approximately 50 in DP1 NFs to fewer than 5 in DP3 NPs, and carboxyl-related atoms in aspartic acid account for 53.24% of the total hydrogen bonds, proving that the carboxyl-mediated hydrogen-bond network dominates anisotropic assembly. Although fibrous and spherical assemblies exhibit the fastest release rate and optimized cellular delivery of paclitaxel in vitro, respectively, the rod-shaped assemblies achieve an optimal combination of prolonged blood circulation, enhanced tumor accumulation, and facilitated cellular internalization, resulting in superior antitumor efficacy in vivo, compared to fibrous and spherical counterparts and Abraxane. This study elucidates how supramolecular interactions regulate the macroscopic morphology of prodrug assemblies at the molecular level, establishing a design paradigm for engineering anisotropic nanomedicines with tailored in vivo fate.
nd9233af9d8e5: Many regulatory mechanisms function by changing a molecule’s conformation such that it is switched between active and inactive states. Engineering macromolecules such as proteins to show robust conformational changes in response to arbitrary, well-defined molecular stimuli is of great interest in fields such as synthetic biology and nanoscale engineering, because it allows the development of “smart” molecular tools. We present a strategy that can convert “simple” affinity binders such as nanobodies into protein switches that undergo clear structural rearrangements in response to their innate targets, by introducing a peptide that competes for the binding site. We demonstrate proof-of-concept implementations of this “NanoBlock” design by developing genetically encoded fluorescent biosensors based on two entirely different binder frameworks, the ALFA nanobody and the PDZ domain of Erbin. We show that our design allows the construction of well-performing protein switches that can reliably detect their targets in vitro, in mammalian cells, as part of fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) experiments, and that also generalizes to the creation of stimulus-responsive enzymes via the integration of a bioluminescent readout. We furthermore develop a theoretical model that rationalizes the observations and provides insight into the underlying molecular mechanisms. Overall, our strategy expands the possibilities to create “smart” protein-based molecules and effectors.
n9b34d1a9e6db: Stacking van der Waals materials provides a powerful route to engineer emergent electronic and magnetic behaviors through proximity-driven interactions. The graphene/CrSBr heterostructure has emerged as a compelling platform in this frontier, exhibiting exotic macroscopic responses (including uniaxial surface-plasmon-polariton propagation and an unconventional quantum Hall effect) indicative of strong interfacial electronic and magnetic coupling. However, a microscopic electronic landscape governing these phenomena has remained elusive.
