Here, we provide a comprehensive spectroscopic characterization of the graphene/CrSBr interface using a combination of angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), low-energy electron microscopy (LEEM), and density functional theory. We resolve a massive redistribution of interfacial charge that concurrently hole-dopes graphene and populates the quasi-one-dimensional spin-polarized conduction band of CrSBr, leading to interfacial metallization. Furthermore, electronic structure of CrSBr exhibits strong momentum-dependent renormalization distinct from conventional charge doping, and theoretical modeling supported by Raman spectroscopy points to additional interfacial compressive strain. In addition, ARPES reveals a splitting-like feature in the graphene Dirac cone consistent with spin degeneracy lifting, providing possible evidence of magnetic proximity coupling. These findings provide crucial microscopic insight into the system’s optical and transport responses and establish graphene/CrSBr as a versatile platform for charge-transfer control, strain-driven band engineering, magnetic-proximity coupling, and directionally confined excitations for next-generation spintronic and nanophotonic devices.
n1cfbde3306ca: The metallic 1T phase of MoS2 provides basal-plane activity and high conductivity that are absent in the semiconducting 2H polymorph, making it attractive for applications in electrocatalysis and energy conversion. However, its intrinsic metastability readily drives relaxation to the 2H ground state, and previous attempts to stabilize 1T-MoS2 have yielded only transient domains or localized perturbations without durable phase retention. Here we show that confining Pt single-atoms (SAs) at the MoS2–graphene heterointerface promotes enhanced stabilization and improved retention of 1T-associated MoS2 signatures, while simultaneously stabilizing the SAs themselves. The interfacial Pt SAs act as atomic-scale anchors, simultaneously redistributing charge and reshaping local coordination to favor the metallic 1T-associated configuration of MoS2. Spectroscopic analyses confirm persistent 1T signatures, and ex situ characterization after operation verifies reliable retention of 1T-MoS2. Density functional theory calculations further corroborate these findings, demonstrating that Pt incorporation reverses the intrinsic phase preference and energetically favors the 1T configuration. Electrochemical measurements further demonstrate nearly unchanged hydrogen evolution activity after 30,000 cycles. Together, these results establish SA-mediated heterointerface engineering as a powerful route to stabilize metastable electronic phases and unlock the full potential of layered materials for energy and electronic technologies.
n2cff323062ce: Biomolecular corona on nanoparticle surfaces enriches low-abundance proteins and compresses the dynamic range of the plasma proteome. Single-walled carbon nanotubes are particularly attractive because their surface chemistry is highly tunable, and their near-infrared fluorescence directly reports corona modulation. However, how surface chemistry shapes the corona and how the corona relates to the fluorescence response remain unclear. We profiled protein enrichment patterns and the resulting fluorescence in a library of 25 chemically modified carbon nanotubes by quantitative proteomics and near-infrared fluorescence spectroscopy. We found that polymer and quantum-defect chemistry orthogonally modulate corona composition, and protein flexibility and solvent exposure are the most significant factors of enrichment, consistent with dispersion-driven, contact-maximizing interactions. Proteomics and fluorescence correlation analyses indicate that enrichment and fluorescence response are partially decoupled. A subset of corona proteins stays optically silent, but where responses occur, enriched proteins respond at lower, physiologically relevant ranges than depleted ones. Our findings inform design principles for carbon nanomaterial-based sensors and biomarker discovery platforms.
nc97c7da524a5: Amorphous solid electrolytes provide a promising route to overcoming the ion-transport limitations of crystalline halide frameworks, yet achieving superionic Na+ conduction remains challenging. Herein, we report a mixed-anion amorphous Na-ion solid-state electrolyte, TaCl5-0.5Na2S (NTSC), synthesized via high-energy ball-milling, which exhibits an ultrahigh room-temperature ionic conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm and a low activation energy of 0.276 eV. Structural analyses reveal a highly disordered framework composed of Ta-centered bipolyhedra interconnected via corner-sharing sulfur atoms [Ta2Cl10S], [TaCl5S], [TaCl4S], and [TaCl4S2], evidenced by comprehensive characterizations, forming a flexible, disordered amorphous network. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations identify continuous Na+-diffusion pathways with low migration barriers. Complementary topological analyses further indicate that sulfur incorporation leads to local lattice distortions, shortens Na–Na hopping distances, and enhances framework flexibility, collectively enabling fast, multidimensional Na+ transport. When applied in all-solid-state sodium-ion batteries (ASSNIBs), NTSC enables high reversible capacity (111.95 mAh/g with a Coulombic efficiency of 92.6% at 0.1 C) and excellent cycling stability (76.9% initial capacity retention after 200 cycles at 0.2 C) at room temperature. This work establishes mixed-anion amorphization as an effective design strategy for high-performance Na-ion solid electrolytes.
n4a9f94d7e394: Interlayer excitons (IEs) in van der Waals heterostructures offer tunable excitonic states with long lifetimes and permanent dipole moments. Prior studies focused on isotropic 2H-phase transition metal dichalcogenides, where bright IE emission is confined near high-symmetry twist angles (0° and 60°), restricting tunability. Here, heterobilayers of monolayer ReS2 and ReSe2, both in the 1T′ phase, exhibit robust polarized IE emission near 1.2 eV across the full twist-angle range (1°–88°), reflecting a hybridization landscape governed by lattice anisotropy rather than valley alignment. The lowest-energy IE transition exhibits a nonmonotonic twist-angle dependence with a total modulation range of ∼60 meV, consistent with moiré-driven band renormalization and modulation of interlayer coupling revealed by first-principles calculations and low-frequency Raman spectroscopy, respectively. Overall IE energy tunability extends to ∼100 meV with multilayer ReS2 and excitation energy variation. These results establish ReS2/ReSe2 as a versatile infrared IE platform enabling polarization-resolved emitters and detectors beyond 2H-symmetry constraints.
n5419ad48a024: Manganese dioxides are pervasive as cathode materials for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries; however, their energy storage mechanism has proven to be complex. Increasing evidence suggests that Mn dissolution contributes to cathode capacity via a reversible dissolution‐redeposition process, in addition to capacity from Zn2+/H+ (de)intercalation. Understanding the role played by Mn2+ in the electrolyte, particularly when introduced as an electrolyte additive, is important for diagnosing cathode degradation. Using operando X‐ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy, we track Mn2+ in operating cells to gain insights into the complexity of the MnO2 cathode. While some suppression of cathode dissolution by the additive cannot be excluded, our measurements suggest that Mn2+ electrolyte additives improve cycling performance by supplying extra redox‐active Mn during charge, rather than solely by suppressing Mn dissolution, thereby compensating for cathode degradation. Benefiting from operando XRF, we propose that a potential contributor to capacity fading is the incomplete dissolution of the MnO2 cathode and incomplete redeposition of Mn2+ from the electrolyte, and that this fading does not appear to be mitigated by using Mn2+ additives. These findings underscore the necessity of directly tracking Mn2+ evolution, and that improving reversibility requires addressing both the dissolution of MnO2 and the redeposition of Mn2+.
n4123a9d6daf0: Epitaxial dielectric thin films have attracted considerable attention for better energy storage performance than bulks and polymers, yet their reported recoverable energy density (W rec) commonly excludes the substrate, which limits its relevance to practical device-level energy storage. Here, we develop a Si-integrated BZT//S-BZT multilayer capacitor to address this issue and simultaneously enhance polarization and breakdown strength (E b). By directly integrating the oxide multilayer on Si-based substrates, the contribution of the substrate to the effective device volume is substantially reduced, enabling a realistic energy density (W rec-real) of 105.51 J/cm3, exceeding that of the overwhelming majority of comparable systems. The BZT and S-BZT sublayers exhibit small lattice mismatch but pronounced dielectric contrast, which induces strong interfacial polarization (P inter) without introducing interfacial structural perturbation. Landau–Ginzburg–Devonshire theory and phase-field simulations consistently verify the interface-induced polarization enhancement and agree well with the experimental observations. To further improve Eb , machine learning was employed to establish the relationship between the multilayer structural parameters and E b and to identify the optimal starting-layer thickness. Experimental results closely reproduce the predicted trend, leading to an optimized Big-Mac-n architecture with a high W rec of 131.21 J/cm3 and an Eb of 6.5 MV/cm. The multilayer also exhibits excellent fatigue, frequency, and temperature stability, together with ultrafast discharge capability. This work establishes a data-driven interface-engineering strategy for reliable, Si-integrated dielectric energy-storage capacitors.
n57b9b7389368: The fast‐charging capability of phase‐separating graphite electrodes is largely constrained by heterogeneous reaction kinetics and sluggish mass transport at both the particle and electrode scales, which increase the risk of parasitic lithium plating and associated safety concerns. A deeper mechanistic understanding of the interplay among phase‐separation dynamics, electrode microstructure, and lithium‐plating propensity is therefore essential for guiding the rational design of advanced electrode architectures and fast‐charging protocols. Here, we combine operando optical microscopy with three‐dimensional microstructure‐resolved phase‐field modeling to resolve the interplay between phase separation and lithium plating. Microscopy captures stages evolution, phase mode transitions and structural dynamics across the particle population and at the single‐particle level, which is driven by the slow interfacial reactions. Non‐equilibrium phase‐field simulations elucidate the kinetic control mechanisms governing phase transitions as the current varies. Importantly, a new mechanism of lithium plating associated with interfacial ohmic resistance is identified. Based on these insights, we evaluate particle‐size‐distribution design and use thermal activation as a mechanistic probe to resolve how temperature alters phase‐separation pathways and lithium‐plating behavior. These results may serve as a foundation for improving the physical understanding and driving optimization of fast charging protocols for lithium‐ion batteries.
nbc2bd4e1dcb1: The rapid development of wearable electronics places higher demands on materials with mechanical flexibility, sustainable energy supply, and thermal management. However, incorporating conductive fillers such as liquid metal (LM) into soft porous materials may introduce additional heat‐transfer pathways and complicate thermal management. Here, a molecular and structural engineering strategy is reported to integrate triboelectric energy harvesting with thermal insulation in a superelastic aerogel. Industrial xylan is converted into carboxymethyl xylan (CMX) through ball‐milling pretreatment and etherification, enabling stable dispersion of LM micro/nanodroplets. Subsequently, by synergistically integrating directional freezing and foaming, an aerogel with a unique interconnected perforated‐bubble structure is constructed. During 1000 compression cycles at a maximum strain of 60%, the aerogel exhibits progressively stabilized cyclic behavior, with residual strains of 8.7% and 11.5% in the transverse and longitudinal directions, respectively. The aerogel‐based triboelectric nanogenerator delivers an output voltage of 112 V, while the aerogel architecture maintains low transverse and longitudinal effective thermal conductivities of 35.8 and 39.5 mW m−1 K−1, respectively. This work provides a structural design strategy for integrating triboelectric energy harvesting, mechanical resilience, and thermal insulation within a multifunctional soft aerogel.
n1fc4a7a1ed2f: Ferroelectric domain walls (DWs) have attracted extensive interest because of their emergent physical properties and potential functionalities in nanoelectronic devices. Although DWs are traditionally proposed to be atomically sharp interfaces, experimental observations frequently report apparent broadening, roughness, and even complex three‐dimension, suggesting structural variations beyond the conventional 2D picture. However, direct experimental characterization of such 3D structures remains challenging because of the intrinsic limitations of projection‐based imaging. Here, we employ energy‐filtered multislice electron ptychography with ∼2 nm depth resolution to directly resolve the 3D morphology of ferroelectric DWs in BiFeO3 nano‐islands grown on SrTiO3 substrates. We reveal that domain walls can exhibit irregular 3D morphologies while remaining intrinsically atomically sharp, with widths confined to approximately one unit cell. The apparent broadening observed in conventional imaging is shown to originate predominantly from depth‐dependent structural variations rather than from a genuine increase in wall width. Furthermore, depth‐resolved strain analysis demonstrates that interfacial strain gradients and dislocations play an important role in stabilizing and modulating 3D domain‐wall configurations. Our findings uncover the 3D nature of ferroelectric domain walls and provide a structural foundation for understanding domain‐wall functionalities.
nef261da50072: Thermocells (TECs) offer a promising route for directly converting low‐grade heat into electricity, while n‐type TECs historically lag behind their p‐type counterparts due to their sluggish reaction kinetics and thermodynamic limitations. Herein, a ternary electrolyte with synergistic coordination effect is proposed to uniquely address these challenges within the ferrous/ferric n‐type TECs. In this electrolyte, 15‐crown‐5 selectively encapsulates Fe3+ while p‐toluenesulfonic acid provides additional coordination sites, effectively suppressing detrimental hydrolysis and enhancing the electrochemical reversibility that is often compromised by the crown ether used alone. Such selective and synergistic coordination directly enlarges entropy change and facilitates charge transfer, significantly contributing to the overall thermoelectrochemical performance. The resulting TECs based on the optimized ternary electrolyte exhibit a notably enhanced thermopower of −2.41 mV K−1 and a markedly increased normalized power density of 1.348 mW m−2 K−2, representing one of the highest values reported for n‐type TECs. The substantial enhancement in both thermopower and power density facilitates an excellent match with the classic p‐type ferricyanide/ferrocyanide TECs, and a device integrated with 14 p‐n TEC pairs is further demonstrated, showing high potential toward practical low‐grade heat harvesting applications.
na793202df5a2: Piezo-photocatalysis has emerged as a promising strategy to suppress charge recombination in conventional photocatalysis for the removal of refractory organic pollutants and green hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. Nevertheless, sulfide-based piezo-photocatalysts still suffer from weak piezoelectric response and ambiguous coupling mechanisms between atomic orbitals and polarization. Herein, we designed Pd-doped and lattice oxygen-modified Zn3In2S6 piezo-photocatalyst (Zn3In2S6-Pd-350) by regulating d-p orbital hybridization at Pd sites to achieve efficient piezo-photocatalytic performance. Lattice oxygen occupies sulfur vacancies and converts Pd–S into Pd–O coordination, enabling strong Pd 4d–O 2p orbital hybridization. The σ* and π* antibonding orbitals act as electron acceptors to accelerate charge separation. The charge asymmetry induced by Pd and lattice oxygen enhanced piezoelectric properties of catalyst, resulting in a 156% increase of the piezoelectric coefficient. Zn3In2S6-Pd-350 achieved 100% degradation of 2,4-DCP and H2O2 yield of 327.9 µmol·g−1·h−1, accompanied by •OH, •O2 − and 1O2 synergistic oxidation. Calculations confirm that single-atom Pd replacing Zn is the active center with optimal Pd–S1O3 coordination, and external strain further enhances O2/H2O adsorption. This work establishes an atomic-level design strategy via orbital engineering, reveals the essential synergy among orbital hybridization, charge distribution and piezoelectric polarization, and provides a feasible route for chlorophenol wastewater remediation and low-carbon H2O2 synthesis.
nbf305e8f8a94: Hard carbon, a leading anode for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), suffers from nonuniform sodium deposition, which causes dendrite growth and compromises safety and cycle life. Here, we report a closed‐pore engineering strategy based on cobalt‐doped hard carbon (CoHC) that couples internal sodium‐cluster confinement with interfacial stabilization. Internally, the closed nanopores redirect sodium storage from surface accumulation to deep pore filling, thereby inhibiting the growth of quasi‐metallic sodium clusters and dendrite propagation. Externally, the closed‐pore architecture regulates interfacial chemistry, leading to a thin, uniform, inorganic‐rich solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) with reduced charge‐transfer resistance. In situ electrochemical tests confirm stable interfaces and suppressed dendrite growth in both Na||CoHC half cells and CoHC||Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP) full cells, whereas severe dendritic deposition occurs on pristine hard carbon (HC) under identical current density. The CoHC anode delivers superior cycling stability with a capacity retention of 95% after 500 cycles, significantly outperforming HC. This work paves the way for dendrite‐resistant, safer, and longer‐lasting sodium‐ion batteries.
n5c212e53564f: Controlling Zinc (Zn) nucleation and subsequent crystal growth is critical for long‐lifespan aqueous Zn‐metal batteries. However, the concurrent parasitic reactions and dendritic growth impede the continuous Zn‐metal electrodeposition. Here, we demonstrate that coordination unsaturation is exploited to reconstruct the electronic structure of a metal host, thereby regulating the crystallographic pathway of Zn deposition. A partially selenized Cu‐OSe framework with locally unsaturated mixed O/Se coordination stabilizes a mixed‐valence Cu configuration and redistributes Cu‐derived electronic states, establishing continuous local‐current pathways. These pathways homogenize interfacial electron transport and redirect Zn growth toward a stable Zn(002)/(100) dual texture. This coordination regime preserves structural integrity while avoiding framework collapse and morphological deformation associated with complete selenization. Macroscale characterization confirms the spatial continuity of local‐current pathways across the Cu‐OSe substrate, attesting to its scalability toward pouch‐cell applications. Accordingly, the Cu‐OSe@Zn anode sustains stable Zn plating/stripping for over 3100 h at 1 mA cm−2 while Cu‐OSe@Zn||VO2 full cells deliver 2200 cycles at 1 A g−1 with 71% capacity retention. These findings establish a direct mechanistic link, whereby coordination unsaturation drives Cu‐centered electronic reconstruction to generate local‐current pathways that direct Zn dual‐texture growth, identifying local coordination engineering as a general electronic‐structure design principle for regulating metal‐electrodeposition interfaces.
nf09cbf791417: Large‐area GaN heteroepitaxy is essential for next‐generation electronic and optoelectronic systems, yet simultaneously achieving low wafer bow and high epitaxial uniformity remains challenging due to the dynamic evolution of thermo‐mechanical stress during growth and cooling. Here, we develop a dynamic wafer curvature engineering strategy based on a thermal‐cycling stress‐loading (TCSL) layer to regulate curvature evolution throughout epitaxy and suppress residual bow after cooling. The TCSL layer consists of a hydrogen‐rich SiO2 film deposited on the backside of sapphire substrates, where hydrogen‐driven viscoelastic relaxation and dehydrogenation‐induced network densification generate asymmetric stress evolution. Applying this strategy to AlGaN/GaN HEMT epitaxy, we realize ultraflat and highly uniform 8‐inch wafers on 1‐mm‐thick sapphire substrates, achieving a bow of 7.4 µm, a warp of 17.2 µm, and relative standard deviations of 0.82%, 1.2%, and 1.8% for epitaxial thickness, Al composition, and sheet resistance, respectively. The AlGaN/GaN heterostructure preserves high crystalline and interfacial quality, enabling a high‐quality two‐dimensional electron gas with a sheet density of 7.0 × 1012 cm−2 and an electron mobility of 2040 cm2/V·s. This work establishes a scalable approach for simultaneous control of wafer flatness and epitaxial uniformity in large‐area GaN heteroepitaxy, paving the way toward highly integrated GaN‐based electronic and optoelectronic technologies.
n2c8fb99dc00e: Unintentionally formed interfacial layers are ubiquitous in semiconductor devices that operate at extreme conditions, but their structure and properties remain unknown due to the layer thinness. Here, we present epitaxial growth and semiconductor properties of NiGa2O4 spinel and its interfaces with Ga2O3 in high‐power and high‐temperature electronic devices. Cubic spinel NiGa2O4 films of 2–200 nm thicknesses and low surface roughness (∼2 nm) were grown on (0001) α‐Al2O3 using pulsed laser deposition at substrate temperatures in the 300–900°C range. The NiGa2O4 optical absorption onset (3.6–3.9 eV) and thermal conductivity (4–9 W m−1 K−1) vary systematically with substrate temperature, consistent with theoretical predictions of varying Ni and Ga cation ordering on the spinel lattice. The valence band offset at the epitaxial NiGa2O4/Ga2O3 interfaces of (100) orientation is determined to be 1.8 eV using a new method that addresses limitations of traditional Kraut analysis. The NiGa2O4/Ga2O3 heterojunction devices with (001) HVPE drift layers exhibit a rectification ratio of 108 (for ± 2V) and a turn‐on voltage of 1.4 V, maintaining diode behavior up to 600°C. These results highlight the potential of NiGa2O4 as a heterojunction partner in β‐Ga2O3‐based devices and show a new approach to investigate such interfacial layers.
n142f0c017a95: Secure edge hardware demands compact device platforms that can integrate low‐power information processing with hardware‐level security. However, this convergence of computation and security remains challenging because accurate analog operation and stochastic security functionality rely on fundamentally different device characteristics. Here we demonstrate that transient fluctuations in a synaptic hybrid ferro‐ionic tunnel diode (HTD) can be harnessed as an in materia physical resource for unified hardware security, enabling both true random number generators (TRNGs) and physical unclonable functions (PUFs) within the same device platform. To achieve this functional separation, low‐frequency noise is introduced as a new degree of freedom for hardware security, serving either as a direct stochastic source or as a guide to the optimal operation condition. Therefore, the HTD supports both static identity and dynamic randomness in distinct operating regimes, while separating information processing in the conductance domain from security generation in the fluctuation domain. In the TRNG mode, the tunneling regime activates shot noise‐dominant fluctuations that provide a broadband entropy source with enhanced thermal stability for TRNG operation. In the PUF mode, voltage‐driven stochastic switching produces device‐specific power spectral density fingerprints, overcoming the limited dimensionality of conventional conductance‐based fingerprints.
n716bbdee4e10: Poor device reproducibility and insufficient processing robustness hinder organic photovoltaics (OPVs) industrialization, primarily due to poor morphological reproducibility of the active layer. Here, we establish a direct correlation between the morphology evolution pathway and morphological reproducibility. When evolution is governed by solid‐state relaxation, the active layer converges into energetically similar low‐energy metastable ensembles, yielding highly reproducible morphologies. In contrast, rapid quenching traps the active layer in a broad distribution of low‐energy metastable states, leading to poor morphological reproducibility. This principle is validated through two independent approaches: molecular structure design and additive engineering. Chemically, acceptor dimerization (PM6:DY2) shifts evolution from quenching‐ to relaxation‐dominated, reducing the coefficient of variation (CV, a reproducibility measure) from 2.14% to 1.19% and increasing the performance figure of merit (P‐FOM, a robustness measure) from 0.925 to 0.944. Physically, replacing the additive 1,2,4‐TCB with 1,3,5‐TIB delays the evolution of PM6:L8‐BO to the relaxation stage, achieving 19.59% PCE while achieving a record‐low CV of 0.86% (reduced from 1.55%) and increasing P‐FOM from 0.935 to 0.955. These findings establish a general principle: solid‐state relaxation‐dominated evolution leads to morphological convergence and device performance consistency, providing a theoretical basis for rational design toward high reproducibility and robustness in OPVs.
n2d9cbfef3e35: Carbazole‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) stand out as competitive hole‐transport materials for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), benefiting from their low‐temperature processing and robust operational stability. Nevertheless, intrinsic SAM aggregation and surface hydrophobicity hinder perovskite precursor wetting, trigger uneven buried‐interface nucleation, and worsen interfacial contact, limiting device performance improvement. Herein, two fluorinated phosphonic‐acid molecules, namely FPA‐Ph and FPA‐Py, are utilized to reconstruct the buried SAM/perovskite interface. Both modifiers improve the wettability of the SAM surface and modulate the local interfacial environment via interactions with the SAM and perovskite components. Relative to FPA‐Ph, the extra pyridinic‐N sites in FPA‐Py further boost surface wettability and strengthen Pb2+ coordination, concurrently generating a smoother and more homogeneous SAM layer. These synergistic effects promote the formation of compact perovskite films, favorable interfacial energetics, and optimized carrier dynamics. Consequently, FPA‐Py‐modified PSCs deliver a champion efficiency of 26.53% while possessing exceptional operational stability against high humidity, elevated temperature, and continuous illumination. This work demonstrates hydrophilization‐assisted molecular post‐treatment as an effective approach to buried‐interface reconstruction and provides rational molecular‐design guidance for the scalable fabrication of inverted PSCs.
ne172531797e5: Photoelectrocatalytic (PEC) water splitting enables sustainable solar‐to‐hydrogen conversion, yet bismuth tungstate (Bi2WO6) photoanodes suffer from severe charge recombination. Herein, we rationally design a novel multi‐site contact Schottky junction with modulated interfacial electronic structure and multi‐site charge transport channels by integrating 2D Fe‐doped Bi2WO6 (Fe‐BWO) nanosheets with 3D RuCu co‐doped WC (RuCu‐WC) dodecahedra. The polyhedral scaffold forms multiple discrete yet intimate contact points at its vertices and edges, constructing abundant parallel electron extraction channels. The introduction of Fe broaden the light harvesting efficiency endowing with an improved interfacial carrier density. Driven by the large work function difference, a strong interfacial built‐in electric field is established, which unidirectionally drives photogenerated electrons from band‐narrowed Fe‐BWO into the interconnected 3D RuCu‐WC conductive network while spatially confining photogenerated holes on the Fe‐BWO basal plane to drive the water oxidation reaction. The optimized photoanode delivers an exceptional photocurrent density of 7.40 mA cm−2 at 1.23 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) with 66.1% charge transfer efficiency. The assembled PEC water splitting cell achieves a remarkable photocurrent density of 6.39 mA cm−2 at 1.23 V and a solar‐to‐hydrogen (STH) conversion efficiency of 5.59%. This work provides a generalizable strategy for enhancing charge separation in semiconductor‐based energy conversion systems.
n3e92d69fb077: While self‐powered flexible e‐skins based on nanogenerators hold immense promise for wearable electronics, severe interfacial mechanical mismatches occur under complex joint deformations, limiting reliable multichannel sensing. Herein, a 4D‐printed mechanical metamaterial‐enabled e‐skin with an auxetic scaffold and AI‐assisted decoding is developed to improve deformation accommodation and support multichannel sensing during joint motion. Benefiting from an auxetic architecture with a tunable negative Poisson's ratio (−0.41 to −1.76), the metamaterial skeleton expands laterally under stretch to mimic the strain‐stiffening behavior of biological tissues. By concentrating local stress, this geometrical programmability transforms the skeleton into an active mechanical amplifier, significantly boosting the triboelectric‐piezoelectric (TENG/PENG) responses. An integrated nine‐channel array captures these amplified spatiotemporal features with high fidelity. During fast running, the device yields robust 3 V outputs and resolves 3 Hz rhythmic motions. Further, by introducing a lightweight 1D convolutional neural network (1D‐CNN) to decouple intricate spatiotemporal crosstalk, the system achieves advanced motion‐state classification with an exceptional accuracy of over 95% on average across different tasks. This integration of mechanics and artificial intelligence offers a robust platform for next‐generation intelligent wearable rehabilitation and human‐machine interfaces.
n3ff04c57a0db: Highly conductive carbon fibers are promising for ultra‐thin microwave absorption (MA), but the significant impedance mismatch limits microwave incidence and subsequent energy dissipation. Conventional interface engineering largely optimizes component composition and loading, whereas the role of radial interface order remains unclear. In this work, the interface sequence is treated as a new structural variable. ZIF‐67 and MIL‐88B nanolayers with tunable electromagnetic (EM) responses were synthesized in situ on carbon fibers. First, the impedance mismatch characteristics of carbon fibers were improved by adjusting the heat treatment temperature and shell loading. Furthermore, the EM response properties of the materials were finely tuned by reversing the growth order of ZIF‐67 and MIL‐88B on the surface. The optimized CFC‐9‐2 achieved minimum reflection loss (RL) of −70.81 dB and effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 4.85 GHz at a thickness of 1.58 mm. Further simulations of far‐field conditions and near‐field Wi‐Fi radiation tests demonstrate attenuation in representative environments. The results demonstrate that the spatial sequence of interfaces serves as a key structural parameter for regulating the transmission and dissipation of electromagnetic energy.
n0b45bb9a385d: Preventing secondary release after capture remains a critical challenge in the management of radioactive methyl iodide (CH3I) from nuclear off‐gas. Here, a metal‐free porous organic polymer, TBPOF‐PZ, was developed by covalently integrating piperazine‐derived tertiary amines and Tröger's‐base bridgehead nitrogen centers into a thermally stable porous architecture. TBPOF‐PZ achieves a high total CH3I uptake of 4.35 g g−1, while 1.60 g g−1 remains irreversibly retained after thermal desorption. Spectroscopic analysis, density functional theory, and pyrohydrolytic combustion‐ion chromatography collectively clarify the chemical immobilization mechanism. TBPOF‐PZ exhibits excellent CH3I retention performance in multicomponent fixed‐bed breakthrough experiments using a simulated realistic gas mixture. Importantly, no obvious deterioration in performance is observed after exposure to an NOx‐containing atmosphere or 240 kGy γ‐irradiation. In addition, CH3I‐loaded TBPOF‐PZ effectively retains iodide under both high‐temperature conditions and prolonged storage. These results establish a covalent porous‐polymer strategy for integrating efficient capture, durable chemical fixation, and leakage resistance under demanding nuclear off‐gas conditions.
n0e3d2d725c0a: Neuromorphic optoelectronic hardware requires 2D channels whose thickness, and therefore band structure, is reproducible across an entire wafer, yet atomic‐layer control of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) must reconcile precision, uniformity, and scalability simultaneously. Here, 6‐inch wafer‐scale atomic‐layer control of WS2 is reported by integrating low‐temperature plasma‐assisted synthesis with a three‐component mixed‐gas (Ar+O2+CF4) reactive ion etching process. WS2 synthesized from electron‐beam‐evaporated W seed layers preserves structural integrity and achieves uniform atomic‐layer control across the wafer, whereas sputter‐derived WS2 etches non‐uniformly with rougher surfaces and partial lattice disruption, as confirmed by ellipsometry, atomic force microscopy, Raman mapping, and cross‐sectional transmission electron microscopy. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations qualitatively support the experimentally observed optical band gap according to the number of layers and provide insight into the layer‐dependent electronic properties of WS2. The layer‐controlled WS2 was subsequently employed to fabricate opto‐memristive devices, which exhibited pulse‐history‐dependent photocurrent modulation at zero read bias. The 4L‐WS2 device balances optical sensitivity against inter‐pulse memory, resolving 16 four‐pulse optical histories into distinguishable analog states. A dual‐state recursive model calibrated from the measured device dynamics achieved a mean waveform‐classification accuracy of 95.8 ± 1.69%. Atomic‐layer control thus provides a manufacturable route from wafer‐scale TMD processing to band‐structure‐programmed neuromorphic optoelectronics.
n501dbe548b77: Pulse monitoring and tooth occlusion detection are two key scenarios for non-invasive monitoring of cardiovascular and oral health. Traditional pressure sensors suffer from a trade-off between sensitivity and measurement range. Their rigid structure and poor surface fit hinder the accurate acquisition of weak pulse signals and the detection of wide-range occlusal pressure. Here, a high-performance capacitive ionic pressure sensor was realized based on the electric double-layer (EDL) effect, featuring both ultra-high sensitivity (73224 kPa− 1) and a wide detection range (0.01–1100 kPa). Compared with most reported ionic pressure sensors, our sensor achieves competitive ultra-high peak sensitivity at low pressure while maintaining an exceptionally broad detection range. Drawing on pulse-diagnosis principles of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), this sensor accurately captures wrist pulse signals at the “Cun, Guan and Chi” acupoints. Integrating machine-learning techniques, the occlusal-pressure monitoring prototype achieves automatic classification of ten distinct occlusal-pressure patterns acquired from dental phantom models. Such a cutting-edge design for the ionic pressure sensor and its application in monitoring of both cardiovascular and oral health are rarely reported in the literature. These findings lay a foundation for the development of adaptive flexible monitoring systems for personalized medicine and intelligent physiological monitoring technology.
n4df967d500f8: Robotics enables regenerative medicine to be more precise, less invasive, and more targeted. Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy shows great potential for tissue regeneration, but challenges such as low cell survival and limited differentiation ability after in vivo implantation hinder its clinical translation. In this study, we propose a magnetic robotic platform capable of autonomously recognizing and targeting injury sites, as well as delivering noninvasive magnetic stimuli to programmatically regulate MSC functions for tendon repair. This platform integrates 3D‐MRI with real‐time recognition to enable spatial perception of deep tissues, which is visualized through panoramic simulation. It provides an engineering‐precise and intelligent automated magnetic stimulation for the diverse tendon injuries scenarios. We identified pulse electromagnetic field (PEMF) parameters that induced proliferation and tenogenesis of MSCs, respectively, and demonstrated the feasibility of programmed PEMF to sequentially regulate cell behaviors of transplanted MSCs, which contributed to the structure and functional recovery of rat injured tendons. Furthermore, we elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms by which different magnetic stimuli regulate MSC functions, providing insight into PEMF‐mediated MSCs responses. Generally, this magnetic robotic system offers a noninvasive, precise, and biosafe strategy to enhance MSC‐based therapies, with significant implications for clinical applications and broader regenerative medicine.
n3d7a1e362e20: Tumor mitochondria regulate cancer progression and immune evasion. However, current therapeutic strategies lack the subcellular precision required to selectively induce immune‐beneficial mitochondrial dysfunction without causing systemic toxicity. Here, we report a biointerface‐customized nanomodulator (C/C‐HP@M2M‐TPP), developed through a biointerface‐engineered strategy (BES), that integrates sequential targeting and controlled activation to induce mitochondria‐specific dysfunction and reprogram tumor immunity. Through a customized biointerface coating, the nanomodulators achieve preferential tumor accumulation and mitochondria‐directed subcellular localization. Co‐delivered calcium ion donors and efflux inhibitors cooperatively induce mitochondrial ion interference and dysfunction, which is further amplified by photothermal activation. This localized mitochondrial interference promotes immunogenic cell death and robust antitumor immune activation, resulting in potent tumor regression in mice. Integrated single‐cell transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identify mitochondrial disruption as a key mechanistic driver of tumor immune reprogramming. This work establishes biointerface‐customized nanomodulation as a subcellular immunomodulatory therapeutic strategy in vivo.
n92543640f1af: The autonomic nerves drive prostate cancer (PCa) progression, yet a strategy for dual modulation of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves remains undeveloped. Here, building on the multicenter clinical findings, we develop a personalized nanotechnology‐enabled dual neurotherapy (denoted as ADNT) for PCa. The ADNT employs hybrid nanovesicles composed of autologous tumor cell membranes and functionalized liposomes to codeliver the β‐blocker and the muscarinic receptor antagonist to autonomic nerves in residual tumor. In refractory, highly invasive, and orthotopic murine PCa models, the ADNT effectively delays postoperative recurrence and metastasis. Light‐sheet fluorescence microscopy visually confirms the downregulation of autonomic nerve infiltration. Cytometry by time‐of‐flight reveals that ADNT remodels neuro–immune crosstalk and the chemokine network, promoting antitumor immune response and suppressing tumor progression. Additionally, ADNT also alleviates cancer‐associated cachexia and anxiety. Combined with immune checkpoint blockade, ADNT induces complete responses in 100% of mice. Immunofluorescence staining of human PCa specimens confirms the clinical translatability of ADNT, establishing ADNT as a promising therapeutic strategy for PCa.
n54ad3eb4fa51: The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small‐particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser‐induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high‐voltage performances. The direct bottom–up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li‐rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic‐resolution imaging, operando x‐ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut‐off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine‐learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition‐metal framework in the high‐entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5–4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg−1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high‐voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next‐generation energy storage research.
nec72d72e5a4d: Aqueous Zn–I2 batteries are promising for sustainable energy storage systems, yet their practical performance is severely limited by the formation and shuttling of polyiodide intermediates. Here, we report a site separation strategy to block the generation paths of polyiodides and address the related issues from the source. This is realized with a site‐separated polymer (SSP) binder that strongly and selectively confines I2 and I− at varied functional groups on different side chains. It disrupts their coupling to generate polyiodides chemically. Meanwhile, these effective interactions regulate the thermodynamic features of iodine species, which disfavors the formation of polyiodide intermediates and promotes direct I2/I− conversion during electrochemical reactions. The binder also reinforces cathode integrity at different iodine loadings. Therefore, the I2/SSP cathode delivers 212 mAh g−1 capacity at 0.2 A g−1 and retains 102 mAh g−1 at 50 A g−1, superior to 172 mAh g−1/11 mAh g−1 with the conventional polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder. I2/SSP also realizes 97.1% capacity retention over 31000 cycles at 20 A g−1, again far exceeding 46.8% after 20000 cycles for I2/PVDF. Under a high iodine loading of 50 mg cm−2, the I2/SSP cathode further achieves 10.1 mAh cm−2 capacity with 97.9% retention over 400 cycles.
n14018800165a: Sn with a high theoretical capacity and a low‐voltage plateau is considered a promising anode material for high‐energy‐density sodium ion batteries (HSIBs). However, the huge volume changes and poor conductivity of its sodiation products make it difficult to achieve long‐term stability and excellent rate performance. Herein, a remarkably simple structural reinforcement and three‐in‐one kinetic enhancement strategy is proposed for microsized Sn (µ‐Sn) electrode by introducing trace µ‐Bi. Interestingly, µ‐Bi spontaneously evolves into a 3D cross‐linked interlocked nanosheet network during cycling, ensuring long‐term structural stability of µ‐Sn. Meanwhile, the diametrically opposed patterns of electrical conductivity change in Bi and Sn during sodiation are utilized to achieve dynamic complementarity of their conductivity and reaction kinetics throughout the entire charge/discharge process. Additionally, the supercontinuous (104) crystal plane in the 3D Bi network and the Bi/Sn heterointerface in‐situ formed further accelerate e−/Na+ transfer. As a result, the prepared µ‐Sn10Bi simultaneously exhibits high reversible capacity, excellent rate performance and ultralong cycle life in both half and full cell at room/low temperatures. Structural evolution/kinetic enhancement/sodium storage mechanism and structure‐activity relationship of µ‐Sn10Bi are revealed in detail, providing a constructive view for designing low‐cost, high‐capacity, structurally stable, fast‐charging anode with wide‐temperature adaptability for HSIBs.
n947686ae7626: Decoupling ionic conductivity from polymer segmental relaxation while maintaining interfacial stability remains a pivotal challenge for solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). In this study, we construct an ionic‐ligand‐assisted transport framework by copolymerizing a fluorinated acrylate polymer with a poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) and optimizing the lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt concentration. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that cationic PIL moieties strongly anchor FSI− anions, creating anion‐rich, spatially correlated coordination pathways that facilitate efficient Li+ hopping. The optimized electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity (0.38 mS cm−1) and an exceptional Li+ transference number (0.77) at 30°C. The fluorinated backbone and PIL synergistically expand the oxidative stability window to 4.94 V and promote an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li‐metal anode. Consequently, Li||Cu cells cycle stably for over 400 cycles with 99.1% average Coulombic efficiency. Solid‐state Li||LiNi0.9Co0.05Mn0.05O2 (NCM90) cells retain ≈81.0% capacity after 600 cycles at 4.3 V, and ≈83.1% capacity after 200 cycles at 4.5 V. Moreover, a high‐energy‐density (515 Wh kg−1) solid‐state pouch cell with an ultrathin Li anode (50 µm) and a high‐loading NCM90 cathode (≈56 mg cm−2) delivers stable cycling and exceptional safety. This ionic‐ligand regulation paradigm provides critical mechanistic insights for designing high‐performance and high‐safety solid‐state batteries.
nf67b121ce351: All‐solid‐state batteries offer a safer route toward electrochemical energy storage with high energy density, but the active‐material utilization is commonly limited by unbalanced carrier transport dynamics through spatially decoupled delivery pathways, which overlap only at restricted reaction fronts. Such an issue is particularly severe for electronically and ionically insulating sulfur/Li2S, making efficient sulfur conversion the key bottleneck for practical all‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs). Here, we propose surface‐bound ion‐electron convergent interphases on the Li2S surface that reconstruct localized triple‐phase contacts into an integrated active surface. Using the effective magnetic moment, originating from spin asymmetry, as a screening criterion for interfacial affinity, Li2FeS2 is identified to form a robust surface‐bound interphase with Li2S, which bridges separated ion and electron pathways at the reaction areas, decreasing the transport tortuosity and lowering the activation barriers for both Li2S oxidation and reduction. Consequently, ASSLSBs stably work over 10 000 cycles at 1 mg cm−2 while delivering a loading‐insensitive sulfur utilization of 97.8% and 95.8% at 1 and 8 mg cm−2, respectively. Moreover, a record areal capacity of 38.69 mAh cm−2 is achieved, highlighting the spatially surface‐bound mixed conductors as an effective design principle for synchronizing coupled ion‐electron transfer (CIET) in all‐solid‐state batteries.
na6c13889b919: Selective ammonium (NH4 +) recovery from complex wastewater streams remains a pivotal challenge in sustainable nitrogen management. Capacitive deionization (CDI) offers an energy-efficient electrochemical route for ion separation, yet its practical application is constrained by the inherent trade-off between NH4 + adsorption capacity and selectivity. Herein, we circumvent this fundamental limitation through the rational molecular engineering of an organic electroactive material, 1,4-bis(1H-imidazo[4,5-b]phenazin-2-yl)benzene (IPB), which features extended electron delocalization and abundant C═N moieties for NH4 +-specific redox-coupled capture. The resulting IPB-based CDI prototype delivers a high NH4 + adsorption capacity of 267.23 mg g−1 and a fast rate of 62.51 mg g−1 min−1, while sustaining remarkable selectivity in complex multi-ion matrices, thereby effectively surpassing the conventional capacity-selectivity trade-off. Notably, CDI adsorption reduces wastewater NH4 + levels to below 3 mg L−1 and achieves 82.3% direct recovery as liquid fertilizer during CDI desorption, as demonstrated by isotope tracing experiments. The CDI process exhibits a low carbon footprint of only 4.66 × 10−2 t CO2-equivalent per tonne of NH4 + treated, underscoring its superior life-cycle sustainability. Therefore, this work proposes a molecularly engineered organic electrode material for high-performance wastewater remediation and circular nutrient recovery, paving the way toward carbon-neutral electrochemical water treatment technologies.
n464138b06e46: Ammonia (NH3) underpins fertilizer production and is emerging as a renewable-energy carrier. Solar-driven gas-phase N2/H2 conversion requires catalysts that couple efficient light utilization with structural stability under H2-rich conditions. Here, Nb5+ incorporation into CeO2 contracts the lattice and induces compressive microstrain, suppressing excessive oxygen-sublattice reduction and preserving Ru dispersion. In situ NAP-XPS and computational results show that Nb-CeO2 maintains an electron-enriched Ru working state under reaction conditions, which is further promoted by illumination. Accordingly, 5 wt% Ru/Nb-CeO2 achieves an NH3 synthesis rate of 7.4 mmol g−1 h−1 at 350°C and 0.1 MPa and remains stable for 144 h. Kinetic analyses and in situ DRIFTS indicate that the electronically promoted Ru state alleviates N2-activation limitations and facilitates subsequent *NHx hydrogenation and NH3 desorption. Scale-up synthesis affords a 3 wt% Ru/Nb-CeO2-L catalyst stable for 480 h and operable under outdoor concentrated sunlight. A screening-level analysis estimates a catalyst-and-feedstock cost of 286–322 USD tNH3 −1 under the lower-bound electricity scenario, 42%–51% below the selected Cs-Ru/MgO benchmark within the same framework. These results identify lattice strain as a promising strategy for simultaneously stabilizing the oxygen sublattice and electronically promoting Ru for efficient solar-driven ammonia synthesis.
n748f7dfff5d7: Granular hydrogels have attracted widespread interest for wound healing applications, yet their static design, in which microstructure and void space remain fixed, contrasts with the dynamic nature of tissue repair where processes like provisional extracellular matrix (pECM) assembly, cell organization, and nascent tissue formation evolve over time. Here, this disparity is addressed by designing dynamic granular hydrogels that are modularly assembled using microgels with pre‐programmed and precise degradation rates ranging from a few days to several weeks. Microgel degradation is controlled via modulation of hydrolytic susceptibility of hyaluronic acid polymers. The biological significance of timed pore expansion in dynamic granular hydrogels is investigated in a mouse muscle crush injury model. While slow‐degrading hydrogels support a distinct spatial assembly of cell‐instructive interstitial matrix and basement membrane proteins in the expanded pore space, this pECM remodeling is adversely altered in non‐degrading or fast‐degrading hydrogels. Slow‐degrading dynamic granular hydrogels also show long‐term therapeutic benefits on muscle wound healing, evidenced by reduced fibrosis, enhanced myogenesis, and improved functional force recovery. Collectively, these striking results demonstrate the profound significance of incorporating dynamicity through controlled microgel degradation in advanced granular biomaterials to improve tissue repair outcomes.
n77cf6ff0225e: The rational design of high-performance adsorbents is central to environmental remediation and separation. Yet whether assembling identical adsorption-active motifs into higher-order architectures can amplify the contribution of each motif beyond simple additivity remains unclear. Herein, the same hydrogen-bonded aramide building block is progressively organized into acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures, establishing a motif-conserved platform for isolating architectural effects on iodine capture. Across the designed architecture series, uptake capacity, kinetics, and retention improve stepwise from the acyclic structures to the macrocycle and further to the cage. Normalization to the number of aramide motifs reveals that the adsorption contribution of each motif also increases along this sequence, demonstrating non-additive amplification rather than simple accumulation of binding sites. Notably, one cage captures up to 84 I3 − per molecule in the presence of a 100-fold excess of competing anions, representing the highest value reported for molecular adsorbents. Structural and computational analyses attribute this behavior primarily to strengthened motif-level host–guest interactions generated by progressive architectural organization, while solid-state packing modulates the distribution and accessibility of adsorption space. This work identifies progressive organization as a design paradigm for amplifying adsorption performance, offering insights into the development of advanced adsorbent materials.
nf9fba03b7493: Perovskite‐organic tandem solar cells (PO‐TSCs) offer a compelling platform for flexible photovoltaics by combining wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite top cells with mechanically compliant organic rear cells. However, their long‐term stability is critically limited by the intrinsic instability of WBG mixed‐halide perovskites. Here, through systematic ageing and mechanistic analyses, we identify halide phase segregation in the WBG perovskite sub‐cell under photothermal stress as the dominant degradation pathway that dictates the operational stability of the PO‐TSC investigated here. To address this challenge, we develop a halogenated cyclodextrin‐based supramolecular strategy that enables precise regulation of perovskite crystallization, defect passivation and halide distribution. Synergistic host‐guest, hydrogen‐bonding, halogen‐bonding and coordination interactions simultaneously regulate crystallization and suppress ion migration to result in stabilized halide homogeneity. Consequently, 1.80‐eV WBG devices achieve 20.60% efficiency with improved operational stability. Integrated PO‐TSCs deliver an efficiency of 27.17% (certified 26.3%) together with T80 lifetimes of 1100 h under maximum power point tracking (MPPT) operation and T85 lifetimes of 1128 h under thermal stress of 85°C, while flexible PO‐TSCs reach an efficiency of 24.00%. This work defines a general supramolecular design paradigm for efficient, durable and flexible tandem photovoltaics.
n1ae874d4db3f: The unique properties and application possibilities of two‐dimensional (2D) materials motivate the exploration of different nanolaminated compounds. Here, by using a molten salt approach, we selectively etch Ti2InB2 with ZnCl2 to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti2B2Clx MBene. Upon etching, indium atoms are completely removed from the precursor and replaced by chlorine surface terminations with a coverage of 1.1 < x < 1.4. Further, in situ x‐ray diffraction indicates a direct biphasic transformation from Ti2InB2 to ml‐MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation. A computational framework based on density functional theory further corroborates these experimental observations by showing a negative reaction free energy for the formation of ml‐MBene, favourable over all competing processes. In addition, A‐element substitution into the 3D Ti2ZnB2 phase is predicted to be endergonic, consistent with the absence of experimental evidence for its formation. Initial Li‐ion battery performance evaluation showed a stable discharge capacity similar to or better than MAX phases and other borides. Altogether, the theoretical framework combined with materials synthesis and characterization provides a general approach for 2D materials development, for further expansion of the family of 2D materials.
n55bb43460350: Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct growth routes that rely on metal catalysts in contact with the substrate, causing metallic residue, film non‐uniformity, and the need for post‐growth processing. Here, we report the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2‐inch sapphire wafer via thermal chemical vapor deposition, in which a remotely positioned catalyst decomposes the carbon precursor into active carbon feedstock, keeping the growth substrate free of metallic contamination. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects no catalyst residue across the wafer and confirms a highly sp2‐hybridized carbon network, while electron microscopy reveals a random polygonal carbon network lacking long‐range periodicity. Raman and atomic force microscopy mapping confirm uniform and atomically smooth monolayer coverage, while electrical measurements establish its insulating character with ambipolar, gate‐tunable hopping transport. This synthesis approach provides precise control over thickness and uniformity at the wafer scale, enabling direct device integration of amorphous carbon for a wide range of applications, particularly as an interlayer for epitaxial growth of freestanding semiconductor membranes.
n870a6c677c0e: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have evolved from passive electrodes into active transducers that sense, amplify, and increasingly compute at the boundary between circuits and living tissue. Over the past decade, advances span molecular design of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs), electrolyte and channel engineering, device architectures, and circuit integration, to system‐level translation. Unlike existing reviews that treat these in isolation, emphasizing single material classes, mechanisms, or applications, this article unifies them through bioelectronic interface design, working from biological demands to demonstrated capabilities. We analyze operating principles, benchmarking metrics and structure–property relationships across p‐type, n‐type, and biodegradable OMIECs. The electrolyte‐channel region emerges as where biology and electronics converge; we survey gel electrolytes, semiconducting hydrogels, and all‐gel devices, alongside planar, vertical, fiber, textile, and printed architectures. We assess how design choices impact performance across electrophysiological, biochemical, implantable, wearable, and plant‐bioelectronic applications, while addressing biocompatibility, stability, and standardization requirements. Finally, we outline OECT‐native platforms that consolidate sensing, memory, computation, and actuation within closed‐loop, autonomous bioelectronic interfaces, arguing that this convergence represents the most consequential near‐term direction for the field.
n2bc00d895f1c: The therapeutic efficacy of cuproptosis is constrained by its insufficient activation and resistance mechanisms. Here, a lanthanide/transition metal ion‐coordinated nanoparticle, La‐Cu@Lap/IWR‐1, with optimized coordination, has been proven to achieve remarkable results in realizing comprehensive resistance‐eliminating cuproptosis activation. La3+ not only enhances Cu2+‐mediated multiple enzyme‐mimetic activities via coordination to amplify oxidative stress but also disrupts lysosomal acidification to improve copper ion availability. Moreover, combined with lapatinib (Lap), it alleviates the shielding effect of mediator of cell motility 1 (MEMO1) on Cu2+, significantly strengthening the cuproptosis activation efficacy. Meanwhile, the released Wnt inhibitor IWR‐1 can not only inhibit the Wnt/β‐catenin signaling pathway that is concomitantly activated during cuproptosis induction to weaken the oxidative stress tolerance of tumor cells but also synergize with Lap to downregulate hypoxia‐inducible factor 1α (HIF‐1α) expression, thereby effectively eliminating cuproptosis resistance. This comprehensive cuproptosis not only triggers significant immunogenic cell death but also synchronously inhibits key steps of tumor metastasis, such as epithelial‐mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix remodeling. This work proposes a therapeutic strategy for achieving comprehensive resistance‐eliminating cuproptosis activation using lanthanide/transition metal ion coordination nanomaterials, providing a new entry point for tumor therapy.
n4368b3f0cd29: Cancer immunotherapy is limited by insufficient immunomodulatory efficacy and systemic toxicity. This study reports a giant silver cluster‐incorporated polyoxoniobate (PONb), K6Na21H39{Ag30Cl4(SeO3)4@(SiNb18O54)6}·96H2O (1), as a potent immunotherapeutic agent. 1 features a unique core‐shell architecture, comprising a silver cluster core [Ag30Cl4(SeO3)4]18+ and a shell of six [SiNb18O54]14− polyanions. Notably, 1 contains the largest silver cluster (30 Ag+) in a molecular PONb with solubility and biocompatibility under physiological conditions to date. In vitro, 1 exhibits potent cytotoxicity against mouse colorectal carcinoma cells with an IC50 of 0.11 µM, triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). Additionally, it induces polarization of macrophages to the antitumor M1‐phenotype. In vivo, it outperforms doxorubicin (DOX) in suppressing tumor growth, with 1 achieving 90.63% tumor inhibition at 5 mg/kg (0.23 µmol/kg). Unlike DOX‐induced immunosuppression and hepatic toxicity, 1 robustly activates antitumor immune response via an ROS‐dependent mechanism by promoting T cell priming in the tumor‐draining lymph node and effector T cell infiltration into tumors, without impairing organ functions. Moreover, 1 converts tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs) from the protumorogenic M2‐phenotype to the antitumor M1‐phenotype, further reprogramming the immune microenvironment in tumor tissues. This study validates PONbs as a promising class of immunotherapeutics, bridging structural innovation in inorganic chemistry with improved cancer immunotherapy.
nae6d27d955fe: We demonstrate the use of macrocyclic BINOL‐phosphates for the active metal template synthesis of [2]rotaxanes via Cu(I)‐mediated alkyne‐azide cycloaddition. This novel methodology represents a key extension of the current active metal template approach beyond nitrogen‐based macrocycles and allowed for the synthesis of 17 differently functionalized chiral rotaxanes in yields up to 93%. Mechanistic studies combining DFT calculations, control experiments, and kinetic experiments support a dinuclear phosphate‐Cu2 intermediate, which makes the formation of the rotaxanes kinetically competitive. Enabled by this novel methodology, we prepared both diastereomers of highly functionalized interlocked bis‐BINOL rotaxanes.
n9f0eba45853c: Functional DNAs have attracted attention in cancer diagnosis and therapy owing to their programmable sequence specificity. However, the designed DNAs often fail to operate in target cells because intracellular environments evolve during cancer progression and across different cell types. Here, we aimed to predict DNA duplex stability across stages of cancer progression using thermodynamic parameters. As direct physicochemical measurements in living cells are challenging, we employed a pseudo‐cellular System for Highlighting the Environments inside the ceLL (SHELL) that preserves native cellular components and molecular crowding. We determined the thermodynamic parameters of DNA duplex formation in SHELLs derived from normal, mild cancer, and aggressive cancer cells. DNA duplexes became progressively destabilized with cancer progression, leading us to derive exact cell‐type‐specific nearest‐neighbor (NN) parameters in SHELL (SHELL‐NN parameters). As an example of how these parameters can be applied, we identify a quantitative design criterion in which duplex regions must be sufficiently stabilized, defined by duplex stability at 37°C (−∆G°37 > 9.8 kcal mol−1) to remain hybridized in normal cells and suppress background dissociation, while still enabling target‐induced dissociation in cancer cells. This environment‐specific thermodynamic threshold provides a quantitative design criterion for functional nucleic acid systems in cancer‐associated cellular environments.
n08d84eed77d4: Enzymatic cyclization of ultrashort single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) remains challenging. While conventional strategies have enabled the preparation of ultrashort ssDNA circles by passively suppressing intermolecular oligomerization, they lack the mechanical driving force to overcome the physical strain required for smaller circles. Herein, we report a conformation‐programmed cyclization (CPC) strategy that uses a V‐shaped DNA scaffold to guide DNA toward a cyclization‐favored conformation, with electrostatic nanoconfinement likely contributing to this conformational control. By utilizing a V‐shaped DNA scaffold with a flexible poly(thymine) hinge, we use the electrostatic interactions within the DNA scaffold under low ionic strength conditions to help pre‐organize the substrate into a pre‐bent, cyclization‐prone state. This strategy enables the near‐quantitative preparation of 15 nucleotide (nt) ssDNA circles (∼97% yield) and produces 14 nt circles with a yield of 71% through a stepwise loading protocol. The CPC platform is broadly applicable, achieving efficient cyclization across a wide size range from 14 to 70 nt. Importantly, the highly strained topology of these prepared circles enables strain‐promoted, toehold‐free strand displacement, significantly accelerating molecular switching kinetics compared to conventional linear duplexes. Our work moves beyond passive reaction‐pathway control toward active conformational engineering, providing a reliable framework for constructing and utilizing strained nucleic acid architectures in DNA nanotechnology.
nbb3406ea1ed8: Owing to safety concerns associated with previous gadolinium‐based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) agents, pyclen‐based Gd chelates are emerging as promising alternatives. However, the development of pyclen‐based chelators has been hindered by synthetic challenges. In this work, we report two new pyclen‐based chelators featuring α‐aryl‐substituents on two of the acetate arms. Using the Petasis reaction, two lanthanide chelators 3a and 3b were synthesized in just two steps from pyclen. 3a‐Gd exhibits superior coordination stability and relaxivity compared to previously reported Gd3+ chelates of comparable molecular weight. It also has low cytotoxicity and produces a strong, long‐lasting in vivo MRI signal, enabling real‐time monitoring of tissues/organs, as demonstrated in heart, liver, and kidney imaging of mice. Additionally, the chelator also shows improved coordination kinetics for In3+, Tb3+, Lu3+, and Y3+, highlighting its potential for the development of a new class of next‐generation radiopharmaceuticals.
n4083857d0a6a: Professor Dr. Günther Maier, “Tetrahedrane Maier,” the chemist who provided the chemical community with so many “impossible” molecules died on April 10 at the age of 94.
nfd1a5254e0e3: Flexible and distributed radiation detection calls for lightweight, mechanically compliant photonic architectures, motivating the chemical design of highly efficient crystalline emitters and the transformation into processable glasses and fibre‐integrated devices. Here, we report a Cu(I)‐alloying strategy for the Ag‐ based hybrid clusters Ag2I2(Dppy)3 (Dppy, diphenyl‐2‐pyridylphosphine) that induces lattice distortion and introduces Cu‐derived electronic states, thereby modulating metal‐halide‐to‐ligand charge transfer and suppressing non‐radiative recombination. This strategy enhances the crystalline‐state light yield by ∼31‐fold, while the resulting glass achieves a light yield of ~20400 photons MeV−1, together with a low x‐ray detection limit and robust operational stability. Moreover, thermal drawing further produces flexible optical fibres with a low propagation loss of 0.41 dB cm−1, integrating scintillation, guided transport and remote readout. These results establish emissive‐centre alloying engineering as an important route towards highly efficient processable scintillating glasses and flexible optical fibres.
n47aeece215d3: We report highly efficient mechanochemical redox reactivity between polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) and base metals, enabling simultaneous polymer decomposition, fluorination of metals without F2 or HF, and mechanochemical dealloying. While milling with metals has recently emerged as a mechanochemical platform for PTFE defluorination, most such work has relied on highly reactive, air-sensitive metals, such as alkali elements. We now demonstrate a proof-of-principle for direct and efficient transformation of PTFE into a mixture of sp2 -carbon and a metal fluoride by ball-milling with stoichiometric amounts of safe-to-handle, abundant, inexpensive metals such as zinc. The reactivity is applicable to other metals, as shown by aluminum, lead and cadmium, and the process is also extendable into a two-step, one-pot mechanochemical strategy to generate NaF as a recycled fluorine source, along with a ZnO/carbon mixture which can undergo carbothermal reduction to recover zinc, suggesting an opportunity to develop a zinc-based PTFE defluorination cycle. Moreover, ball-milling with PTFE is shown to transform brass into a mixture of copper metal and ZnF2, providing a proof-of-principle for mechanochemical dealloying of mixed-metal materials using fluoropolymer waste as a reagent. This work introduces a different, mechanochemistry-based paradigm for straightforward, atom-economic, and potentially more sustainable PTFE defluorination, presenting its valorization as a mechanochemical fluorinating agent.
n34f59b7068f1: C─H monofluoroalkylation of pyridines is a highly desirable transformation in medicinal chemistry because the monofluoroalkyl group is known to impart favorable properties to drug candidates, and pyridine rings are prevalent in drug molecules. However, only a few methods have been reported, and they are limited to ortho‐selective reactions. Herein, we report an unprecedented method for meta‐selective C─H monofluoroalkylation of pyridines via reactions between difluoroalkyl radicals and dihydropyridines generated in situ. During the reactions, a defluorination/olefin isomerization cascade converts initially formed difluoroalkylated dihydropyridines to monofluoroalkylated pyridines. The method accommodates a broad range of pyridine substrates, as well as other N‐heteroarenes and fluoroalkylating reagents, and shows promise for late‐stage functionalization of pyridine‐containing drugs.
n5a110f3d5d51: The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a prototypical proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) reaction, yet the atomistic origin of its metal‐dependent pH effect remains unclear. Here, combining constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics with in situ infrared spectroscopy, we unravel the microscopic origins of metal‐dependent pH effects in HER catalysis on Pt(111) and Au(111). We reveal that HER kinetics are governed by two competing spatial proton transfer topologies associated with the Volmer water‐dissociation step: a low‐barrier cross‐layer proton transfer (CLPT) pathway and a high‐barrier intra‐layer proton transfer (ILPT) pathway. For Pt(111), strong metal–water interactions yield a pH‐responsive water network. Under acidic conditions, a balanced intra‐ and cross‐layer hydrogen‐bond network promotes the CLPT in the Volmer step, thereby accelerating HER kinetics. By contrast, alkaline media induce a rigid H‐down interfacial water layer that favors the sluggish ILPT pathway. Conversely, weak metal–water interactions on Au(111) maintain a pH‐insensitive, predominantly parallel‐flat water orientation that restricts the Volmer step to cooperate only with the high‐barrier ILPT in both acidic and alkaline solutions. Our findings establish a fundamental causal link among metal–water interactions, interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, proton transfer pathways, and HER kinetics, providing atomistic insight into the design of pH‐robust electrocatalysts.
n045ab3586acb: Conductive coordination polymers (CCPs) could combine the merits of both conductive polymers and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) and hence have attracted extensive attention for various applications. However, the modulation of their properties is challenging and rarely studied. Herein, three CCPs, denoted as Cu─6O, Cu─6N, and Cu─3O3N, featuring Cu─O4, Cu─(NH)4, and Cu─O2(NH)2 units respectively, are constructed to systematically investigate the effect of the ligating atoms and bonding states on the properties. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu─O bonds are dominated by electrostatic interactions, whereas Cu─N bonds exhibit stronger covalent character, and the mixed Cu─O2(NH)2 unit further enhances the overall bond strength by optimizing orbital hybridization and energy matching. Consequently, Cu─6O shows the weakest Cu─X (X═O or NH) bonds, poorest thermal stability and undergoes irreversible degradation upon base conditions at pH above ∼9.5, while also suffering severe structural degradation under electrochemical condition. The degradation mechanism was also revealed. Conversely, the stronger coordination bonds in Cu─6N and Cu─3O3N endow them with superior thermal, chemical, and electrochemical stability. This work highlights the essential role of ligating atoms in determining the bonding states and provides a design principle for developing robust CCPs.
n4a8a292b6c01: The discovery of novel ribozymes is crucial for both advancing RNA technologies and illuminating potential RNA world scenarios. Currently, catalytic evolution of ribozymes primarily relies on the slow, random process of natural or artificial selection. In this study, we show that a distinct catalytic feature can be deliberately imposed onto a preexisting ribozyme scaffold through ribozyme redesign with a minimal alteration rather than molecular evolution. We demonstrate a single‐nucleotide mutation repurposes an alkyl‐transfer ribozyme into a multifunctional hydrolysis ribozyme, while preserving its overall catalytic scaffold. This hydrolase ribozyme operates analogously to a canonical protein enzyme, transforming various ester and ether substrates into the release of carboxylic acids, alcohols, and amines. Structural and kinetic analyses uncover a water‐mediated mechanism for ester/ether bond cleavage. Application of this hydrolase ribozyme in living cells enables controlled activation and release of diverse payloads on demand, such as fluorescent and drug molecules, for cell‐specific discrimination. This study highlights the previously underappreciated multifunctionalities within RNA catalytic architectures, broadening the scope of developing versatile ribozymes for diversified applications.
ndb6c13d6dd96: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction (CO2RR) to value‐added multicarbon products using non‐copper‐based catalysts remains a major challenge, especially for selective ethanol production. Herein, we report that chiral Co3O4 featuring strong electron spin polarization achieves a maximum ethanol Faradaic efficiency of 90% at ‐0.9 V versus NHE in KHCO3 electrolytes under a 30 bar CO2 pressure, substantially outperforming both racemic Co3O4 and previously reported non‐copper‐based catalysts. The enhanced spin polarization in chiral Co3O4 facilitates electron transfer and promotes the activation of the adsorbed CO2, while also lowering the free energy change for C–C coupling to form *COCHO intermediate, thereby promoting ethanol production. Our work establishes spin polarization as a key determinant for efficient C–C coupling on non‐copper‐based catalysts and provides mechanistic principles for the rational design of CO2RR electrocatalyst.
nf8e5c78f96e9: The development of highly active and stable low-Pt alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalysts is crucial for reducing the cost of hydroxide exchange membrane fuel cells (HEMFCs). Here, it is realized by a HOR/ORR bifunctional Pt@MoOx/C catalyst featuring strong metal-support interaction (SMSI). The partially covered MoOx species exhibit strong interactions with Pt, which stabilize the Pt nanoparticles under both HOR and ORR conditions. The modulated electronic structure arising from SMSI optimizes the binding of hydrogen and hydroxyl species on Pt sites. In addition to the conventional electronic effect of SMSI, the catalyst–electrolyte interfacial water structure is also regulated, resulting in a more interconnected hydrogen-bond network. Consequently, Pt@MoOx/C exhibits outstanding activity and stability toward both the HOR and ORR. It delivers an HOR exchange current density of 3.55 mA cmPt −2, which is 4.4 times that of commercial Pt/C, and a ORR mass activity of 1.08 A mgPt −1 at 0.9 V versus RHE, 2.3 times that of commercial Pt/C. Furthermore, an HEMFC employing Pt@MoOx/C as both the anode and cathode catalysts, with an ultralow total Pt loading of 0.1 mgPt cm−2, delivers a peak power density of 920 mW cm−2 and operates stably for over 250 h.
n70116340e730: Ru‐based catalysts demonstrate attractive activity and cost advantages for alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR), yet their practical deployment is limited by rapid deactivation at high anodic potentials in fuel cells. Here we identify reversible hydroxyl‐related surface passivation, particularly excessive *OH accumulation, as a key contributor to high‐potential Ru deactivation, and demonstrate that it can be mitigated through coupled regulation of *OH coverage and interfacial hydrogen supply. Guided by this mechanistic insight, we design a Pd‐core, tetra‐element‐ensemble Ru skin catalyst (Pd@Tees Ru), where electronic modulation of the multimetallic Ru shell suppresses excessive *OH accumulation, while the Pd core serves as a dynamic lattice‐hydrogen reservoir. Electrochemical evidence reveals the anodic release of interstitial hydrogen from the Pd core, sustaining *H coverage at the active interface and mitigating excessive accumulation of hydroxyl‐related surface species. Such synergistic interfacial regulation enables sustained HOR activity at potentials above 0.5 V. An anion‐exchange membrane fuel cell with the Pd@Tees Ru anode achieves a peak power density of 1.78 W cm−2 under H2/O2 conditions and operates stably for 200 h at 500 mA cm−2.
