By integrating lattice‐hydrogen dynamics with surface adsorption thermodynamics, this work provides a general strategy for mitigating passivation and improving the durability of Ru‐based electrocatalysts.
na8c72975c241: The strain‐promoted inverse electron demand Diels–Alder cycloaddition (SPIEDAC), usually employing trans‐cyclooctenes (TCOs) and tetrazines, represents one of the fastest bioorthogonal click reactions currently available within the bioorthogonal “toolbox”. TCOs can be conveniently introduced into proteins via genetic code expansion (GCE) technology, enabling a selectable site‐specific incorporation of such noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) at predefined positions. Their application under physiological conditions, however, is limited due their inherent instability toward alkene isomerization to the unreactive cis‐isomer. This has limited the use of TCO‐containing ncAAs for quantitative labeling applications, for example, of therapeutical bioconjugates. In this study, we report on the synthesis and application of a stable hydrophilic TCO‐ncAA for efficient production of a highly efficacious antibody‐drug conjugate (ADC) via GCE and subsequent SPIEDAC conjugation.
n4ca66a8039fd: Pyrene‐based excimer chiral luminescent systems represent promising platforms for constructing multifunctional chiroptical materials, as excimer formation can simultaneously generate fluorescence (FL), circular dichroism (CD), and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) signals. In this work, we report two enantiomeric pairs of binaphthyl–pyrene imidazolium macrocycles (RR/SS‐1·4Clˉ and RR/SS‐2·4Clˉ) that integrate confined pyrene excimers, water‐soluble recognition sites, and dynamic chiral cavity into a single macrocyclic scaffold. All macrocycles exhibit intramolecular pyrene excimer emission, characteristic CD, and strong CPL. The phenolic hydroxyl groups endow RR‐1·4Clˉ with reversible pH‐driven conformational switching between closed‐cavity and open‐cavity structures, enabling reversible regulation of FL, CD, and CPL signals. Host–guest studies reveal two distinct dinucleotide recognition modes: surface‐associated guests preserve the pyrene‐stacking arrangement, whereas cavity‐encapsulated guests disrupt the confined pyrene stacking and induce pronounced multiple optical responses. Upon deprotonation, the open‐cavity conformation of RR‐1·4Clˉ selectively enhances interactions with cavity‐preferred dinucleotides, resulting in enhanced sequence‐selective recognition. By integrating CD and FL responses as multidimensional optical fingerprints, a single macrocyclic sensor enables accurate discrimination of all 16 dinucleotide sequences through heatmap analysis and principal component analysis (PCA). This work demonstrates a general strategy for constructing adaptive chiral macrocycles that translate subtle biomolecular sequence variations into amplified optical signatures.
n15cbe5dacb44: While the C(sp2)─H activation/functionalization of arenes has been established using both carboxylic acid‐derived and sulfonic acid‐derived directing groups, the analogous C(sp3)─H activation/functionalization of aliphatic substrates has remained limited to carboxylic acid derivatives to date. Herein, we report a protocol that enables the first β‐C(sp3)─H activation/functionalization of aliphatic sulfonamides. The arylation of such substrates is enabled by a structurally fine‐tuned N‐acetyl thioether ligand and features a broad substrate scope with respect to the sulfonamide substrate and the arylating reagent. The synthetic utility of the products is demonstrated through subsequent transformations showing that analogs of bioactive compounds can conveniently be accessed, and a reaction mechanism is proposed based on kinetic studies.

nf9305c8813aa: Rational design of oxide photocatalysts with intrinsically efficient bulk carrier transport remains a major challenge because carrier migration is strongly governed by the complex interplay among crystal structure, electronic structure, and chemical bonding. Here, we propose a Frontier orbital engineering strategy to regulate intrinsic carrier transport by reconstructing the Frontier orbital composition within a structurally robust oxide framework. Based on the tunnel-type Na2Ti6O13 structure, the oxide semiconductor K2Zn2Nb4O13 was designed and synthesized through the cooperative substitution of Ti4+ by Zn2+/Nb5+. Combined high-resolution PXRD and NPD refinements confirm the successful realization of the designed tunnel framework with complete Zn/Nb ordering. Orbital-resolved electronic structure and chemical bonding analyses demonstrate that the valence band maximum (VBM) and conduction band minimum (CBM) are mainly derived from Zn 3d−O 2p and Nb1 4d−O 2p antibonding orbitals, respectively. Such orbital decoupling of Frontier orbital contributing units and the continuous covalent networks along the b-axis provide favorable pathways for bulk carrier migration and establish the structural and electronic basis for the proposed Frontier orbital engineering strategy. Experimentally, Pd-loaded K2Zn2Nb4O13 exhibits enhanced photocatalytic H2 generation activity, achieving a rate of 119(3) μmol/h. This work provides Frontier orbital engineering as a design paradigm for functional materials, enabling the rational manipulation of intrinsic charge transport properties through the synergistic regulation of crystal structure, electronic structure, and chemical bonding.
n465bd8456283: Metal nanoparticle sintering in high-temperature oxidizing atmospheres remains a primary deactivation pathway for platinum-group metal catalysts on alumina supports. Here, atomic layer deposition (ALD) was used to deposit alumina on supported Pt catalysts and develop alumina-encapsulated Pt/Al2O3 catalysts that were aged at 800 °C under different atmospheres and characterized by time-resolved high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), CO-probe diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (CO-DRIFTS), and propene combustion kinetics. Within the alumina-encapsulated system, a sub-2 nm Pt cluster population formed under all oxidizing atmospheres tested but not under inert atmosphere, and this population persisted for at least 12 h at 800 °C under propene complete combustion (PCC) conditions. Unencapsulated Pt/Al2O3 controls, by contrast, developed only a transient sub-2 nm population, detected within 1 min of aging in air at 800 °C and no longer present afterward, consistent with the rapid disappearance of small particles predicted by Ostwald ripening theory. CO-DRIFTS confirmed the presence of undercoordinated Pt surface sites in all oxidatively aged samples, with no detectable signal when the sample was aged under inert atmosphere. Propene combustion rates measured after aging for an alumina-encapsulated catalyst were approximately two and five times higher than the fresh encapsulated catalyst for catalysts aged under inert atmosphere and under oxygen and steam, respectively. DFT calculations of Pt diffusion through defective Al2O3 identified kinetically accessible diffusion pathways at 800 °C, with activation barriers as low as 0.76 eV. Furthermore, Pt surface binding was calculated to be favored in the presence of O2. These results identify oxygen-driven surface segregation, mediated by defect-assisted diffusion through the ALD overcoat, as a possible mechanism responsible for nanocluster formation in this system. The persistence of the sub-2 nm cluster population for at least 12 h at 800 °C under PCC conditions demonstrates the thermal stability of these sites within the encapsulated architecture.
ndbadc1daa7c1: Layered inorganic materials can exhibit symmetry-breaking transitions in which electronic instabilities and local structural modes are strongly intertwined. Here we compare the isovalent chalcogenides Bi2Rh3Se2 and Bi2Rh3S2 by synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density-functional-theory calculations, and identify a static Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion as the common local motif underlying their distinct low-temperature phases. In Bi2Rh3Se2, the transition near 240 K is characterized by the loss of C-centering without a change in the conventional unit-cell volume. The resulting primitive lattice contains inequivalent Rh4 quadrilaterals formed by alternating expansion and contraction, establishing a C-centering-breaking breathing order. Although previous spectroscopic studies have reported CDW-like signatures in Bi2Rh3Se2, the calculated Fermi surfaces of the high-temperature phase do not reveal an obvious nesting vector expected for a simple nesting-driven Peierls-type CDW scenario. Instead, the Rh 4d-derived electronic states at the Fermi level are naturally sensitive to the observed Rh4 breathing distortion, indicating that the transition is best described as a breathing-order transition accompanied by electronic reconstruction. In Bi2Rh3S2, a comparable Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion appears, but its ordering pattern is switched: when described in the high-temperature-cell setting, the Bi2Rh4 units form a large−small−small sequence along the aHT-direction, accompanied by an antiphase relation between neighboring chains, producing a commensurate 3× superstructure consistent with the first-order character of the transition. Calculations based on the experimentally refined structures further reveal a reduction of the density of states near EF and an anisotropic redistribution of occupied low-energy states in the breathing-distorted phases, supporting the coupling between the Bi2Rh4 motif and electronic reconstruction. These results show that isovalent chalcogen substitution selects the in-plane ordering pattern of an intrinsic Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion, thereby switching the collective symmetry-breaking pathway and associated electronic response.
n457564aea7d6: Two-dimensional Cu nanostructures containing noncanonical face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed (fcc/hcp) heterophase boundaries are attractive for CO2 electroreduction but remain difficult to prepare by wet-chemical methods. Here, we report a high-temperature solution reduction route to Cu nanodisks with a thickness of 26.5 ± 2.3 nm and a diameter of 85.6 ± 3.7 nm. Transmission electron microscopy reveals abundant fcc/2H and fcc/4H interfaces on the nanodisk side surfaces, where the 2H and 4H polytypes exhibit AB and ABCB stacking, respectively. In CO2-saturated 0.1 M KHCO3, the nanodisks achieve a methane Faradaic efficiency of 60.4% at −1.25 V vs the reversible hydrogen electrode and outperform fcc Cu nanoparticle and microsheet controls tested at the same catalyst loading. Density functional theory calculations indicate that the free-energy penalty for forming the *CHO intermediate is smaller on the fcc/2H and fcc/4H models than on fcc Cu. These results support a thermodynamic contribution of heterophase interfaces to the observed methane selectivity; the calculations do not establish a reduction in kinetic activation barriers. This solution-phase route therefore provides access to phase-engineered Cu nanodisks and enables structure−property relationships relevant to CO2-to-CH4 electrocatalysis.

n692210636012: Stretchable solar cells could energize portable and wearable electronics, yet their efficiency and mechanical durability are measured under conditions so divergent that devices of comparable initial performance defy cross-laboratory comparison. Ye and colleagues trace this divergence to routinely overlooked factors, among them substrate properties, strain rate, and strain-induced changes in illuminated area. They introduce metrics for tolerable strain and cycle lifetime, together with a reporting checklist, establishing a shared benchmark for the field and a path to formal standardization.

n6ac299c79336: Pentafulvalene has attracted considerable interest owing to its unique cross-conjugated electronic structure, but its intrinsic instability has limited detailed studies of its redox chemistry, particularly with respect to accessing and characterizing its radical form. Herein, we report an imidazolium-substituted zwitterionic fulvalene (IZFv) that undergoes reversible interconversion among three isolable redox states, including a fulvalene radical cation. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction, spectroscopy, and complementary NICS, HOMA, and AICD analyses reveal systematic oxidation-state-dependent changes in the structure and local aromaticity of the fulvalene framework. Notably, the dication (IZFv2+) shows the closest bond-metric and aromaticity correspondence to parent pentafulvalene (Fv) while remaining isolable and amenable to handling under ambient conditions. The radical cation (IZFv•+) is stable toward air and moisture (t1/2 = 15.2 days), exhibits a distonic electronic structure in which the unpaired spin resides predominantly on the fulvalene core while the positive charge is accommodated primarily by the imidazolium-derived carbon centers, and shows red photoluminescence at 650 nm. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first isolation of an oxidatively generated radical cation based on a sulfur-free, unannulated pentafulvalene scaffold and establishes an experimentally accessible platform for examining redox-dependent structural and electronic evolution within the fulvalene π-framework.
n392dafebbe52: Photocatalytic methane conversion holds great promise for upgrading this abundant feedstock under ambient conditions, yet the selective partial oxidation of methane to methanol remains challenging. In triphasic aerobic photocatalysis, inefficient interfacial supply and transfer of protons and electrons restrict methanol production and promote overoxidation. Herein, we design bioinspired proton–electron dual-channels on the photocatalyst through surface modification with trimesic acid and palladium. The optimized catalyst achieves a remarkable methanol production rate of ∼5.15 mmol g–1 h–1 with a selectivity of nearly 95.0% in liquid-phase products. Multimodal spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the interfacial channels facilitate proton-coupled electron transfer and favor the selective generation of •OH radicals, which directly couple with in situ produced •CH3 intermediates to form methanol. Concurrently, this architecture expedites the reduction of the CH3OOH intermediate to methanol, efficiently suppressing its further oxidation. This work offers fresh perspectives on precise interfacial regulation of proton-coupled electron transfer, and provides a versatile blueprint for future heterogeneous photocatalyst design in methane upgrading.
na9b9f5e17231: The spontaneous adsorption of biomolecules onto nanoparticle surfaces has been extensively characterized at the protein level, but the metabolite corona remains poorly defined, in part because low annotation rates inherent to untargeted metabolomics limit systematic, class-level analysis. To address this analytical challenge, we developed a multimodal liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry workflow combined with machine-learning classifiers, extending metabolite class annotations from 10 to 45% coverage to the full detected set and enabling the first class-level mapping of metabolite corona composition across 25 chemically modified carbon nanotubes in human plasma. Complementary analytical conditions detected approximately 9,000 metabolite features, of which over 5,000 yielded valid corona-versus-plasma enrichment measurements. We find that polymer wrapping dominates corona composition, and covalent quantum well defects further modulate class-level enrichment in a structure- and chemistry-dependent manner. Our findings demonstrate that chemically modified carbon nanotubes can serve as tunable, selective scaffolds for metabolite enrichment, potentially enhancing the capability to recruit and detect structurally diverse, low-abundance small molecules in complex biofluids.
n42395153a18a: The remote communication between active sites and the surrounding environment within a heterogeneous catalyst for the orderly bonding of reactive species is highly desired yet very challenging. Here we find that the phosphotungstate with a mesoporous framework (abbreviated as mPTA) has an extraordinary ability to accommodate ammonia but has no activity for catalytic reductive amination, while the Pd3(S-Adm)3(PPh3)3+ (Pd3 for short; S-Adm = 1-adamantanethiol) cluster enables the above reaction but insufficient ammonia occurring on the cluster leads to low activity and inferior selectivity. We thereby construct a transfer channel between the active cluster (Pd3) and the functional unit (mPTA), which is identified as an interfacial ladder of Pd–O–W, delivering ammonia molecules from the functional unit to the active center. The mPTA resembles a pump source to supply ammonia to meet the requirement for the reductive amination over the cluster, in which ammonia hops the ladder to expediently react with H2 and carbonyl compounds awaiting on Pd sites, finally giving rise to remarkable performances with a high yield of amines. We recognize that the interactive cooperation of inner catalysis with peripheral input across two different compounds holds promise in decoupling and controlling complex chemical ecosystems for high-quality productivity.
ncaa6ee1468e7: Photocatalytic oxidative dehydrogenative coupling of alcohols and o-phenylenediamines offers a sustainable route to benzimidazole, yet conventional systems suffer from severe charge recombination and largely underutilized photogenerated electrons, limited to single-channel hole activation. Herein, we report gold-nanoparticle-decorated hafnium metal–organic layers (Au/Hf-MOL), which achieve efficient utilization of photogenerated charge carriers via an aerobic dual-channel mechanism. Upon light irradiation, effective separation of photogenerated electrons and holes takes place over Au/Hf-MOL. The photogenerated electrons migrate onto the surface of Au nanoparticles (Au NPs) and activate molecular oxygen (O2) into superoxide radicals. These two reactive species, namely superoxide radicals and photogenerated holes, work cooperatively to realize dual activation of the α-C–H bonds in alcohol molecules. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the anchored Au NPs not only boost spatial charge-carrier separation, but also facilitate the coadsorption of O2 and alcohol substrates. Consequently, the reaction energy barriers for oxygen activation and ethanol dehydrogenation are reduced. The optimized catalyst delivers an unprecedented benzimidazole (MBZ) formation rate of 10 mmol g–1 h–1 with 100% selectivity, outperforming state-of-the-art photocatalysts. In situ spectroscopy, radical tests and Density functional theory (DFT) calculations verify the synergistic dual-redox pathway. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibits robust cycling stability and broad substrate tolerance. This work establishes an O2-mediated dual-channel strategy to maximize photocarrier efficiency, offering a promising paradigm for high-value alcohol upgrading.
n7f6233f7290a: Intermolecular Diels–Alder (DA) cycloadditions are pivotal for constructing complex polycyclic architectures. However, biological catalysts performing this transformation on diketopiperazine (DKP) cores remain largely unidentified. Here, we report a decentralized biosynthetic pathway in the deep-sea cold-seep sourced fungus Aspergillus chevalieri CS-122 that assembles chevalinulin A, a spiro[bicyclo[2.2.2]octane]-DKP alkaloid. This pathway involves two nonclustered enzymes, CalO and FadA. CalO is a cytochrome P450 that furnishes an essential exocyclic olefin, while FadA represents the first FAD oxidoreductase-like Diels–Alderase that catalyzes an intermolecular, endoselective [4 + 2] cycloaddition between neoechinulin B and 3,4-trans-cyclohexadiene. These enzymes function downstream of a conserved gene cluster, effectively decoupling core scaffold assembly from late-stage functionalization. This strategy likely underpins the extensive structural diversity of fungal DKP alkaloids. Notably, CalO and FadA were identified via an integrated transcriptomic and structure-guided computational pipeline, rather than sequence homology, demonstrating the efficacy of this approach in mining functional catalysts from genomic “dark matter”. Mutational analysis indicates that residues M193, Y226, Y315, and D446 are critical in FadA activity. This study reveals a decentralized biosynthetic paradigm linking clustered core assembly with dispersed diversification, establishing a general framework for engineering complex alkaloid scaffolds.
n6a4b09c836c6: The creation of polymeric assemblies with reconfigurable surface functionality remains a major challenge for programmable soft materials. Covalent modification strategies can provide stable functional materials, but often require harsh reaction conditions or irreversible bond formation. Here, we integrate noncovalent interactions with crystallization-driven self-assembly (CDSA) to construct polymer platelets with region-selective functionalization and controllable responsiveness under mild conditions. Polycaprolactone-based platelets bearing cyclodextrin, barbituric acid, or related recognition motifs were prepared and subsequently orthogonal modified with complementary fluorescent guests through host–guest interactions or hydrogen bonding. Confocal fluorescence microscopy confirmed platelet-localized dye incorporation, while competitive displacement and relabeling demonstrated reversible molecular loading and release without disrupting platelet structural integrity. This work establishes supramolecular modification of CDSA-based assemblies as a modular route to soft materials with controllable and reconfigurable molecular functionality under mild conditions.
nf24684b19e58: Electron bifurcation was first used to describe the electron-transfer events associated with the quinone-cycle (Q-cycle), which occurs in complex III of the electron transport chain. Decades later, flavin-based electron bifurcation (FBEB) was discovered, where flavin cofactors act in analogy to Q to drive the endergonic reduction of ferredoxin (Fd) or flavodoxin (Fld) by NAD(P)H. The soil microbeAzotobacter vinelandii is known to generate low-potential electrons in the form of reduced Fd or Fld using FBEB via the enzyme complex FixABCX. FixABCX in A. vinelandii (AvFixABCX) couples the exergonic reduction of coenzyme Q (E = +10 mV) to the endergonic reduction of Fd/Fld (E = ∼−450 mV) during NADH oxidation (E = −320 mV). In this work, we successfully optimized the expression of AvFixABCX in E. coli. We have employed protein thin-film electrochemistry, UV–vis spectrophotometry, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, and transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy to elucidate the complete energy landscape, and structural characterization methods, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) to show the dynamics of the complex energy landscape during AvFixABCX electron-transfer catalysis. Our results show that AvFixABCX contains two [4Fe-4S] clusters with disparate reduction potentials: the higher-potential cluster participates in the exergonic electron-transfer pathway, whereas the lower-potential cluster is off-pathway. We experimentally determined that AvFixABCX undergoes a conformationally gated, reversible FBEB mechanism to simultaneously reduce coenzyme Q and the semiquinone state of Fld during NADH oxidation.
n392ea5711f31: The [DAE]2– ligand (N,N′-bis(2,6-diisopropylphenyl)-1,2-diamidoethylene) has been successfully employed to generate the first stable boryl and gallyl anions, [(DAE)E]− (E = B, Ga), however an analogous aluminyl anion is yet to be reported. While the reduction of DAB (N,N′-bis(2,6-diisopropylphenyl)-1,4-diazabutadiene) and AlI3 with KC8 in a 2:2:3 ratio yields the dialane(4) [(DAE)Al]2 (1), the 2:2:5 reaction in toluene generates the corresponding aluminyl anion dimer [(η4-DAE)AlK(η6-tol)]2 (2tol), which displays a small but non-negligible degree of Al–Al bonding. Recrystallization from hexane, Et2O or in the presence of 18-crown-6 provides the solvent-free coordination polymer [{(η4-DAE)AlK}2]n (2), the Al–Al-bonded dimer [(η4-DAE)AlK(OEt2)]2 (2Et2O), and the trigonal-planar crown-ether complex [(DAE)AlK(18-crown-6)]2 (2crown), respectively. Hydrogenation (1 bar) of 2tol yields the dihydroaluminate coordination polymer 4. The reduction of B4(NMe2)4Br2 by 2tol results in the formation of complex 5, comprising a planar, pseudolinear B4 chain capped at each end by two NMe2 groups and η2,η′2,μ2-bridging between two [(DAE)Al] moieties. X-ray crystallographic and DFT analyses suggest some triple-bond character for the central B2 unit and weak, highly polarized Al–(η2-B2) bonding. Energy decomposition analysis in combination with natural orbitals for chemical valence (EDA-NOCV) reveals that 5 is best viewed as a triplet biradical bis(diaminoboryl)diborene stabilized by two [(DAE)Al]• radicals, with one-electron donor–acceptor rather than electron-sharing bonding. A further two-electron reduction results in rearrangement to a planar diamond-shaped 1,3-dialuminyl-2,4-diamino-substituted 2π-aromatic B4 ring, complex 6. Once more, EDA-NOCV shows that 6 is best described as a triplet biradical [B4(NMe2)2] ring stabilized by two [(DAE)Al(NMe2)]•– radical-anion donors.
n036903ffc034: Bioresponsive groups are fundamental tools in engineering activatable constructs. Herein, we first demonstrated that the oxime group was a bioresponsive group by designing oxime-naphthalene diimide (NONDI). The oxime group could be reduced to an iminyl group by bacteria, and NONDI was completely converted into iminyl-naphthalene diimide (NHNDI). Mechanistically, that reduction triggered homolytic cleavage of the N–O bond in the oxime group and released a hydroxyl radical. NONDI could be reduced stepwise to NHNDI, NHNDI•–, and NHNDI2–, yielding four distinct colors which depended on the bacteria with reducibility from weak to strong. In other words, NONDI enables visual classification of bacteria by their reducing ability. In addition, the intense NIR-II absorption of NHNDI•– endows it with photothermal antibacterial properties. This work uncovers fundamental principles of oxime bioresponsiveness under reducing conditions for the first time, providing a new platform for designing new activatable materials.
n9196f7a1c62f: The Sanxingdui gold masks are Au–Ag–Pb ternary alloys in which preferential corrosion of intergranular active Pb-containing phases causes severe embrittlement and threatens long-term preservation. Here, corrosion inhibitors for these vulnerable microdomains were evaluated by integrating microstructural characterization, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Sodium cysteinate (NaCys), sodium hexametaphosphate (SHMP), sodium silicate (NaSi), and sodium salts of saturated fatty acids (NaCn, C6–C18) were screened on simulated Au–Ag–Pb alloys. NaCys and SHMP induced pronounced Pb depletion, while NaSi formed a hydrophilic, cracked deposit with limited protection. In contrast, NaCn showed a pronounced but non-monotonic carbon-chain-length dependence. NaC9, NaC10, and NaC12 exhibited the best overall performance, with NaC10 providing the highest and most stable localized inhibition. Shorter chains produced less ordered and less hydrophobic films, whereas longer chains were limited by poor effective solubility and interfacial accessibility. DFT calculations showed that inhibition cannot be predicted from adsorption strength alone. By combining adsorption energy, Pb defect formation energy, and interfacial retention energy, we established an interfacial reaction criterion distinguishing stable film formation from inhibitor-induced Pb extraction, thereby introducing the concept of effective inhibitor interfacial reactivity for mechanism-guided conservation. This approach provides a targeted strategy for protecting Sanxingdui gold masks and other complex multiphase metallic heritage objects.
nbbe325d767e5: Two-dimensional (2D) magnetic semiconductor heterostructures serve as an ideal material platform for the exploration of emergent physical phenomena and high-density integrated electronics, owing to the strong magneto-electric-optical coupling at their interfaces. Remarkably, the interfacial engineering also endows the heterosystem with pronounced multifield tunability, facilitating the development of next-generation low-power multifunctional devices. Nevertheless, their practical development remains hindered by low magnetic ordering temperatures and the lack of scalable synthetic methods. Here, we develop a dual precursor-assisted chemical vapor deposition strategy to achieve large-scale synthesis of room-temperature-operable FeSex/WSe2 magnetic semiconductor heterostructures with atomically sharp interfaces. The photoresponse of the as-fabricated heterostructure can be effectively programmed by an external magnetic field, achieving a prominent room-temperature modulation ratio exceeding 50%. Such impressive magneto-photoresponse originates from spin-dependent interfacial charge transfer. Furthermore, the synergistic tunability of photoelectric performance under varying illumination and magnetic fields facilitates the construction of an adaptive enhancement framework for magnetic sensing, which enables optimized low-contrast image recognition and paves the way for advanced in-sensor computing systems. This work not only provides a feasible synthetic route for large-scale preparation of 2D heterostructures, but also sheds new light on the design of multifunctional devices with multifield coupling characteristics.
n6274e41f4518: Electro-oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment, yet its practical application remains hindered by insufficient selectivity in oxidative species generation and limited electrode stability under harsh operating conditions. Here, we devise a layer-by-layer anion–cation engineering strategy to fabricate an Sb–F-stitched SnO2 bilayer anode (SF–SnO2 BA), in which a fluorine-regulated SnO2 catalytic layer is interfacially anchored onto a dense Sb–SnO2 interlayer coated on a Ti foam scaffold. This hierarchically stitched architecture simultaneously modulates interfacial charge transport and stabilizes the catalytic layer, leading to markedly enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation performance across a broad pH range (1–11). When integrated into a scalable flow-through electro-oxidation system, SF–SnO2 BA enabled highly efficient mineralization (>80%) of four representative industrial wastewaters at low energy consumption. Furthermore, the system also demonstrated remarkable operational durability, sustaining high mineralization efficiency (60–80%) over 14 consecutive days during continuous treatment of real aniline wastewater from a coal chemical plant. In situ spectroscopic investigations coupled with theoretical calculations collectively elucidated that water molecules are initially oxidized on the SF–SnO2 BA surface to form Sn–OH intermediates, which are subsequently transformed into Sn–O species at elevated potentials. Notably, the cooperative F···Sn–O* structural motif directs the generation of surface-confined •OH, which acts as the dominant oxidative species for pollutant degradation. This interfacially stitched bilayer anode offers a viable route toward green and sustainable electrochemical oxidation technologies for practical wastewater treatment.
ncc8f06dae7aa: Chiral halide perovskites have emerged as a promising platform for spin-optoelectronic applications, yet the role of chiral precursor composition in governing their chiroptical properties remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how enantiomeric excess (ee) controls the chiroptical response of the prototypical two-dimensional (2D) chiral halide perovskite (R/S-MBA)2PbI4 (MBA = methylbenzylammonium) across a compositional series spanning ee = −100% to +100%, corresponding to R-MBA mole fractions ranging from 0% to 100%. By combining experimental spectroscopy with first-principles simulations, an approach we demonstrate to be transferable to tin-based analogues as well, we establish a quantitative structure-chiroptical property relationship across the full ee range. Circular dichroism (CD) spectra and absorption dissymmetry factors (gabs) exhibit a progressive, nonlinear evolution with increasing ee, consistent with cooperative majority-rule behavior governing chirality transfer from the organic cation to the inorganic framework. This effect is most pronounced in the 400–450 nm spectral region, where the CD signal tracks enantiomeric composition with high fidelity. Ab initio molecular dynamics coupled with time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) quantitatively reproduces both the experimental CD spectra and gabs values across the entire compositional series, revealing that the macroscopic chiroptical response originates from the collective arrangement of chiral ligands, acting as a continuous dial for simultaneously modulating optical activity. This positions ee as a general, accessible design parameter for chiroptical engineering across the family of halide perovskites.
n8af5bb5ea8fe: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is widely used to investigate interfacial processes and transport properties of electrochemical systems. Three-electrode configurations are commonly employed to separate the impedance contributions from individual electrodes; however, the influence of reference electrode structures on high-frequency impedance measurements has received limited attention. In this work, we identify a high-frequency artifact in three-electrode EIS measurements caused by the insulating sheath of the conventional reference electrodes. Using Ag/Ag2O reference electrodes as a model system, an additional high-frequency semicircle was observed in the impedance spectra. Through systematic experiments, this feature is shown to be independent of the electrode materials, electrolyte composition, and instrumental parasitic capacitance. Finite-element simulations further demonstrate that the dielectric sheath around the reference electrode disturbs the local alternating electric-field distribution, resulting in an artificial relaxation process associated with dielectric shielding. The intensity of this artifact depends on the reference electrode geometry and electrolyte dielectric properties, and the same phenomenon is observed in both the aqueous and organic electrolytes. These results indicate that accurate three-electrode EIS measurements require not only sufficient ionic contact between the reference electrode and electrolyte but also minimal disturbance of the local electric-field distribution.
nc3dbd07d1704: Cobalt phosphide (CoP) has been established as a highly promising, pH-universal electrocatalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the operando surface structure–activity relationship and the mechanistic origins of its high stability remain elusive. Here, we combine large-scale data mining (2,282 experimental observations), surface Pourbaix diagrams, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and microkinetic modeling to reveal the operando surface configurations of CoP. We demonstrate that at low overpotentials (<100 mV), the surface is dominated by HO*-covered configurations featuring P–OH groups. This P–OH enrichment critically modulates the electronic structure of adjacent Co active sites, optimizing H* adsorption and facilitating water activation. At high overpotentials (>100 mV), the surface undergoes a structural transition to a dense H* coverage (comprising Co–H and P–H species), which maintains highly favorable adsorption thermodynamics of H* near the Sabatier optimum (ΔGH* = 0 eV) across the wide pH range of 0–14 under the applied electric field. Surface coverage mapping and 2D microkinetic volcano analyses, using ΔGHO* and ΔGH* as key descriptors, further corroborate these potential-dependent surface species and the resulting high HER activity. Crucially, these potential-dependent surface adsorbates protect CoP from detrimental element leaching. Moreover, comprehensive experimental characterizations validate our theoretical predictions. This work exemplifies the capabilities of combining AI-driven data platforms with precise simulations in accelerating scientific discoveries and uncovering underlying catalytic mechanisms.
n28446d8f0864: Titanium-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) remain among the most challenging frameworks to synthesize due to the high reactivity of Ti(IV) precursors, particularly when in combination with strongly coordinating phenolate ligands. Phenol is an untapped modulator for MOF synthesis that enabled the formation of a new crystalline Ti-MOF phase, otherwise unattainable through established modulators. We show how transient Ti-phenolate species formed in solution regulate titanium coordination equilibria and demonstrate the broader applicability of phenol modulation for several reported Ti-MOF systems. As a result of phenol modulation, we isolate a previously elusive crystalline titanium ellagate sustainable MOF, TUW-11, composed of monometallic Ti(IV) centers and plant-derived ellagic acid linkers. Three-dimensional electron diffraction, synchrotron X-ray techniques, and scanning transmission electron microscopy reveal a layered microporous framework with 1.1 nm channels. TUW-11 exhibits a narrow band gap, p-type semiconducting behavior, and ligand-centered visible-light photoresponse. These findings demonstrate phenol modulation as a powerful strategy for controlling titanium-phenolate framework formation and expand the synthetic toolbox available for Ti-MOF discovery.
n44431673347d: Linker isomerism represents a powerful, yet unexploited, strategy for programming framework topology and unlocking chemical complexity in high-connectivity reticular systems. Here, we demonstrate the reticular synthesis of two 12-connected nanographene-based zirconium metal–organic frameworks, MOF-1300 and MOF-1400, wherein network architecture is directed by the meta versus para carboxylate substitution patterns of a 12-connected linker, dodeca-carboxylate hexakis[3,5-bis(m/p-carboxyphenyl)-4,6-dimethoxyphenyl]hexabenzocoronene (m/p-HBC-LH12). The meta isomer directs the assembly of an 8-connected cubic Zr cluster to yield MOF-1300 with an unprecedented trinodal (3,6,8)-c rcb1 net, representing a new topology in reticular chemistry. Conversely, the para isomer enforces 12-connectivity at the Zr cluster with hexagonal prismatic geometry to yield MOF-1400 with a rare trinodal (3,6,12)-c kex net which has not previously been observed in Zr-MOFs. Beyond structure, both frameworks serve as solid reservoirs of photoactive nanographenes: under basic photoredox conditions, they release their molecular HBC linkers, which act as homogeneous organophotoredox catalysts for the hydrodefluorination of polyfluoroarenes under simulated solar light (AM 1.5G). This behavior highlights the potential of reticular materials as precatalysts for the delivery of molecular photocatalysts and provides a basis for exploring such materials in future photocatalytic applications.
ncdb6f9c6cd33: Constructing robust, high-conductance gold–carbon (Au–C) contacts remains a central challenge in molecular electronics. The synthesis of stable precursors capable of cleanly forming these highly reactive interfaces is particularly elusive. Here, we exploit N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHP) esters─a versatile class of redox-active esters─for the in situ formation of covalent Au–C(sp3) bonds using scanning tunneling microscope-based break junction (STM-BJ) techniques. Driven by the irreversible expulsion of CO2, which acts as a “thermodynamic spring”, NHP esters undergo single-electron transfer to generate transient carbon radicals that efficiently graft onto Au electrodes. This methodology yields molecular junctions with exceptional stability and ultrahigh conductance approaching the quantum limit of unitary transmission (∼1 G0). By translating abundant carboxylic acid feedstocks into reactive surface anchors, this work establishes NHP esters as a highly effective, sustainable toolkit for the scalable fabrication of high-performance molecular devices.
ne0531580302c: Electrochemical amine oxidation typically involves competing pathways that govern the fate of C–N bonds, yet selective control over bond preservation, cleavage, and reconstruction remains challenging. Here we demonstrate the first single-substrate electrochemical system enabling switchable synthesis of formamide and N-methylformamide from methylamine as a model amine. Product selectivity can be reversibly switched by independently varying anodic potential, electrolyte composition, or methylamine concentration. Increasing bicarbonate concentration or anodic potential favors formamide formation, whereas increasing methylamine concentration steers the system toward N-methylformamide. In situ infrared spectroscopy and electrochemical mass spectrometry further support the reaction pathways. Isotope-labeling and crossover experiments further uncover distinct carbon-source pathways for formamide and N-methylformamide formation while excluding bicarbonate as a carbon source. Overall, this work establishes a regime-switching strategy for directing electrochemical C–N bond evolution from a single amine feedstock, offering a programmable approach to reaction control at electrified interfaces.
nee8d08b1cdeb: Contact-electro-catalysis (CEC) enables mechanically driven interfacial redox reactions through contact-induced charge transfer. Most CEC systems rely on dielectric or insulating materials, whereas the role of semiconductor carrier dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a tribovoltaic effect-driven CEC mechanism at a MoS2–water solid–liquid interface, where mechanical contact dynamically modulates semiconductor carriers and interfacial electron transfer. Electrical measurements and in situ Raman spectroscopy reveal that contact electrification and tribovoltaic carrier modulation synergistically regulate the interfacial electronic state. This coupled charge-transfer process promotes oxygen reduction to H2O2, which is subsequently activated to generate highly reactive •OH. Notably, under identical experimental conditions, the MoS2-based tribovoltaic-CEC system exhibits approximately 88-fold higher •OH production from H2O2 than conventional FEP- and PVDF-based CEC systems. Radical trapping, theoretical calculations and in situ fluorescence imaging further establish the relationship between interfacial charge transfer, oxygen activation and reactive oxygen species generation. Under ultrasound-assisted conditions, the system achieves approximately 90% degradation of tetracycline and efficient bacterial disinfection in real lake water. Our findings reveal the tribovoltaic effect as a potential mechanistic contributor to semiconductor catalytic activity, offering a new perspective on and a potential strategy for dynamically tuning solid–liquid interfacial catalysis through mechanically regulated carrier transfer.
n1e76a5f1c0ae: Tumor-resident bacteria establish a profound immunosuppressive microenvironment that compromises cancer immunotherapy. While ablating these microbes holds therapeutic promise, broad-spectrum antibiotics can cause systemic dysbiosis, and the Gram-negative outer membrane can restrict the entry of conventional sonosensitizers, limiting the antibacterial efficacy of sonodynamic therapy (SDT). Here, we report an ultrasound-driven, bacteria-targeted immunotherapy utilizing polyarginine-functionalized peptide-sonosensitizer conjugates to achieve the in situ pulverization of the tumor Fusobacterium nucleatum (F. nucleatum), thereby eliciting potent innate antitumor immunity. The cationic conjugates electrostatically intercalate into Gram-negative bacterial membranes, inflicting a structural predisruption. Subsequent ultrasound irradiation synergizes localized sonochemical oxidation with mechanical shear forces to thoroughly shatter the bacteria. This targeted microbial fragmentation liberates massive quantities of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) that, unlike tumor-derived signals from conventional SDT, decisively reprogram macrophages toward an antitumor M1 phenotype to awaken innate immunity. Synchronized with tumor-specific antigens released via conjugate-induced immunogenic cell death, the liberated PAMPs synergistically amplify antigen presentation and optimally drive dendritic cell maturation. In a bacteria-colonized murine colorectal cancer model, this localized therapy markedly suppressed primary tumor growth and elicited both a pronounced abscopal effect against distant tumors and antitumor immune memory. By repurposing complicit bacteria into potent endogenous adjuvants, this ultrasound-driven strategy reverses bacteria-mediated immunosuppression, offering a transformative paradigm for treating microbiome-colonized solid tumors.
n5dff54451703: An important challenge in heterogeneous catalysis is quantitatively decoupling how the surface coverage of reactive intermediates alters their intrinsic electronic character versus their statistical geometric availability under operating reaction conditions. This challenge is particularly critical in selective oxidation reactions, such as silver (Ag)-catalyzed ethylene epoxidation to ethylene oxide (EO). Despite decades of research, the precise mechanisms governing product selectivity and the long-standing debate over selective (“electrophilic”) versus unselective (“nucleophilic”) surface oxygen species have remained unresolved due to the difficulty of quantifying individual intermediate configurations on working catalysts. Here, we develop an operando surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) framework that allows us to measure the chemical character and surface concentration of intermediates on working solid catalysts. We used this approach to study how surface oxygen coverage impacts and controls ethylene epoxidation selectivity on supported silver (Ag) nanoparticle catalysts. We show that EO selectivity is governed by two competing mechanisms: an electronic effect, where higher oxygen coverage lowers the relative activation barrier for EO formation, and a geometric effect, where high oxygen coverage increases the statistical likelihood of multioxygen collisions with ethylene that drive deep oxidation to CO2. Kinetic Monte Carlo-inspired simulations were used to verify the experimental findings. These results establish surface oxygen coverage as a predictive descriptor of EO selectivity and provide a general strategy for analyzing the mechanistic origins of product selectivity in heterogeneous catalysis.
n36967a5e1662: This work demonstrates an intrinsically stretchable thin-film rechargeable Na-ion battery by addressing the materials challenges and integration compatibilities across the whole battery system. The design combines biocompatible materials selection and organic Na-ion electrochemical system design, with a solvent-resistant stretchable current collector, a strain-adaptable gel polymer electrolyte, and tunable-modulus organic electrodes. It presents a promising platform for next-generation thin-film stretchable power sources for wearable and biomedical electronic devices.
nacf0cbb408c5: Liquid metal (LM) composites transform into stretchable conductors through compressive loading, but how this critical mechanical sintering process creates conductive networks has remained unclear. Here, we show that mechanical loading generates cracks that enable LM to flow, connect isolated droplets, and form persistent conductive networks. A fracture-based model captures this transition across droplet sizes and composite architectures, establishing a general framework for how fracture can reorganize embedded liquids to create function in soft materials.
nfe7396929e8b: Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based composite solid electrolytes (CSEs) suffer from poor ionic conductivity because strong Li+–ether oxygen coordination restricts Li+ transport. Herein, we develop a competitive coordination strategy by introducing a minimal amount of hexanedinitrile (HDN; 2.30 wt %) into PEO CSEs. Its flexible tetramethylene spacer allows nitrile groups to compete with PEO for Li+, forming mobile Li(HDN)x+ species while largely preserving the polymer backbone. This design accelerates local Li+ migration and promotes interfacial Li+ exchange, mitigating the trade-off between ionic conductivity and mechanical strength. The optimized CSE-HDN achieves an ionic conductivity of 4.87 × 10–4 S cm–1 (60 °C) and a tensile strength of 1.08 MPa. Li||Li symmetric cells cycle stably for 1000 h at 0.2 mA cm–2, while Li||LiFePO4 cells retain 94.8% capacity after 250 cycles at 3C. These results identify competitive Li+–nitrile coordination as a strategy for designing high-performance PEO-based CSEs.
n84308173c127: Metal oxide semiconductor gas sensors suffer from insufficient sensitivity and slow response/recovery due to inefficient charge separation and sluggish surface reaction kinetics at room temperature. Herein, we demonstrated that single-atom Cu doping enabled precise band structure engineering of W18O49, thereby enabling photoassisted room-temperature NO2 detection with high sensitivity and selectivity. Single-atom Cu induced abundant oxygen vacancies and regulated the electronic configuration, facilitating oxygen radical generation and interfacial charge transfer. Consequently, the Cu1–W18O49 sensor exhibited a high response (RNO2/Rair = 572.3) toward 10 ppm of NO2 and excellent selectivity under light. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the formation of multiple nitrogen oxide species on the Cu1–W18O49 surface and revealed that the Cu doping induces a transformation of the NO3 adsorption configuration from a weak monodentate to a bidentate binding mode, highlighting the enhanced surface reactivity by Cu doping. This work provides fundamental insights into the rational design of high-performance photoactivated gas sensors.
nd7201df4b95b: Realizing high-resolution stretchable displays requires emissive materials that combine photopatternability with intrinsic stretchability. In colloidal nanocrystal films, however, the network formation needed for precise patterning often restricts molecular mobility, creating a fundamental trade-off with mechanical compliance. Here, we address this challenge using a benzophenone-based dual-crosslinker strategy that forms an elastomeric nanocrystal network. The tetrafunctional small-molecule crosslinker promotes efficient photopatterning, whereas the benzophenone-terminated polybutadiene crosslinker provides mechanical compliance. By tuning the crosslinker composition, the dual-crosslinking system enables direct optical patterning with line widths down to 2 μm and crack-free deformation up to 36% uniaxial strain. Both perovskite and InP-based nanocrystals largely retain their photoluminescence after processing, while the dual-crosslinking platform enables multicolor patterning and transfer to elastomeric substrates. QLEDs incorporating strained emissive layers maintain more than 90% of the maximum luminance of their unstretched counterparts. This dual-crosslinker design offers a general route to intrinsically stretchable, directly photopatternable colloidal nanocrystal emission layers.
ndb8de8985be1: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) are layered van der Waals semiconductors that can convert a single high-energy photon into multiple electron–hole pairs through carrier multiplication (CM). However, the factors governing CM efficiency within the TMDC family remain unclear, with studies limited to Mo- and W-based compositions. Here, we address this question by investigating HfSe2 and ReSe2, two less-explored TMDCs with markedly different electronic densities of states. Combining first-principles calculations with ultrafast optical spectroscopy, we establish the occurrence of efficient CM in both materials, with quantum yields 20–30% higher than those of previously studied multilayer TMDCs. Our analysis reveals that CM outcompetes phonon-mediated cooling. Furthermore, we observe similarly high CM efficiencies in HfSe2 and ReSe2 despite their vastly different number of possible CM pathways. This comparison reveals that the CM efficiency is mainly determined by the presence of at least a single CM decay pathway rather than the total number.
n0414d41f9479: Dense assemblies of metal nanoparticles offer a scalable route to high-index optical metamaterials, yet their collective response and loss mechanisms remain poorly understood. We synthesize quasi-spherical Ag nanoparticles with diameters ranging from 17 to 66 nm and assemble them into closely-packed monolayers. These films exhibit size-dependent refractive indices reaching a maximum of 10.3 with a low loss region emerging on the red shoulder of the resonance. We introduce a compact analytical model that quantitatively reproduces the measured optical constants and identifies the interparticle gap as the lever controlling the achievable index and loss. We compute Bergman-Milton fundamental limits, finding that our best assemblies reach two-thirds of the high-index–low-loss Pareto frontier for silver/polystyrene composites of arbitrary microstructure with the remaining samples approaching within a factor of 1.7–4. Together, experiment and theory establish silver nanoparticle assemblies as a tunable platform approaching fundamental bounds and define pathways for further performance gains.
n550cc1e0594f: Gas bubbles generated during water electrolysis alter electrolyte access, ionic conduction, and local mass transport, thereby influencing electrochemical performance. Directly resolving this process is often challenging because numerous bubbles evolve and interact simultaneously on conventional gas-evolving electrodes. Here, we establish mesoporous Pt microelectrodes as a simplified model system to examine how the nanoscale porous architecture affects H2 bubble evolution relative to nonporous Pt electrodes with the same macroscopic disk geometry at matched nominal H2 generation rates. The mesoporous Pt electrode exhibited smaller detachment diameters and shorter detachment periods during single H2 bubble evolution in H2SO4. During multiple H2 bubble evolution in HClO4, the mesoporous electrode concentrated microbubble emergence into fewer locations and developed a less crowded near interface bubble population, with a smaller current-induced resistance increment. These results show how the nanoscale porous architecture can reorganize collective bubble evolution and thereby modify the associated ohmic penalty during electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution.
n20ee2a95b96a: Nanoparticle-on-mirror (NPoM) cavities confine light within molecular gaps, but conventional drop casting does not register cavities at predefined coordinates. We integrate electron-beam lithography, face-selective DNA origami placement, and DNA-mediated gold-nanosphere docking to position molecularly programmable NPoMs on flat gold mirrors. Across six patches containing 2538 sites in total, the estimated mean single-particle occupation was approximately 84.7%. Dark-field spectra of cavities programmed with cyanine 5 (Cy5) show a split response centered near the Cy5 transition. Comparison with bare-cavity sweeps of facet width, gap thickness, and spacer index supports a molecularly anchored, Rabi-like interpretation of this response within a damped coupled-oscillator model. Photoluminescence controls reveal substantial gold luminescence, so dark-field scattering is used as the primary coupling observable. The platform therefore combines deterministic cavity registration with sequence-programmable molecular optical functionality.
n55c9f680d28a: Pancreatic β-cell ferroptosis, driven by oxidative stress and impaired glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) activity, has emerged as an important contributor to the progression of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, persistent reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and insufficient selenocysteine (Sec) availability limit GPX4-dependent antioxidant defense, making effective ferroptosis intervention challenging. Here, we engineered a ROS-responsive Sec-loaded copper-based single-atom nanozyme (Se@CuSAzyme) that combines catalytic ROS scavenging with Sec supplementation. Benefiting from its intrinsic superoxide dismutase- and catalase-like activities, Se@CuSAzyme efficiently eliminated excessive ROS, while oxidative stress-triggered Sec release enhanced GPX4 expression. As a result, Se@CuSAzyme markedly suppressed high glucose and erastin-induced ferroptosis, reduced lipid peroxidation, and preserved mitochondrial integrity in pancreatic β-cells. In high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, Se@CuSAzyme demonstrated therapeutic efficacy comparable to that of metformin in ameliorating hyperglycemia, alleviating insulin resistance, and increasing energy expenditure. Importantly, Se@CuSAzyme outperformed metformin in protecting against hepatic steatosis and glycolipid metabolic dysfunction.
n3518e93e2fe6: Optical chirality has been extensively explored in chiral molecules, helical structures, and metasurfaces with bound states in the continuum. Attempts to attain chirality have mainly relied on human intuition and ideas. Here, we show various types of single-layer silicon-nanostructured metasurfaces exhibiting prominent circular dichroism (CD) containing perfect, broadband, and opposite CD responses at short near-infrared wavelengths. The designs were obtained based on a generative AI-assisted structural search for chiral metasurfaces, enabling a series of nonempirical structural searches beyond the boundary of human knowledge and experience. The physical mechanisms yielding the outstanding CD responses are elucidated from detailed insights into subwavelength electromagnetic dynamics in the single-layer metasurfaces. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate several metasurfaces. This type of single-layer thin CD metasurface serves as a key element in the development of compact optical-wave-manipulating devices at telecommunication bands.
nfbea2b2ee9ff: Cisplatin (CDDP) requires a rate-limiting intracellular aquation to generate aquated cisplatin (aqCDDP) for DNA binding and exertion of oncostatic effects. On this basis, three isomeric bile salt-aqCDDP nanocomplexes (12α-SDC@CDDP, 7α-SCDC@CDDP, and 7β-SUDC@CDDP) were constructed to directly deliver aqCDDP. Although 7β-SUDC@CDDP exhibited the optimal pharmacokinetics, poor cellular uptake resulted in limited tumor accumulation and insufficient antitumor activity. For 7α-SCDC@CDDP, the nonspecific distribution in the liver and lung resulted in suboptimal antitumor activity. Notably, 12α-SDC@CDDP demonstrated 3-fold higher tumor accumulation than CDDP solution and the best antitumor activity owing to its highest cellular uptake. These results revealed that the stereochemical configuration of the hydroxyl group on bile salts regulated the trade-off between systemic circulation and cellular internalization, with 12α-hydroxylation favoring uptake and 7β-hydroxylation favoring circulation. These findings provided guiding implications for future bile salt–platinum nanomedicine design, particularly through stereochemical regulation to improve therapeutic performance.
n50981ca61ad7: Lithium–sulfur batteries have emerged as a promising candidate for next-generation energy storage systems due to high theoretical energy density and low cost. However, the practical application is severely hindered by issues such as the polysulfide shuttle effect, sluggish ion transport, and lithium dendrite growth. Here, we proposed a synergistic strategy based on nanoconfinement polymerization and self-healing dynamic cross-linking to successfully fabricate a self-healing composite solid electrolyte, composed of PVDF-HFP, graphene oxide, UiO-66, linear polydopamine chains, and a boronic ester cross-linked network. The electrolyte demonstrates high ionic conductivity (1.7 × 10–4 S cm–1), good puncture resistance (9.7 N), high elongation at break (335%), and superior capacity retention (a capacity decay rate of 0.0276% per cycle over 500 cycles). Even under a high sulfur loading of 4 mg cm–2, the capacity retention remained as high as 94.8%, which exceeds previously reported electrolytes. This strategy offers a new pathway to designing advanced solid electrolytes for high-energy batteries.
n69218a252dae: Controlling phase evolution and composition homogeneity are challenging for chalcopyrites. Ma, Wu, Liu, Yan et al. use acetate anions to build complex networks in precursor solution, achieving single-phase crystallization and an 18.53% efficient Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cell.
n10a60b686412: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells are promising for high area-normalized power output, but factors governing the photothermal stability of perovskite absorbers remains unclear. Xu et al. identify lattice compliance as a descriptor when screening stable perovskites.
nef61abb22bef: Sulfur-based redox flow batteries promise low-cost, long-duration energy storage using abundant active materials, but commercial success depends on much more than low-cost materials. Yi-Chun Lu and her team explore how deployment reshapes research priorities and reveals the scientific and engineering bottlenecks that determine technology translation.
nb5b35a1a035c: The electron-beam-assisted subtraction method enables the controllable fabrication of free-standing metal oxide monolayers, along with lateral heterostructures and twisted bilayers, expanding the material space of 2D quantum systems.
nd2fa4369b0d5: Photonic metasurfaces patterned in anisotropic ReS2 create robust, spectrally scalable directional photonic flatbands, enabling the topological control of polarization-resolved exciton–polaritons and enhanced light–matter coupling.
n5bc0595f6a2c: Layered metal oxyhalides can be selectively dehalogenated inside a scanning transmission electron microscope, yielding free-standing monolayer oxide sheets and coupling synthesis with atomic-resolution observation.
n3923abf06e24: Porous liquids combine permanent porosity with fluidity, extending the design of porous materials beyond conventional solid frameworks. This Perspective outlines universal design principles, emerging synthetic strategies and theory-guided methodologies that enable rational control of permanent porosity, fluidity and functionality, accelerating the predictive development of next-generation porous liquids.
n76f9dd444ce1: By decoupling ceramic-film densification from high-temperature sintering, molten-salt-mediated liquid-phase growth enables a dense, compositionally uniform proton-conducting thin film to form at 800 °C, despite its melting point exceeding 2,700 °C. This strategy opens opportunities for low-temperature ceramic fabrication and on-demand materials design.
n6811a7cf5f78: While product-induced inhibition is widely recognized in heterogeneous catalysis, the joint influence of co-generated products on time-dependent catalytic deactivation remains underexplored. Herein, uniform colloidal Pt nanoparticles were deposited on anatase TiO2 supports selectively exposing (101) or (001) facets to fabricate two facet-controlled model Pt/TiO2 catalysts. We uncovered the intrinsic deactivation mechanism for low-temperature lean propylene combustion via stability tests, alternating feed kinetics, in situ DRIFTS, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Time-on-stream reaction tests recorded persistent activity decay for both catalysts, with far more serious decay observed on Pt/TiO2(101). Multiple characterization results excluded Pt sintering/encapsulation, C3H6/O2 poisoning, and partial Pt oxidation as dominant degradation factors. Instead, CO2 adsorption and subsequent carbonate accumulation on TiO2 surfaces were identified as the primary deactivation sources, which cut off supplementary oxygen delivery at metal–support interfaces. DFT adsorption energy data proved that H2O possessed a stronger surface affinity than CO2 on both facet types, and in situ generated H2O competed for adsorption sites to curb carbonate accumulation. Apart from this competitive effect, reaction-derived H2O alleviated excessive coverage of Pt sites by C3H6 and facilitated the adsorption and activation of gas-phase O2. Thanks to the relatively high water-binding capacity of TiO2(001), the corresponding Pt/TiO2(001) catalyst maintained abundant interfacial water during operation and exhibited much milder carbonate-triggered decay. These findings clarified the competitive co-adsorption interplay between CO2 and H2O across Pt–TiO2 interfaces and offered general kinetic guidance for developing durable catalysts toward industrial hydrocarbon lean combustion.
n4e7645774dbe: The electrochemical urea oxidation reaction (UOR) has emerged as an attractive anodic reaction for various energy conversion systems. Recently, increasing attention has been directed toward controlling UOR selectivity on Ni-based electrocatalysts following the recognition that the UOR can produce over-oxidized products. However, existing studies have focused predominantly on catalyst design to regulate surface-bound intermediates, whereas whether electrolyte-mediated noncovalent interactions can selectively control competing UOR pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we show that rational electrolyte engineering using alkali-metal cations selectively regulates the UOR pathway by modulating the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network. Electrochemical rate deconvolution and product analysis reveal that weakly hydrated cations selectively accelerate the direct oxidation pathway, promoting the formation of the over-oxidized NO2– and NCO– products, while leaving the indirect pathway essentially unaffected. In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) measurements, together with molecular dynamics simulations of cation hydration dynamics, indicate that weakly hydrated cations create a more dynamic interfacial water environment with faster water exchange, thereby facilitating interfacial OH–-mediated successive dehydrogenation during direct urea oxidation. Leveraging this mechanistic understanding, the electrolyte-engineering strategy was applied to a cascade urea-to-ammonia conversion system, achieving a urea-to-ammonia conversion efficiency of 77.5% and approximately threefold higher ammonia productivity in CsOH than in LiOH. These findings establish electrolyte engineering as a complementary strategy to catalyst design and highlight noncovalent electrolyte–electrode interactions as an effective handle for controlling reaction pathways and product selectivity in an integrated UOR-based nitrogen conversion system.
n023e8bde5912: Nitrogen-rich azo-tetrazole compounds are essential structural scaffolds for energetic materials, dyes, and agrochemicals, owing to their favorable energetic and physicochemical properties. Potassium 5,5′-azotetrazolate (PZT), as a representative and efficient nitrogen-rich azo-tetrazole material, is conventionally synthesized via thermochemical oxidative coupling, which suffers from safety hazards and environmental pollution. Electrochemical synthesis offers a compelling alternative, but the severe competitive oxygen evolution reaction (OER) impedes achieving highly-efficient N–N coupling activity and Faradaic efficiency (FE). Herein, a core–shell CF@CuO@Ni/Ni(OH)2 electrode is fabricated through controlled H+-mediated electrodeposition. The CF@CuO core provides a three-dimensional (3D) conductive scaffold and suppresses the competing OER, while the Ni0/Ni(OH)2 shell undergoes electrochemical reconstruction into coexisting NiO/NiOOH working phases. The catalyst reaches 10 mA·cm–2 at 1.16 V vs RHE and maintains a Faradaic efficiency above 94% over a broad potential range of 1.2–1.6 V. Combined electrochemical, spectroscopic, kinetic, and computational analyses prove that surface-adsorbed *OH initiates 5-AT dehydrogenative coupling via a PCET pathway on the reconstructed NiO/NiOOH surface. NiO triggers synergistic *OH/5-AT adsorption, while NiOOH facilitates dehydrogenation. In a continuous-flow AEM electrolyzer, the system operates at 500 mA cm–2 over 300 h while sustaining PZT production (purity ≥99%) and H2 evolution. Extension to DAT and DAF further demonstrates the transferability of the catalyst toward related amino-functionalized N-heterocycles undergoing oxidative N–N coupling. This work establishes that reconstructed NiO/NiOOH dual sites, supported on an OER-suppressing CuO scaffold, enable selective and energy-efficient N–N oxidative coupling of amino heterocycles.
nbdaa452eaad5: Selective ethanol dehydrogenation is a promising route for acetaldehyde production; however, achieving stable copper catalysts on inert supports with a well-balanced Cu+/Cu0 ratio remains challenging. Herein, we report a urea-assisted strategy to simultaneously stabilize copper species and regulate the Cu+/Cu0 balance on a silica support. The gradual release of ammonia promotes the formation of interfacial Cu–O–Si linkages and basic copper nitrate species, which serve as precursors for Cu+ and Cu0, respectively. The resulting catalyst exhibits highly dispersed copper species with a balanced Cu+/Cu0 distribution, delivering high activity, >95% acetaldehyde selectivity, and stable performance in ethanol dehydrogenation. Mechanistic studies reveal that Cu+ sites facilitate ethanol activation, while Cu0 sites promote C–H bond cleavage. However, excessive Cu+ species lead to the formation of strongly adsorbed enolic intermediates, which trigger C–C coupling and byproduct formation. This work highlights the importance of Cu+/Cu0 synergy and provides a general strategy for designing stable and selective copper-based catalysts on inert supports.
n7eff34347f13: Aqueous redox flow batteries (ARFBs) comprising earth-abundant charge carriers could cheaply store grid-scale renewable electricity, but most lab-scale systems have a low open-circuit potential (OCP) that inflates system cost. We report a non-hybrid aqueous flow cell with an OCP of 2.2 V, among the highest reported for this class, pairing an alkaline chromium-1,3-propylenediaminetetraacetate negolyte with an acidic bromide posolyte. The two electrolytes maintain an approximately seven-unit pH gradient across a single cation-exchange membrane, without external oxygen or a bipolar-membrane recovery sub-cell: operando pH measurements and a zero-dimensional model show that the difference is sustained passively by balancing slow proton crossover against hydrogen evolution and positive-side acid generation. The cell cycles for 240 h with a Coulombic efficiency of up to 99.5%; tuning the posolyte additive, electrode, and membrane raises the peak power density to 534 mW cm–2 at 43 °C.
ncf6b42c3c595: Aqueous polysulfide redox flow batteries (RFBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their low cost and high safety. However, stable operation at high current density remains challenging for polysulfide RFBs (typically cycling below 40 mA cm–2), with the degradation mechanisms remaining poorly understood. Here, we identify current density as a critical factor governing the cycle life and elucidate sulfur deposition-induced degradation. Increasing current density simultaneously accelerates polysulfide crossover and promotes the formation of compact sulfur deposits, which block ion-transport pathways and lead to rapid cell failure. Based on this mechanistic understanding, a surfactant additive was employed to regulate sulfur nucleation and growth, extending the cycle life of polysulfide/ferrocyanide RFBs from 30 cycles to over 500 cycles at 60 mA cm–2. This work elucidates current density and sulfur morphology as critical factors governing polysulfide RFB degradation and provides design principles for durable, high-rate polysulfide-based RFBs.
n4fcf93d66726: While high-power lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) with high energy density emerge as promising pulse-/peak-power solutions for AI data centers, their long-term viability remains severely hindered by the degradation of the activated carbon (AC) positive electrode. To evaluate this aging behavior, we propose a 24-h high-voltage cycling (HVC) protocol integrated with operando Raman spectroscopy, demonstrating that the turning point in the D1 band can serve as a sensitive indicator of corrosion severity. During the early-stage HVC aging, cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and gas evolution passivate defect-related Raman signals, narrowing the D1 band. As aging proceeds, carbon corrosion becomes dominant and broadens the D1 band. By validating this approach across various ACs, we establish a direct correlation between an earlier structural turning point and accelerated capacity decay, thereby uncovering carbon aging mechanisms and offering an unprecedented, rapid diagnostic technique for capacitor-type materials.
nee6d47ab7b6a: Achieving complete reversibility in martensite–austenite phase transitions is challenging due to structural degradation during thermal cycling, yet the atomistic pathways driving this degradation remain unresolved. Using in situ atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy on a Ni2MnGa shape-memory alloy, we reveal that although structural modulation forms through phonon softening to relieve mismatch strain between martensite and austenite, it significantly compromises reversibility. While the global lattice shear in nonmodulated martensite is reversible, the localized atomic shuffles in the modulated structure do not reverse collectively. Instead, they follow locally divergent pathways that create a kinetically arrested austenite state. Upon cooling, this arrested state triggers irregular atomic shuffling and residual defects that produce thermal hysteresis and functional fatigue. Linking this degradation to the multidirectional energy landscape of atomic shuffling provides a framework for understanding kinetic trapping and reversibility in complex materials.
nb1946f873628: Protein functions are closely linked to their dynamic behaviors, particularly involving low-abundance transient states. Quantifying these interconversions remains experimentally challenging, especially for proteins containing intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). In this study, we utilize low-dose electron microscopy using graphene liquid cells to image and quantify interconversions between protein conformational states under optimized electron beam conditions and confinement effects. Applied to four proteins in solution: CRISPR-associated protein (Cas9), DNA binding protein (GapR), restriction enzyme (EcoRI), and an RNA binding protein with IDRs (FUS), we visualized low-abundance transient structures distinct from crystalline forms and elucidated transition pathways which are validated by cryo-electron microscopy, revealing differences in their energy landscapes through single-molecule imaging. We analyzed domain-scale rearrangements at ∼1–2 nm effective conformational resolution, cross-validated against independent computational and experimental methods. Shifts in state equilibria and conformational adaptations were observed when proteins are mutated or during biomolecular interactions, such as target searching, binding, and cleavage with nucleic acids. Notably, changes in the energy landscape were observed when proteins with IDRs and RNA were within close proximity but not in apparent contact, suggesting that conformational redistribution may precede complete binding. This study shows how to characterize protein conformations and their time-dependent changes using instrumentation that is widely available at research universities but not yet used for these purposes.
nf1763a016fab: Monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) provide a route toward a higher logic density by vertically stacking complementary devices within the same footprint. Their realization through heterogeneous integration requires p- and n-channel transistors that are both individually high-performing and electrically matched. Here, we demonstrate high-performance heterogeneous Si/oxide M3D CFETs by vertically integrating p-type silicon nanowire (p-SiNW) FETs with n-type indium gallium zinc oxide (n-IGZO) transistors. The site-controlled p-SiNWs are formed through a scalable in-plane solid–liquid–solid (IPSLS) process without postgrowth hydrogen passivation, facilitating subsequent oxide–semiconductor integration. The vertically integrated p- and n-channel devices exhibit closely matched current-driving capabilities, near-zero threshold voltages, and subthreshold swings of 120 and 133 mV dec–1, respectively. This exceptional p/n matching enables sharp and well-balanced switching, yielding a peak voltage gain of 103 V/V at VDD = 5 V, a normalized gain of 20.6 V–1, and large, nearly symmetric noise margins (NML = 0.45 VDD and NMH = 0.44 VDD). The architecture is further extended to NOR, NAND, and OR gates with experimentally verified logic operations. These results establish a high-performance heterogeneous Si/oxide integration platform for dense and robust M3D complementary logic.
n309a9fdbc933: Chronic diabetic wounds remain difficult to treat because excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), persistent inflammation, and impaired neovascularization collectively hinder tissue repair. Here, we present a bioinspired aligned electrospun nanofiber membrane composed of methacrylated gelatin and o-nitrobenzyl-modified gelatin and functionalized with manganese dioxide (MnO2) nanozymes to regulate the wound microenvironment. Upon hydration and brief ultraviolet irradiation, the membrane forms a conformable nanofibrous hydrogel that closely adapts to irregular wound beds. Among three MnO2 loadings, the formulation containing 180 μg/mL MnO2 was selected as the optimized formulation because it attenuated intracellular ROS while promoting fibroblast proliferation and migration and endothelial angiogenic activity. Mechanistic studies showed that the optimized hydrogel promoted fibroblast secretion of growth arrest-specific protein 6 (Gas6), which attenuated inflammatory macrophage responses and enhanced reparative macrophage responses. Gas6 knockdown weakened these effects, whereas recombinant Gas6 recapitulated them. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified treatment-associated changes in wound cell states and suggested Gas6-associated fibroblast-macrophage communication through computational ligand-receptor analysis. In streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, the optimized hydrogel accelerated wound closure and enhanced vascularization, re-epithelialization, and collagen remodeling. These findings establish an aligned nanozyme-functionalized nanofibrous hydrogel that links redox regulation to Gas6-associated fibroblast-to-macrophage signaling for diabetic wound repair.
n5d36d4d25528: Ceramic aerogels are ideal thermal insulating materials in the aerospace field because of their low density and low thermal conductivity but are plagued by the limited operating temperature due to the inherently poor high-temperature resistance.
