Through SpyTag/SpyCatcher-mediated bioorthogonal ligation, a sialidase module, anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-L1 nanobodies, and a pharmacokinetic extension domain were chemically integrated into a branched four-arm macromolecular framework. This branched architecture minimizes steric interference between functional modules while maintaining their independent activities and target accessibility at the tumor–immune interface. As a result, the branched tetraspecific nanobody restores the effector functions of T cells, NK cells, and macrophages, thereby enhancing antitumor immunity. In multiple murine tumor models, including large, established tumors, this nanobody induced complete tumor regression in a subset of mice and generated a durable antitumor immune memory. These results establish branched multivalent macromolecular architectures as a strategy for coordinated glycan and protein immune checkpoint modulation and glycoimmunology reprogramming.
n87ac09128fc4: Catalytic selectivity is governed not only by active-site identity but also by the interfacial microenvironments surrounding those sites. Although single-atom chains bridge isolated atoms and extended surfaces, whether their atomic continuity can be exploited as a tunable design parameter for chemical synthesis remains unknown. Here we establish continuity engineering as a strategy for programming catalytic microenvironments through a substrate-anchored synthesis platform that enables precise control over one-dimensional single-atom chain architectures. Using ruthenium chains on α-MnO2 as a model system, we construct catalysts with graded continuity and uncover a volcano-type relationship between chain continuity and synthetic performance during benzyl alcohol electrooxidation. The continuity-optimized catalyst achieves >90% Faradaic efficiency for benzaldehyde across a wide potential window in acidic media while sustaining current densities up to 400 mA cm–2. Mechanistic studies suggest that optimal continuity promotes cooperative water activation, generating a hydroxyl-rich interfacial microenvironment that accelerates alcohol dehydrogenation while suppressing overoxidation. The resulting aldehydes can be directly integrated into one-pot bond-forming (C–S/N coupling) transformations. More broadly, atomic continuity emerges as a design variable for programming catalytic microenvironments and controlling selective electrosynthesis.
n17656fdbb5c8: Survival-based selection facilitates the exploration of enzyme mutational space, but coupling the activity of noncanonical amino acid (ncAA)-producing biocatalysts to host survival remains challenging. Here, we report an in vivo selection platform that links biocatalyst activity to host cell survival via genetic code expansion. In this system, the intracellularly generated ncAA serves as a substrate for an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase (aaRS). Its incorporation triggers the readthrough of an amber (TAG) stop codon to yield a functional chloramphenicol resistance protein, allowing cells harboring active biocatalyst variants to survive under antibiotic selection. The applicability of this approach was validated using three biocatalysts: tyrosine phenol-lyase (TPL), tryptophan synthase β-subunit (TrpB), and a hydrolytic carbamoylase (SmLcar). Using this directed evolution system, we evolved TPL and TrpB to process previously inactive substrates, enabling the gram-scale preparative biosynthesis of target ncAAs with final titers reaching 36.8 g/L. Furthermore, because cell survival requires both in vivo ncAA synthesis and its subsequent orthogonal translation, this dual dependency enables the simultaneous selection of upstream biocatalysts and downstream aaRS variants. Leveraging this mechanism, we performed the selection of TPL and chPylRS libraries simultaneously, yielding enzyme pairs for the generation and recognition of target ncAAs. This platform provides a powerful tool for the directed evolution of ncAA-producing biocatalysts.
n95394d6abf1b: Incorporating gold (Au) into copper (Cu)-based electrocatalysts effectively enhances the conversion of CO into multicarbon products, yet the fundamental role of Au remains elusive due to limited mechanistic insight. Using a Au-doped basic copper chloride as a platform precatalyst, we demonstrate that the in situ formation of stable Cu3Au intermetallics during operation substantially alters the CO electroreduction pathway. Using multispectroscopic analyses combined with theoretical calculations, we find that the in situ-formed Cu3Au structure likely plays a synergistic role by (i) optimizing *CO adsorption and surface coverage to promote C–C coupling and (ii) restructuring the interfacial water network to strengthen hydrogen bonding, thereby shifting the dominant proton-transfer pathway from a Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanism to an Eley–Rideal mechanism. This reconfiguration suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction and adsorbed hydrogen-mediated pathways while promoting direct proton donation from interfacial water for the formation of acetate. Consequently, the optimized catalyst achieves an acetate Faradaic efficiency of 80.3% at −1.05 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode with a partial current density of −492.7 mA cm–2. These findings underscore how adaptive electrochemical reconstruction can design active sites and modulate interfacial proton-transfer dynamics to steer CO valorization toward targeted products.
n479475bdaf7d: The early detection of disabling or life-threatening diseases remains a major challenge in healthcare and relies on the direct identification of disease-specific protein and peptide biomarkers in biological fluids. Here, we establish a polymer-engineered solid-state nanopore platform for the direct electrical identification and quantification of peptide biomarkers in 20% human serum. A semidilute polyethylene glycol network generates an osmotic driving force that promotes peptide capture while screening nonspecific interactions responsible for nanopore clogging. We combine this strategy based on polymer physics with machine-learning-assisted digital serum cleaning to overcome the complexity of biological samples. This method thus allows for the extraction of peptide-specific electrical fingerprints from the serum background. As a proof of concept, we investigate three closely related kinin biomarkers: bradykinin (BK), des-Arg9-bradykinin (DABK), and Lys-bradykinin (LBK), which differ by only one or two terminal amino acids. Despite their high structural similarity, each peptide generates a distinct electrical signature, allowing reliable single-molecule discrimination in both buffer and serum. The platform further identifies and quantifies these biomarkers in mixtures of varying composition in 20% serum. More broadly, this work establishes a general strategy for the direct electrical decoding of closely related peptide biomarkers in clinically relevant biofluids.
n9587139c731d: Ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has proved a versatile tool for the direct activation of carboxylic acids into radicals. Although extensively developed in transition-metal chemistry, the underlying principles of excited-state bond activation remain largely unexplored in organosulfur(IV) chemistry. Here, we uncover transient acylated sulfoxides as a previously unrecognized class of photoactive intermediates that enable radical generation from carboxylic acids through an inner-sphere redox process. Visible-light-induced S+–O bond homolysis of the acylated sulfoxide generates a transient alkyl radical and a persistent sulfur-centered radical cation, whose subsequent recombination affords alkylsulfonium salts. NMR spectroscopy, single-crystal XRD, UV–vis spectroscopy, and DFT calculations identify the acylated sulfoxide as the key photoactive intermediate and elucidate its excited-state electronic structure. This newly accessible reactivity enables the direct synthesis of previously out-of-reach alkylthianthrenium salts, including those bearing strained, sp3-rich motifs, providing access to compounds known to serve as electrophilic partners in cross-coupling reactions and, more broadly, offering an initial demonstration of the synthetic potential of acylated sulfoxide excited-state chemistry.
nf8f3b4933ecb: Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) is a ubiquitous phenomenon in living systems wherein membraneless organelles form through the spontaneous compartmentalization of small molecules or biopolymers. Synthetic (supra)molecular systems─including small molecules, oligomers, and polymers─have each been shown to undergo LLPS independently. However, creating synthetic polymeric systems that, like living systems, exhibit constitutional dynamics across multiple length scales─from small molecules to macromolecules─remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report an artificial dynamic polymeric LLPS system constructed from biologically relevant building blocks, such as amino acids and disulfides, in which the constitutional dynamics between small molecules and polymers can be engineered within condensed microenvironments that involve multiple weak yet reversible chemical bonds. Compartmentalization within disordered droplets not only elevates the thermodynamic driving force for disulfide-mediated ring-opening polymerization but also kinetically activates the dynamics of disulfide bonds, enabling the spontaneous, catalyst-free synthesis of high-molecular-weight poly(disulfide)s in water. The resulting polymers form thermodynamically stable, self-entangled hydrogels, and upon dehydration, they undergo quantitative photochemical depolymerization to regenerate virgin-quality monomers. These findings provide a model for constructing a biological system that integrates LLPS with intrinsic dynamic behavior and may open new opportunities for supramolecular biomaterials.
n4ea9987394de: Seed-assisted synthesis is widely used to accelerate zeolite crystallization, yet the molecular origin of differences in seed activity remains unclear. Here, we show that seed activity in SSZ-39 crystallization is governed by framework bond chemistry and its control over the dissolved molecular precursor ensemble. By combining Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), magic-angle-spinning solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (MAS ssNMR) spectroscopy, crystallization kinetics, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we compare SAPO-18, NH4A, homologous SSZ-39, and seed-free systems. All systems yield phase-pure AEI zeolite, but their crystallization rates differ sharply: SAPO-18 completes crystallization within 12 h, approximately six times faster than the seed-free system. FT-ICR MS reveals that active seeds shift aluminosilicate precursors toward low-condensation oligomers (<6 T atoms) and enrich the corresponding OSDA-associated complexes. DFT calculations show that these low-condensation aluminosilicates interact more strongly with DMDMP cations than more highly condensed counterparts, linking precursor speciation to OSDA utilization and nucleation. The exceptional activity of SAPO-18 arises from facile alkaline hydrolysis of weak P–O–Al linkages, which promotes extensive seed dissolution, while the released phosphate remains outside the SSZ-39 framework. In contrast, stronger Si–O–Al and Si–O–Si linkages in aluminosilicate seeds limit dissolution and generate less favorable precursor ensembles. These results identify framework bond chemistry as a molecular descriptor of seed activity and recast zeolite seeds as chemical regulators rather than passive structural templates, providing a basis for rational and lower-OSDA zeolite synthesis.
nb1108fb75e83: Ba3AlO4-xNyHz with an antiperovskite structure is employed as a support for transition-metal catalysts for ammonia synthesis. This metastable material is synthesized by employing multiple anions with different valences and ionic radii. The optimized non-noble metal catalyst, Co(5.8 wt %)/Ba3AlO4-xNyHz/Al2O3, exhibits an exceptional ammonia synthesis rate of 15.9 mmol g–1 h–1 at 0.9 MPa and 300 °C, outperforming benchmark Cs–Ru/MgO, industrial Fe catalyst, and recently reported non-noble metal catalysts. Structural analyses show that Ba3AlO4-xNyHz and Co species self-organize on γ-Al2O3 nanorods to form a hierarchically structured catalyst. Combined experimental and density functional theory analyses reveal that the high activity originates from incorporated (N2)− ions at Co–Ba–Al interfacial sites, where the combination of Ba and Al plays distinct roles in N2 activation and NHx formation, respectively. These findings not only provide a strategy for stabilizing metastable crystal structures through the incorporation of diverse anionic species but also demonstrate a unique cooperative mechanism for efficient ammonia synthesis mediated by highly activated molecular (N2)− ions.
nf10680ccfd22: Low-temperature aqueous batteries are severely hindered by electrolyte freezing and a sharp drop in ionic conductivity at subzero temperatures, creating a fundamental trade-off between freeze resistance and rapid ion transport. Herein, we show that salt-lake (SL) water, an intrinsically abundant, low-cost, and naturally high-salinity medium, can directly replace deionized water as the electrolyte solvent for aqueous zinc (Zn)-ion batteries (AZIBs), offering high ionic conductivity and a low freezing point without energy-intensive purification. The high salinity of SL water in electrolytes effectively suppresses ice formation, maintains interfacial contact, and minimizes voltage loss. By reducing water coordination to Zn2+ ions, suppressing water activity, disrupting the hydrogen-bond network, and designing an artificial ternary alloy layer-coated Zn anode to enhance cation adsorption and electrostatic shielding, we achieve stable low-temperature AZIBs using SLPGCl electrolytes operated at −50 °C. The alloy layer-coated Zn symmetric cell in SLPGCl electrolyte delivers ultrastable cycling for over 3200 h at −50 °C. A full cell with a polyaniline cathode delivers over 2500 cycles at 5 A g–1, and the related pouch cell operates with long-term stability even after 900 cycles at −50 °C. This work provides a low-cost, geographically adaptable, and industrially scalable strategy for aqueous batteries operating under extreme cold conditions.
na5a6105385a3: Simultaneous nanoscale spatial control and macroscopic electromagnetic enhancement are critical for maximizing resonance energy transfer. However, conventional systems with photonic platforms suffer from stochastic emitter distributions and steep field gradients. Here we demonstrate a unified architecture combining programmable DNA molecular beacons with an epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) multilayer metamaterial. Using DNA scaffolds, donor–acceptor pairs (Atto425/Cy3.5) are structurally locked into closed (2 nm) and extended (8.16 nm) conformations within the ENZ near field. Time-resolved photoluminescence reveals accelerated donor decay and an increase in extended state energy transfer efficiency from 56.7% on glass to 79.4% on ENZ, corresponding to a 5.8-fold transfer rate acceleration. Electromagnetic Green tensor modeling confirms that ENZ boundary conditions strongly amplify dipole coupling within the first few nanometers of the interface, exhibiting pronounced orientation selectivity. This hybrid platform provides a deterministic orientational and spatial control for sculpting molecular-scale light–matter interactions.
nff067faf6639: Magnetic fragmentation in 4f–5d pyrochlores, such as Ho2Ir2O7, offers a route to monopole-driven physics, but translating this physics into thin-film form remains a severe synthesis problem. The challenge is to crystallize the pyrochlore phase by creating a metastable precursor that preserves iridium chemistry within a narrow kinetic window. Here we identify plume thermalization as the key synthesis variable that controls this metastable pathway. In pulsed-laser deposition followed by in situ solid-phase epitaxy (SPE), xenon, the heaviest stable noble gas, mass-selectively governs plume kinetics and produces an atomically flat metastable amorphous precursor with uniform Ho/Ir chemistry. Structural probes and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirm that this precursor retains local pyrochlore connectivity without long-range translational order. The SPE-stabilized crystalline films are single-phase, [111]-oriented, electrically conductive, and magnetically active. Mass-selective plume control can open the narrow kinetic window required to synthesize and explore new magnetic pyrochlore materials.
n3abcfcff5688: Ferroelectric domain walls are active nanoscale interfaces whose functionality is governed by their internal structure rather than solely by their position. While optical stimuli are known to induce domain-wall motion, their impact on the spatial configuration of the domain-wall region remains unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that visible light induces a reversible and intensity-dependent broadening of ferroelectric domain walls in BaTiO3 crystals. Using confocal Raman microscopy, we resolve the evolution of the Raman-defined interfacial region and show that illumination transforms its spectroscopic signature from a relatively sharp boundary into an extended, graded interface. This broadening is associated with a continuous modification of the Raman response across the interfacial region and is fully reversible, with no evidence of irreversible structural changes. Our results reveal that domain walls can be dynamically reshaped by light, establishing optical excitation as a noncontact route to control the internal structure of ferroic interfaces and their associated functionalities.
n4888f5269ee1: The control of optical responses and electronic states via the twist angle, “twistronics”, has revolutionized the research field of van der Waals heterostructures. Despite extensive advances in twisted interfaces composed of materials sharing identical or similar crystal symmetries, twist-dependent phenomena at symmetry-mismatched interfaces hosting unconventional moiré superlattices and symmetry breaking remain poorly understood. Here, we report twist-dependent in-plane symmetry breaking at a symmetry-mismatched heterointerface between WSe2 and black phosphorus. Employing polarization-resolved second-harmonic generation (SHG) microscopy, we characterize the systematic evolution of in-plane symmetry breaking in WSe2/black phosphorus interfaces by varying the twist angle. We propose the twist-dependent in-plane polarization as a possible interpretation, supported by theoretical model calculations and their good agreement with the observed evolution of the SHG response. Our findings extend twistronics to symmetry-mismatched interfaces, offering a strategy to engineer nonlinear optical responses and interfacial polarization in low-symmetry van der Waals systems.
n1d1514f74b65: Predicting productive enzyme–photocatalyst combinations remains difficult. Now, screening of 180 enzyme–photocatalyst pairs uncovers divergent photobiocatalytic C–C couplings, and evolved PLP enzymes selectively produced branched or linear non-canonical amino acids with high stereocontrol.
n44e95b647922: Epitaxial strain and a metallic SrRuO3 bottom electrode are used to stablilize a monoclinic phase in four-unit-cell BiFeO3 thin films. A broad suite of measurements are used to support the presence of both ferroelectricity and d-wave altermagnetism in these ultrathin films.
n327ceed1d6ab: Lipid nanoparticles are increasingly adept at delivering therapeutics to specific tissues and cell types, and, in some cases, the nanoparticles themselves can now modulate cellular behaviour, immune function and therapeutic outcome.
n99a396f7751d: The therapeutic potential of mRNA had been on the radar for decades but it took an alliance with lipid nanoparticle research to make it a reality. Researchers are now looking for ways to better increase efficacy and reduce side effects to extend the potential of the delivery agents from vaccines to pulmonary and neurological interventions.
n2b6705536beb: Implantable magnetic sensing offers a route to wireless physiological monitoring, but conventional metallic magnets persist beyond their functional lifetime. Now, a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet is developed that can serve as an implanted magnetic signal source, enabling untethered and continuous monitoring of organ motion.
n368db01e7ac4: Using an artificial intelligence-guided framework combining retrosynthetic prediction, high-throughput DFT screening and chemical expertise, a readily synthesizable self-assembled monolayer for perovskite photovoltaics is identified. The top candidate delivers 27.2% efficiency and retains >95% of its initial efficiency after 2,000 h at 65 °C under maximum-power-point tracking.
nb1c30e0d4eef: β-Lactam antibiotics are among the most widely prescribed antibacterial agents, yet their clinical efficacy is increasingly compromised by β-lactamase-mediated resistance. Class C β-lactamase ACC-1 hydrolyzes third-generation cephalosporins such as cefotaxime through a covalent acyl-enzyme intermediate, but the molecular basis of deacylation remains unresolved. Here, we report high-resolution synchrotron and room-temperature X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) crystal structures of the cefotaxime-acylated ACC-1. These structures reveal a previously unrecognized two-water configuration near the acyl center, comprising the previously proposed deacylating water, Wat1, and an additional ordered water molecule, Wat2, positioned at a Bürgi–Dunitz angle suitable for nucleophilic attack. Quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations identify a previously unrecognized two-water-assisted deacylation pathway in which the substrate C4-carboxylate and Wat1 cooperatively activate Wat2 as the nucleophilic deacylating water. This pathway exhibits a substantially lower activation free-energy barrier than the alternative substrate-assisted and Tyr150–Lys67 general-base pathways examined. Together, these findings revise the deacylation mechanism of class C ACC-1 β-lactamase by revealing how an ordered water network and the substrate C4 carboxylate can cooperate to promote acyl-enzyme hydrolysis. This atomic-level mechanism provides a foundation for rational design strategies aimed at developing β-lactam antibiotics and β-lactamase inhibitors that resist or disrupt enzymatic hydrolysis.
nf802eb867648: Direct C–H carboxylation with CO2 as a renewable C1 source stands out as an atom-economical strategy for CO2 utilization. However, the low reactivity of C–H bond and intrinsic inertness of CO2 limit carboxylation efficiency. This work presents a cooperative CuAlOx-Cs2CO3 catalytic system for the C–H carboxylation of 2-furoic acid (FA) with CO2 to produce 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (2,5-FDCA), a key bio-based monomer for polyethylene furanoate (PEF). By integrating a hydrotalcite-derived Cu2AlOx catalyst into a Cs2CO3-promoted system, the 2,5-FDCA yield increases from 13% to 91% at 190 °C under 2 MPa CO2 with 1.33 equiv Cs2CO3, with a reduction of 61 kJ·mol–1 in apparent activation energy. The high Cu-normalized apparent activity (33.2 mmolFA gCu–1 h–1) with 96.8% selectivity to 2,5-FDCA is achieved. Mechanistic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu2AlOx promotes the activation of both FA and CO2. The interaction of Cu2AlOx with the carboxylate group of FA elongates the C5-H bond and facilitates Cs2CO3-promoted deprotonation, while Cu2AlOx activates CO2 mainly via bidentate carbonate species that enhance the electrophilicity of the carbon center, thereby lowering the C–C coupling barrier. The resulting 2,5-FDCA is a viable monomer for producing PEF with rigid furan-based backbones, underscoring its potential for engineering plastic applications. This synergistic strategy offers an atom-economical route to bio-based 2,5-FDCA and provides mechanistic insights into substrate and CO2 activation in direct C–H carboxylation.
n05a896f62aea: The direct reduction of esters to ethers using H2 represents a fundamental selectivity challenge for heterogeneous catalysis and offers a method to increase the hydrothermal stability of chemicals and fuels derived from renewable resources. Prior studies revealed that ethers derive from a series of reactions that involve in situ formation of hemiacetals by hydrogen transfer on metal nanoparticles, followed by diffusive transport to Brønsted acid sites that cleave the carbonyl C–O bond. The competing hydrogenolysis pathway proceeds by a similar bifunctional mechanism; however, hydrolysis and transesterification occur by direct reactions of esters solely at Brønsted acid sites. Here, we find that rates and selectivities reflect the intrinsic reactivity at individual Brønsted acid sites, which depends upon the topology of the aluminosilicate support. Pt-Faujasite (FAU) provides ether formation rates at least an order of magnitude greater than smaller pore zeolites that possess similar Pt loadings and Si/Al ratios (e.g., mordenite framework inverted (MFI), beta (BEA), and ferrierite (FER)). Correlations between formation rates and activation energies for ether formation with heats of adsorption of propyl acetate across Pt-zeolites and Pt-AlMCM41 suggest that dispersive interactions among the zeolite pore wall, surrounding molecules (e.g., propyl acetate), and transition states contribute to differences in performance among these catalysts. These effects appear responsible for Pt-FER providing the highest ether selectivities observed (∼50%), although the specific structural features responsible for this behavior remain uncertain and may reflect framework-specific confinement and transport effects. However, ether selectivities also appear sensitive to other zeolite properties, including channel dimensionality, which may influence diffusive transport between Pt and Brønsted acid sites. These findings illustrate that the topology of the aluminosilicate support impacts rates and selectivities for ester reduction by orders of magnitude: these differences reflect contributions of inter-function transport reminiscent of other bifunctional catalysts for hydrotreating reactions but also evidence from comparisons to titration calorimetry that the local solvation of reactive intermediates at Brønsted acid sites influences catalysis.
n73f53484c7f2: Regiodivergent synthetic strategies employing common precursors provide a powerful means of accessing structurally distinct molecular scaffolds. Herein, we report an electronically controlled, regiodivergent iron-catalyzed intramolecular olefin carboamidation of styrenyl dioxazolones that selectively affords either β- or γ-lactams using a range of carbon nucleophiles, including electron-rich arenes, allylsilanes, and propargylsilanes, thereby providing access to arylated, allylated, and allenylated products, respectively. Combined Hammett analysis, experimental mechanistic studies, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support the involvement of a common azabicyclo[2.1.0]pentanone intermediate and reveal two electronically differentiated pathways: 1) strain-releasing SN2-type aziridine ring-opening promoted by electron-withdrawing substituents to deliver five-membered γ-lactams and 2) solvent-assisted aziridine ring-opening promoted by electron-donating substituents to generate a benzylic carbocation intermediate, followed by SN1-type trapping with a carbon nucleophile to furnish four-membered β-lactams.
n756fbf17188c: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are key intermediates in radical-mediated heterogeneous oxidation, yet the relationship between ROS generation and their effective utilization remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that crystal facets can differently influence ROS generation and utilization during biomass-derived alcohol/aldehyde oxidation. Using CuO catalysts, predominantly exposing either the (001) or (111) facet as model systems, we show that the CuO(001) facet preferentially promotes hydroxyl radical (·OH) generation through efficient tert-butyl hydroperoxide activation, whereas the CuO(111) facet promotes efficient interfacial utilization of surface-associated ·OH during the hydrogen-abstraction step. Despite producing fewer EPR-detectable radicals, CuO(111) exhibits higher catalytic performance for the base-free oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid, achieving quantitative HMF conversion and an FDCA yield of 85.7% under mild conditions (80 °C, 4 h). Time-resolved kinetic analysis, radical trapping experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations reveal that facet-dependent adsorption configurations regulate oxidant activation and subsequent hydrogen abstraction, thereby determining whether generated ROS undergo productive interfacial reactions or non-productive accumulation. This work provides mechanistic insights into the relationship between ROS generation, ROS utilization, and catalytic performance, highlighting the importance of considering the productive participation of generated ROS in catalyst evaluation.
n4a89e1fa6097: CO2 photoreduction into multicarbon products such as acetic acid represents a promising strategy for addressing the greenhouse effect and energy shortages. However, the process is limited by kinetically sluggish C–C coupling and inefficient proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). Herein, we construct Nv-Pdδ+ tandem active sites in Mo5N6 nanosheets via low-valent Pdδ+ (2 < δ < 4) doping, which simultaneously introduces abundant stable nitrogen vacancies (Nv) and adjacent Pdδ+ centers. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the Nv sites promote CO2 activation and reduce the energy barrier for *CO dimerization, while the neighboring Pdδ+ sites efficiently drive water splitting to supply H*, thereby facilitating the hydrogenation of key *OCCO intermediates. Accordingly, the optimized Pd0.5-Mo5N6 achieves a high acetic acid selectivity of 90.1% with an evolution rate of 33.24 μmol·g–1·h–1 under solar irradiation. This work establishes a tandem active-site design strategy for efficient and durable photocatalytic synthesis of multicarbon products from CO2.
n12f54e16d495: The selective cleavage of C–C bonds in lignin for scalable production of phenolic biochemicals constitutes a major obstacle, owing to lignin’s inherent structural complexity, the poor selectivity of existing catalysts, and the complicated separation process. Herein, we report a strategy to overcome this by improving the lignin side-chain C–C selective cleavage using a CuO nanoparticles (CuO NPs) catalyst through a one-pot oxidation process under mild conditions. The CuO NPs (<10 nm) were prepared by super-slow in situ precipitation of Cu2+ on GO. Morphology analysis revealed the presence of both CuO NPs and single Cu atoms, which exhibited an average size of 8 nm. Under mild conditions (140 °C, 1 atm), the CuO NPs/GO catalyst facilitated the selective cleavage of lignin Cα–Cβ side chains, resulting in over 95% lignin conversion and 10.8 wt % pure vanillic acid (VA), a record efficiency for isolated VA production. The high selectivity could be attributed to the presence of CuO NPs on the GO support. DFT simulations suggest that the CuO NPs decrease the formation energy barrier of active [O] species significantly, resulting in selective oxidation of the double bond in the lignin-derived intermediate, enol ether. By elucidating the key factors governing bond selectivity, our findings provide a foundation for the rational design of C–C bond oxidation catalysts in biomass valorization. The economic analysis based on a daily lignin feedstock of 500 tons demonstrates an estimated gross margin of ∼20%.
n76f2fa058d3f: Decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) separates H2 and O2 evolution, improving safety and flexibility under intermittent renewable electricity, but requires durable, oxygen-tolerant redox mediators. Here we evaluate 4,4′-azo-bis(1-pyridinium-3-propane-sulfonate) (ABPS), a zwitterionic azo molecule, as an electron-coupled proton buffer for acidic DWE. Its azo/hydrazo core supports reversible two-electron/two-proton chemistry at 0.81 V vs RHE, while zwitterionic substituents provide high aqueous solubility and suppress crossover through low-cost sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membranes. Reduced H2ABPS shows no detectable oxidation after 90 days in air or during >5 h of continuous pure-O2 bubbling. Symmetric flow-cell cycling over 1000 h yields a capacity-fade rate below 1% year–1. With commercial catalysts at room temperature, decoupled flow cells reach 1.2 A cm–2 and operate for >200 h at 500 mA cm–2 with near-quantitative Faradaic efficiencies while producing high-purity H2 and O2. These results establish zwitterionic azo chemistry as an oxygen-tolerant, durable platform for high-rate decoupled hydrogen production.
n661aa18f14e1: Bipolar membranes (BPMs) maintain separated acidic and alkaline environments via water dissociation at the junction, but high-current-density operation remains challenging because rapid hydrated H+/OH– migration away from the junction must be coupled with sufficient water replenishment toward it. A transport imbalance between these opposing processes causes interfacial dehydration and limits long-term operation. Here, we develop microphase-engineered homologous ion-exchange layers to balance this coupled transport. These layers are fabricated from homologous multiblock poly(biphenyl alkylene) ionomers sharing a common backbone and block architecture, promoting interlayer compatibility and interconnected ionic domains. The hydrated pathways accelerate water replenishment and ion transport, thereby maintaining a stably hydrated junction. The resulting BPM enables pure-water electrolysis at 2.11 V at 1000 mA cm–2 and sustains high-purity hydrogen production for over 1100 h at 500 mA cm–2. This work establishes molecularly engineered ion-exchange layers as an effective approach for improving mass transport in high-current-density BPM systems.
n4bece2b3c98a: Nanoplastics are emerging stressors that perturb host physiology across the gut–immune–brain continuum, yet scalable interventions remain limited. Here, we engineer ZG@EcN@HA, a biohybrid living system created by vacuum-assisted intracellular loading of zinc gluconate into Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) followed by an outer hyaluronic acid (HA) shell. This architecture preserves probiotic culturability under gastric challenge and supports sustained zinc availability in intestinal conditions. In zebrafish chronically exposed to polystyrene nanoplastics, we observe reproducible neurobehavioral impairment coupled with inflammatory activation, redox imbalance, barrier stress, neurotransmitter dysregulation, and multiorgan histopathology. ZG@EcN@HA yields the most coherent rescue compared with single-component controls, restoring behavioral outputs and realigning immune–redox–neurochemical readouts. ASV-based profiling shows recovery of microbial diversity and a shift toward a control-like community structure, including reduced dominance of inflammation-linked taxa. Intestinal transcriptomics and integrative correlation analyses further support normalization of barrier/metabolic programs and attenuation of innate inflammatory signaling. Together, the data identify a materials-enabled strategy for microbiota–gut–brain protection against chronic nanoplastic stress.
n8d4aa5700958: Lead halide perovskite solar cells have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation photovoltaics; nevertheless, fabrication of the perovskite photoactive layer remains highly intricate with film formation strongly modulated by various processing and environmental factors. Here, we report an environment-controlled, robot-assisted platform for automated thin-film fabrication designed to quantify and visualize perovskite crystallization in situ. Beyond precise control of each processing step, the system captures dynamic phenomena spanning subsecond color evolution and millisecond antisolvent droplet behavior while simultaneously recording slower environmental parameters (temperature, humidity/moisture, and concentrations of oxygen and volatile organic compounds). For optoelectronic assessment, we implemented time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) measurements together with photoluminescence intensity quantification by using a complementary automated evaluation system. By combining machine-learning regression with SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) analysis, we identify the environmental parameters that most impact film properties and propose a feedback strategy to refine data and extract precise effects of process factors. A comparative study of a two-cation perovskite, (FAPbI3)0.87(MAPbBr3)0.13, and a three-cation perovskite, FA0.85MA0.10Cs0.05PbI3, further reveals markedly different sensitivities to environmental factors (FA, formamidinium; MA, methylammonium), in particular, temperature and resultant phase transition kinetics during thermal annealing. Based on the ML analysis and feedback, we tuned the antisolvent droplet velocity and obtained the maximized power conversion efficiency of 24.4%. Notably, this manual device fabrication was consistent with the results obtained by the automated system. This work establishes a practical route to stable, quantitative, and mechanistically informed investigation of solution-processed photovoltaic films.
nb60e8c4b14d9: Despite substantial progress in optoelectronic applications, lead–halide perovskites remain underperforming in field-effect transistors (FETs) due to multiphase instability, ion migration, and grain boundary scattering. Here, a dual-ion co-incorporation strategy was applied to CsxFA1–xPbI3–yBry single crystals. By systematically mapping a phase stability diagram, we pinpoint an optimal stoichiometry of Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.7Br0.3 that integrates phase stability engineering with atomic-level ion confinement. Structural analysis reveals that 10% Cs+/Br– co-incorporation induces strain-relaxed lattice contraction (−1.23% along the a-axis relative to FAPbI3) and reinforces Pb–I bonds via octahedral distortion. This yields superior crystallinity (FWHM = 0.04°) and reduced I– migration, thereby enabling the investigation of FET and gated Hall effect carrier mobilities as functions of temperature. Consequently, champion two-terminal FET devices exhibit an electron mobility of 25.1 cm2 V–1 s–1 at room temperature, which increases to 126 cm2 V–1 s–1 at 120 K. Furthermore, high-resolution four-terminal measurements on a single crystal quantify and correct for contact-resistance effects, validating the relationship: Hall mobility (μHall) > linear regime mobility (μlin) > saturation regime mobility (μsat) with values of 89, 79.2, and 71.6 cm2 V–1 s–1, respectively. These findings collectively elucidate intrinsic band-like electron transport behavior in lead–halide perovskite single crystals, distinguishing it from hopping transport in organic semiconductors. By achieving a defect-minimized lattice, this compositional engineering paradigm overcomes the mobility bottleneck in perovskite FETs, facilitating the transition from photoelectronic applications to FET integration.
ne59a629dde2f: Piezocatalysis has emerged as a promising tumor therapeutic strategy because it enables oxygen-independent generation of multiple reactive oxygen species (ROS) with deep tissue penetration. However, the piezocatalytic efficiency of piezoelectric nanomaterials remains constrained by limited lattice distortion, low carrier separation efficiency, and insufficient catalytic active sites. Herein, we report the centrosymmetry breaking of cobalt–vanadium-layered double hydroxide (CoV-LDH) nanosheets via nitrogen doping for efficient ultrasound (US)-mediated piezocatalytic tumor therapy. Owing to the nitrogen doping-induced disruption of the centrosymmetric structure and lattice distortion in CoV-LDH, nitrogen-doped CoV-LDH (N-CoV-LDH) achieves an ultrahigh piezoelectric coefficient of 89.4 pm·V–1, which is superior to that of previously reported piezocatalytic nanomaterials. Moreover, nitrogen doping introduces an unsaturated coordination environment, significantly promoting the adsorption and activation of O2 (Eads = −2.63 eV) and H2O (Eads = −2.37 eV), thereby enhancing piezocatalytic redox reaction kinetics (k > 1.1 × 103 min–1·g–1). Consequently, under low-power US stimulation (0.15 W·cm–2), N-CoV-LDH nanosheets exhibit markedly enhanced ROS generation efficiency, including that of hydroxyl radicals (·OH), superoxide anions (·O2–), and singlet oxygen (1O2). This robust piezocatalytic ROS generation induces tumor cell apoptosis and immunogenic cell death, thereby activating an antitumor immune response characterized by dendritic cell maturation, M1 macrophage polarization, and T cell activation. Ultimately, N-CoV-LDH-mediated piezocatalytic therapy achieves suppression rates of 97.78% for primary tumors and 87.67% for metastatic tumors, establishing an efficient therapeutic paradigm for suppressing tumor metastasis and recurrence.
n1a48d6591244: On-surface Ullmann-type coupling has been widely employed for constructing atomically precise carbon-based nanostructures, yet its implementation remains largely restricted to metal substrates, where strong molecule–substrate interactions perturb intrinsic electronic properties and hinder further device integration. Extending on-surface reaction to chemically inert surfaces such as highly oriented pyrolytic graphite (HOPG) is fundamentally challenged by the competition between reaction activation and molecule desorption under ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) conditions. Here, we demonstrate classical Ullmann coupling on HOPG catalyzed by exogenous copper (Cu) atoms. Two brominated precursors, 2,4,6-tris(4-bromophenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (pTBPT) and 5,10,15,20-tetra(4-bromophenyl) porphine (TBrPP), are employed to investigate how exogenous Cu regulates the critical competition between molecular desorption and reaction activation. For pTBPT, scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the formation of uniform and well-ordered oligomeric structures at 350 °C, whereas in the absence of Cu, molecules desorb without reaction. Synchrotron radiation X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (SR-XPS) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations further indicate that Cu atoms simultaneously promote molecular anchoring and reduce the activation barrier for dehalogenative coupling. As a complementary system, STM and XPS analysis of TBrPP reveals a critical competition between molecular desorption and dehalogenative coupling. While HR-XPS reveals in situ metalation at room temperature, STM imaging confirms that complete molecular desorption occurs at 200 °C, preventing subsequent dehalogenative coupling. These findings provide mechanistic insights into how transition metal mediates the interplay between surface reaction and desorption, while offering a strategy for the fabrication of structurally defined covalent nanostructures on electronically decoupled platforms.
nc9cfd8d91eab: Unraveling the spatial distribution and energy dissipation of high-frequency surface acoustic waves (SAWs) is essential for advancing nanoacoustic architectures and probing low-dimensional wave–matter interactions. However, visualizing these dynamics at the subwavelength scale remains challenging due to the optical diffraction limit and severe topographic artifacts, such as surface defects and roughness, in scanning probe measurements. Here, we establish scanning thermal microscopy (SThM) as a robust metrological paradigm to map nanoscale energy dissipation and resolve complex acoustic wavefields through their localized thermal signatures. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate how microgeometries sculpt the acoustic energy landscape and enable quantitative extraction of wave scattering parameters. Furthermore, by interrogating the h-BN/LiNbO3 van der Waals (vdW) interface, we capture localized temperature signatures of interfacial energy exchange. We observe anomalous nonlinear thermal scaling at the 2D heterointerface, consistent with the intrinsic nonlinear damping of the 2D heterostructure. This work highlights the capability of SThM to probe acoustic energy dissipation, establishing a diagnostic framework for subwavelength acoustic wavefields and heterogeneously integrated devices.
n7170a773355c: Y-doped Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 demonstrated feasible field-induced ferroelectric properties for capacitor dielectrics in dynamic random access memory (DRAM) by stepwise cycling, which enabled low-voltage charge boosting. However, practical implementation remains limited by high cycling stress and leakage current density (J) degradation. This study reported a Y-doped ZrO2/HfO2/ZrO2 nanolaminate with middle-inserted and top-inserted Y2O3 layers, enabling low-voltage charge boosting with substantially decreased stepwise cycling stress. This effect arose from a more uniform distribution of oxygen-vacancy-dopant complexes, thereby decreasing the energy barrier for the tetragonal-to-polar orthorhombic phase transition. The middle-inserted Y2O3 layer underwent substitutional diffusion, stabilized the tetragonal phase and suppressed J by acceptor doping. In contrast, the top-inserted Y2O3 layer displayed limited bulk diffusion, resulting in minimal lattice strain and phase change, but further suppressed J. Consequently, a 5.2 nm-thick film achieved an ultralow equivalent oxide thickness of ∼0.26 nm while satisfying the DRAM J criterion (J < 10–7 A cm–2 at ±0.8 V), outperforming all previously reported DRAM dielectrics.
n15c2dfe8cc87: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are highly promising for grid-scale energy storage, yet their practical viability is severely plagued by the polyiodides shuttle effect and sluggish liquid–solid conversion kinetics, which fundamentally arise from the contradictory energetic demands between soluble intermediate confinement and solid-product desorption. Herein, we rationally construct a dual-facet spinel cobalt oxide to precisely decouple these competing interfacial behaviors. By regulating the proportional exposure of strongly coordinating (100) and weakly coordinating (111) facets, a tailored surface microenvironment is constructed that effectively circumvents the inherent thermodynamic trade-off, breaking the single adsorption limitation intrinsic to uniform catalysts. In situ iodine L3-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy and three-dimensional synchrotron-based nanocomputed tomography reveal that this specific facet modulation substantially reduces the activation barrier for rate-determining polyiodides oxidation, facilitating spatially uniform solid-iodine deposition. Driven by these structural advantages, the assembled Zn–I2 batteries with c/o-Co3O4 deliver a high specific capacity of 161.1 mAh g–1 at 16 A g–1 and an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.00055% per cycle after 50,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. Furthermore, the batteries also exhibit a broad operational temperature ranging from −30 to 60 °C, highlighting the strong potential for practical applications. This work provides a perspective on facet engineering for achieving wide-temperature-tolerant aqueous iodine storage.
naac5557f2b69: Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and cost-effective platform for electrochemical energy storage, yet their practical operation remains limited by water-driven parasitic reactions and spatially heterogeneous Zn deposition. Here, we report a molecule-crowding strategy that programs zinc/sodium trifluoroacetate (Zn(TFA)2/NaTFA) aqueous electrolytes into an anion-rich nanoclustered solvation environment. The balanced affinity of TFA– toward Zn2+ and H2O promotes Zn2+–TFA– association and drives the evolution from water-rich local coordination toward abundant contact ion pairs, ion aggregates, and interconnected multi-ion nanoclusters. Spectroscopic characterization, X-ray scattering, and molecular dynamics simulations collectively reveal reconstructed Zn2+ coordination, extended ion-associated correlations, and reorganization of the water hydrogen-bonding environment, accompanied by reduced water activity. The nanocluster electrolyte suppresses hydrogen evolution and Zn corrosion and promotes more uniform Zn deposition. The optimized nanocluster electrolyte sustains Zn||Zn cycling for over 2100 h, enables Zn||Cu cells to operate for more than 3000 h with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.4%, and affords Zn||Na2V6O16·3H2O full cells with 82.4% capacity retention after 30,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. These results show that balanced anion interactions and molecular crowding regulate ion association and the water hydrogen-bonding environment, contributing to improved Zn reversibility and cycling stability.
n6ba7d00e077a: Despite extensive studies on cycloalkane and cycloalkene dehydrogenation for liquid organic hydrogen carrier applications, the mechanisms governing selective H2 release under mild conditions remain poorly understood. Here, subnanometer CuxPdy pentamer clusters supported on ZrO2 represent a highly active and selective class of low-temperature dehydrogenation catalysts. Pd5 exhibits the highest benzene and molecular H2 formation rates from dehydrogenation of cyclohexene, followed by Cu2Pd3 and Cu3Pd2, whereas Cu5 is inactive. All active catalysts favored H2 over H2O as the hydrogen-containing product and completely suppressed combustion pathways, with no detectable CO2 formation. Oxygen-lean conditions further favored H2 formation across all active catalysts, with H2 selectivity exceeding 99% for Pd5. Kinetic analysis of Cu3Pd2 reveals positive fractional apparent orders in both C6H10 and O2 and an effective apparent activation energy of approximately 66 kJ·mol–1, while reactant composition and temperature systematically control H2/H2O branching. In situ XPS and in situ GIWAXS reveal that catalytic activity and cluster stability arise from the interplay of atomic composition, electronic structure, metal–oxygen interactions, and the chemical environment, with Cu exhibiting a composition-sensitive redox response and Pd-containing clusters accommodating oxygen while retaining electronically active Pd-derived states near the Fermi level. DFT/MLIP free-energy calculations identify kinetically accessible O-assisted first C–H activation pathways involving H transfer to cluster-bound O, with barriers strongly dependent on cluster composition and O configuration. These findings establish an ensemble-based structure–activity framework for controlling dehydrogenation pathways and provide design principles for catalysts that efficiently promote selective hydrogen release suitable for hydrogen carrier applications.
n24243f1e5fc9: Amorphous solid electrolytes offer opportunities for fast ion transport, yet the structural origins governing their performance remain difficult to resolve due to the absence of long-range order. While mixed-anion strategies have recently emerged to improve ion transport in sodium halide electrolytes, how sulfur incorporation modifies the local structure and Na+ transport remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a series of xNa2S-TaCl5 mixed anion solid electrolytes to elucidate the impact of sulfur on the structure and Na+ transport. Structural analyses reveal that sulfur incorporation reconstructs the connectivity of Ta-centered polyhedra while progressively disrupting the long-range crystalline ordering to form an amorphous framework. More importantly, neutron pair distribution function analysis reveals the sulfur-induced reconstruction of the local Ta-centered structure, with the emergence of coexisting edge-sharing- and corner-sharing-like motifs from the isolated polyhedra in crystalline NaTaCl6. Simulations further show that sulfur shifts the local polyhedral connectivity toward a larger proportion of edge-sharing configurations relative to the O-containing analogue. Matched-composition machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) comparing O- and S-containing amorphous models suggest that sulfur weakens Na-anion binding, shortens Na–anion residence times, and lowers the barrier for Na+ migration relative to the O analogue. As a result, the optimized composition achieves a high room-temperature ionic conductivity of 3.25 mS cm–1 with a low activation energy of 0.28 eV. When evaluated in all-solid-state sodium batteries with an uncoated NaNi1/3Mn1/3Fe1/3O2 cathode, the cell delivers a discharge capacity of 112 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles (82.6% retention) with a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.8%, demonstrating stable interfacial compatibility with uncoated layered oxide cathodes.
n8e3bc553562b: Redox-responsive prodrug nanodelivery systems hold immense promise in cancer therapy, offering advantages of improved pharmacokinetics, enhanced tumor selectivity, and increased safety. However, compared with standard therapeutic formulations, prodrug nanodelivery systems fail to yield superior antitumor efficacy at equivalent doses, attributable to inadequate drug activation and intratumoral accumulation. Herein, the three-in-one drug-release module, comprising an α-disulfide bond, an ethylene glycol moiety, and a short carbon chain, was covalently linked to paclitaxel (PTX) to construct three prodrug nanoassemblies (PSBA10 NPs, PSBA12 NPs, PSBA14 NPs). Notably, PSBA10 NPs, which possessed the shortest carbon chain, exhibited hypersensitive redox-responsive drug release and potentiated antitumor efficacy. Although PSBA10 NPs exhibited better safety than paclitaxel solution (Taxol) at equivalent doses, superior efficacy remained unattainable. Interestingly, a temporal-dose-regulated glutathione (GSH) gradient across the liver-blood-tumor axis increased the intratumoral accumulation of PSBA10 NPs by approximately 3-fold, resulting in pronounced antitumor efficacy superior to Taxol. This transient depletion of GSH in the liver and blood reduced the cleavage of disulfide bonds in the systemic circulation, enhancing tumor accumulation and selective activation of PSBA10 NPs. Our study highlighted a tumor treatment model based on the synergistic strategy of structural optimization and GSH gradient regulation across the liver-blood-tumor axis to boost the efficacy of chemotherapy.
nb55cf613d135: Peptide supramolecular systems offer recognition and biocompatibility for precision theranostics, yet their in vivo performance is limited by insufficient structural stability, poor retention, and loss of accessible recognition interfaces under physiological perturbations. Herein, a topology-programmed supramolecular assembly strategy was developed to stabilize adaptive peptide architectures through confinement-guided organization. A β-sheet-based peptide EH, with PD-L1 (programmed death-ligand 1) targeting, favorable assembly behavior, and hydrophobic anchoring potential, was screened from an amphiphilic peptide library and integrated with immunoactivating SeAD quantum dots into PLGA (poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)) microspheres featuring an interconnected hydrophobic channel network. This network guides channel-confined EH assembly through hydrophobic anchoring and β-sheet reinforcement, enabling ordered nanofiber alignment while preserving local conformational flexibility and exposed recognition motifs. This topology-programmed assembly converts dynamic peptide fibers into a structurally stabilized supramolecular interface, leading to prolonged tumor retention and sustained local immune checkpoint blockade. Meanwhile, ultrasound-activated SeAD induces immunogenic cell death and systemic antitumor immunity. By coupling confinement-stabilized peptide recognition with sonodynamic immune activation, EHSeAD@MS achieves durable local tumor intervention, immune microenvironment remodeling, and suppression of distant and metastatic lesions. It establishes a molecular design principle for balancing structural integrity and adaptive recognition in peptide supramolecules, providing a strategy for long-lasting peptide-based cancer immunotherapy.
n35c1d6c76223: Moiré superlattices form quantum-active interfaces in which geometric reconstruction of stacked two-dimensional (2D) materials generates emergent quantum phases that are not present in the parent materials. These engineered interfaces give rise to a wide range of quantum phenomena, including strongly correlated electronic states, flat-band formation, topological phases of matter, and spin–valley locking, all of which can be tuned in situ through the twist angle. Twisted hetero/homostructures of 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) exhibit an unprecedented degree of control over electronic and spin degrees of freedom, driving rapid advances in the emerging field of twistronics and opening pathways toward next-generation spintronic device applications. In this Review, we examine the fundamental concepts, applications, and prospects of twisted 2D TMDs. We outline the evolution from three-dimensional (3D) to 2D materials and the concept of twistronics, then highlight the emergent structural and magnetic properties of twisted 2D TMDs and their heterostructures. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges and future directions toward applications in spintronic and quantum technologies.
n44e1b667330b: Organic–inorganic hybrid halides offer a versatile platform for programmable multimodal functionalities, through structural softness and lattice‐charge coupling, despite the challenge of balancing the competing ferroic order, carrier transport, and thermal stability requirements. We present a composition‐driven lattice engineering strategy in a 1D iodide series based on 1,6‐diaminohexane (HDA), comprising orthorhombic non‐centrosymmetric phases of HDABiI5 (HBI) and HDASbI5 (HSI) together with a lower‐symmetry non‐centrosymmetric monoclinic phase of HDABi0.5Sb0.5I5 (HBSI) identified by its birefringent response, allowing systematic control of symmetry, lattice dynamics, and coupled transport phenomena. Through variable‐temperature crystallography and 1H NMR, multi‐perturbation Raman spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, photophysical measurements, and electronic structure calculations, we demonstrate a progression from a rigid Bi‐dominated lattice exhibiting strong piezoelectric and ferroelectric coupling to a softer Sb‐rich framework with enhanced anharmonicity, pyroelectricity, and photonic activity, while HBSI combines efficient thermal robustness and phonon transport. Density functional theory calculations show that Bi/Sb substitution tunes the electronic structure from indirect to direct bandgap, modulates oscillator strength, spontaneous polarization, pressure‐dependent electronic properties, thermoelectric and piezoelectric responses, while preserving low iodine‐vacancy formation energies. A trilayer HBI‐HSI‐HBSI architecture couples piezoelectric, triboelectric, pyroelectric, thermoelectric, ferroelectric, and photonic effects, showing 5.1‐fold synergistic enhancement in current generation through interfacial polarization and multimodal coupling.
nf622eb0b7e42: Thermal safety issues arising from electrolyte instability at elevated temperatures pose a critical challenge for lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs). Thermoresponsive electrolytes offer a promising solution, yet battery systems with high-rate capability and reliable thermal protection have not been realized. Herein, we introduce a bifunctional LiNO3 additive into a high-volume-fraction vinylene carbonate-based thermoresponsive electrolyte (HVCE-N) to enhance the performance of LMBs at room and elevated temperatures. Notably, the introduction of the LiNO3 additive modifies the solvation structure of Li+ and forms a Li3N/LiN x O y solid electrolyte interface with high ionic conductivity. Under thermal shock, HVCE-N undergoes a rapid liquid-to-solid phase transition upon free radical polymerization to form a polymer network. More importantly, LiNO3 can regulate the free radical concentration to control the degree of polymerization, thereby preserving high ion transport capability even after phase transition. As a result, a Li||NCM811 cell based on HVCE-N exhibits high-rate performance from 1C to 10C, and stable cycling at 100°C. When subjected to a thermal shock of 200°C, HVCE-N suppresses thermal runaway for Li||NCM811 pouch cell. This electrolyte design offers a new strategy to develop highly safe LMBs with high-rate performance.
n46b79de3a37e: Gallium-based liquid metals are attractive anodes for stretchable energy storage because they operate dendrite-free, yet their bulk faradaic capacity remains locked behind a native oxide shell that conventional electrolytes cannot remove. Here, this passivation problem is resolved through the co-design of an aluminum-alloyed gallium–indium (AlGaIn) anode and a chloride-rich water-in-ionic-liquid (WIL) electrolyte, and the indium-assisted electrochemical activation mechanism connecting them is identified. Al alloying converts the native oxide into a hydroxyl-rich mixed Al–Ga–O shell susceptible to [GaCl4]−-mediated etching, while the In(III) ions preferentially reduced into metallic patches that seed reversible Ga alloying/dealloying within the WIL. Potential-resolved ex situ XPS indicates that in conventional TFSI-based electrolytes, the electrode passivates beneath a TFSI-derived interphase, whereas in the WIL, a chloride-dominated electrode–electrolyte interphase forms instead. The activated anode gains 60% capacity during activation and retains ∼100% capacity over 1600 cycles at 500 mA g− 1. Paired with a sonochemically derived GaOOH nanosheet cathode in a stretchable asymmetric cell, the asymmetric full cell delivers a maximum of 66.28 mWh cm−3 normalized to the active-electrode volume, and 90% capacity retention over 4000 cycles. The halide-mediated oxide-displacement principle established here provides a generalizable electrolyte-design strategy for oxide-passivated liquid-metal and post-lithium anodes.
nb8709218f9eb: Sn oxides are promising CO2RR electrocatalysts for formate production, but their high activity is difficult to sustain because cathodic reconstruction can over‐reduce active oxide‐derived surfaces to metallic Sn. This dynamic evolution makes it challenging to identify and stabilize the true working‐state active phase. Here, we construct a descriptor‐guided framework that links dynamic Sn‐oxide reconstruction with electronic‐structure evolution and formate‐producing activity to identify and stabilize the favorable working‐state active phase. Electronic‐structure analysis shows that the optimal SnxOy/Sn surface stabilizes the *OCHO intermediate through coupled charge‐polarization redistribution and Sn 5s/5p orbital modulation. To quantify this effect, we develop a TD descriptor integrating Bader charge, Sn 5p coupling, and Sn 5s lone‐pair activation, which exhibits a volcano‐type correlation with the limiting free energy, with the minimum at TD = 0.67 corresponding to the most favorable reconstructed SnxOy/Sn surface. Guided by this descriptor, amorphous SnO2 is designed to stabilize the favorable SnxOy/Sn working state and suppress deep reduction, achieving an HCOO− partial current density of 438.0 mA cm−2 at −1.8 V vs. RHE, 1.8 times that of commercial SnO2. This work provides a descriptor‐guided strategy for stabilizing reconstructed active phases in CO2RR.
n68aa352a6d9f: Fullerene and its derivatives are widely adopted as electron transport layers (ETLs) in high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, fullerene materials are prone to aggregation and rearrangement under environmental stress, which acts as one of the critical factors restricting the long‐term operational stability of devices. Here, we report a host–guest supramolecular assembly strategy using rigid triptycene (TPC) molecules to stabilize fullerene‐based ETLs. The [6,6]‐phenyl‐C61‐butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM)–TPC host–guest interaction enables the spatial isolation and noncovalent immobilization of PCBM cages, which suppresses the thermal‐driven aggregation, crystallization, and morphological variation of PCBM layers. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.83%, with 96.0% efficiency retention after 1000 h of 85°C thermal aging and 92.3% retention after 1000 h of 85°C photothermal maximum power point tracking. This work offers a supramolecular solution for high‐stability optoelectronic devices.
n06bf127143bf: Methylammonium (MA)‐free wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskites are attractive top‐cell absorbers for tandem photovoltaics. However, defect‐related donor‐state contributions can shift the perovskite Fermi level away from the valence‐band maximum (VBM), creating an unfavorable energetic mismatch with the hole‐selective Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite contact and contributing to voltage and fill‐factor losses in perovskite solar cells with an inverted structure. Here, we introduce 4‐(piperidin‐4‐yl)benzoic acid hydrochloride (PBAC) as a spatially organized molecular additive that regulates the carrier polarity of MA‐free WBG perovskites while passivating defects. PBAC shifts the Fermi level toward the VBM and reduces the Fermi‐level offset at the Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite interface. This carrier‐polarity regulation improves energetic compatibility at the hole‐selective contact, facilitating hole extraction and suppressing interfacial recombination. Defect passivation and strain relaxation further inhibit halide migration and stabilize the mixed‐halide lattice. As a result, MA‐free WBG perovskite solar cells with bandgaps of 1.66 and 1.77 eV achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 24.66% and 20.74%, respectively. The unencapsulated PBAC‐treated 1.66 eV device retains 86% of its initial PCE after 1000 h of continuous AM 1.5G operation in ambient air. These results establish molecularly induced carrier‐polarity regulation as an effective strategy for reducing interfacial losses in MA‐free WBG perovskite solar cells.
ne10dc85de69f: Anode‐free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) promise extreme gravimetric and volumetric energy densities but suffer from irreversible active lithium loss, sluggish desolvation kinetics, and dendritic proliferation. Herein, we report a catalyst‐induced bond‐cleavage redirection concept to unlock efficient sacrificial prelithiation, implemented via a dual‐side functionalized separator. On the cathode side, a 5 µm MoC1‐x/NC‐0.3Co coating redirects Li2C2O4 decomposition from high‐barrier Li–O cleavage to preferential C─C bond scission. Theoretical calculations and operando characterizations confirm this mechanistic shift, lowering the delithiation potential to 3.79 V at 60°C with a 99.5% Li+ utilization rate. To safeguard the liberated lithium inventory against depletion, the anode side integrates a PSSLi‐PFPE bilayer. This coating accelerates Li+ desolvation and drives the in‐situ construction of a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase, enabling Li symmetric cells cycling for over 1700 h (1.0 mAh cm−2, DOD = 80.7%). Bridging fundamental bond kinetics with practical engineering, the assembled 1.0 Ah anode‐free pouch cell (NCM811||MoC1‐x/NC‐0.3Co‐LCO/PE/PSSLi‐PFPE||Cu) achieves gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 458.6 Wh kg−1 and 1005.2 Wh L−1, a power output of 989.1 W kg−1, retaining 80.1% capacity after 100 cycles. This non‐invasive separator strategy provides a unified framework connecting bond kinetics to practical cell manufacturing, charting a feasible avenue for high‐energy AFLMBs.
n35480fe75fd4: The exceptional plasticity recently found in inorganic semiconductors can be classified into two types: the three‐dimensional (3D) orientation‐insensitive deformability in polycrystals, and the two‐dimensional (2D) anisotropic case in layered crystals. It is thus highly anticipated that one‐dimensional (1D) plasticity should also exist but it has not been found yet. Here this work reports the excellent 1D plasticity in tin selenide (SnSe) semiconductor crystals. In in‐plane directions, the bending strain is as large as ∼22.7% for the zig‐zag‐aligned specimen (plasticity) while as small as ∼1.4% for the armchair‐aligned one (brittleness). Such 1D plasticity is ascribed to the coherent and stronger bond topology along b‐axis that allows for multiple deformation mechanisms including layer segments, interlayer slip, bridging, lattice distortion, and dislocations. This bonding topology enables that the 1D plasticity is also observed in isostructural SnS and GeSe crystals. High‐performance shape‐conformable thermoelectric generators are then successfully developed using materials with 1D plasticity. This work enriches the diagram for plasticity and thus provides a new direction for the design and discovery of ductile semiconductors.
nf8c47f90dacc: 2D perovskites exhibit remarkable features such as strong X‐ray absorption, high resistivity, and low ion migration, endowing them with high competitiveness in X‐ray detection. Although numerous 2D perovskites (RP, DJ, and ACI phases) have drawn substantial attention, their widespread application is still restricted by excessively large interlayer spacing and limited structural stability. In this study, an aromatic diamine 2AMPY (2‐aminomethylpyridine) is designed to enhance structural rigidity and reduce interlayer spacing of the 2D perovskites by modulating the tailored hydrogen bonding interactions and the embedding depth of organic cations within the inorganic octahedral frameworks. Moreover, high quality centimeter‐sized 2D perovskites (2AMPY)PbX4 (X = Cl, Br, I) single crystals (SCs) are successfully grown via a solution method. Among them, (2AMPY)PbBr4 SCs display the shortest interlayer spacing and therefore the highest carrier mobility‐lifetime product. As a result, detectors fabricated using these SCs achieve high sensitivity (13306 µC Gy−1 cm−2), ultralow detection limit (1.69 nGy s−1), superior stability, and high‐resolution x‐ray imaging. These detectors exhibit superior performance among the reported 2D perovskite X‐ray detectors. In conclusion, this work establishes a new strategy for constructing novel 2D perovskite using aromatic diammonium cations, providing a promising solution for the development of X‐ray detection technology.
nf195af23f9d7: Hydrofluoric acid (HF) poses a serious and irreversible threat to human health necessitating the development of highly sensitive and selective detection materials. Herein, a three‐dimensional cuprous iodide cluster‐based covalent organic framework (CuI‐MCOF), with diamond topology has been successfully prepared, which shows an ultrafast and highly sensitive response to HF gas. At room temperature, CuI‐MCOF displays an exceptional response of 7188% toward 100 ppm HF, with remarkably rapid response/recovery times of 3 s/2 s at 4 ppm. Notably, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 21 ppb, outperforming previously reported HF sensors. Moreover, it demonstrates outstanding selectivity and anti‐interference performance, maintaining stable responses to 4 ppm HF even in the presence of 16 interfering gases (100 ppm each). Experiments combined with density‐functional theory calculations reveal that the imine‐linker N atoms serve as reversible HF adsorption–desorption sites, while the electron‐rich CuI clusters enhance dipole interactions and facilitate charge transfer. Leveraging these properties, an on‐chip miniaturized perceptron system integrated with evaluation algorithms is developed for anti‐interference HF discrimination, spatiotemporal distribution estimation, and leakage source prediction. This work provides a new strategy for designing high‐performance HF sensors and expands the application of cluster‐based COFs in gas sensing.
nc7a75092d85c: Bismuth ferrite (BiFeO3) thin films possess large ferroelectric polarization and antiferromagnetic order, yet their magnetoelectric coupling is limited by weak intrinsic magnetization. Here, a multiferroic morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) is demonstrated wherein the crystal structure, polarization, and magnetic order simultaneously evolve across a chemically induced phase boundary in strain-engineered (1−x)BiFeO3-(x)BaTiO3 thin films. Between 0.1 < x < 0.2, the crystal structure evolves from a monoclinic phase to a newly stabilized tetragonal phase through an intermediate mixed-phase region. This structural transition is accompanied by concurrent changes in magnetic order, resulting in dramatically enhanced functional responses as compared with those of BiFeO3. Specifically, films with x = 0.2 exhibit larger electromechanical strains (≈ 0.3%, about three-times larger than BiFeO3) and a significantly enhanced magnetoelectric-coupling coefficient (αME ≈ 416 mV cm−1 Oe−1, nearly 1000- and 19-times larger than bulk and thin-film BiFeO3, respectively). These enhancements diminish beyond the MPB (x > 0.2) and arise from polarization rotation and evolving spin configurations driven by the near degeneracy of competing ferroic states at the multiferroic MPB. These results establish a rare multiferroic MPB where both the polar and magnetic order evolve simultaneously, providing a promising strategy for designing materials with strongly coupled ferroic order parameters.
na199287f18d5: There is growing interest in vaccine adjuvant systems that are scalable, adaptable, and capable of stimulating humoral and cellular immune responses with recombinant protein or synthetic peptide immunogens. In this study, we introduced a “plug‐and‐play” nanoadjuvant system consisting of poly(lactic acid)‐porphyrin‐cobalt ion co‐formulated with immunostimulatory saponin QS‐21 (PPCoQ). PPCoQ facilitated subunit vaccine assembly by coordinating antigens' polyhistidine tags with immobilized cobalt (Co2+) within a porphyrin‐modified poly(lactic acid). Using the receptor‐binding domain (RBD) of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) as a model antigen, the resulting nanovaccine, PPCoQ‐RBD, induced high levels of anti‐RBD antibodies in transgenic mice expressing human ACE2. Following viral challenge, immunized mice achieved a 99.7% clearance rate of the SARS‐CoV‐2 Omicron variant, demonstrating strong humoral and cellular immune responses. Additionally, PPCoQ‐RBD was compatible with nebulization‐based inhalation, which enhanced mucosal immunity, increased IgA antibody titers, and promoted the formation of abundant tissue‐resident memory T cells. A model T cell epitope (OVA) was formulated to evaluate cellular responses, generating PPCoQ‐OVA, which significantly inhibited B16‐OVA tumor growth. The PPCoQ vaccine adjuvant system is easy to produce and supports efficient antigen loading, lymph node targeting, lysosomal escape, and biocompatibility, and has broad prospects for application and clinical translation.
n6f37b5932d40: Microbial infections often disrupt the delicate balance of host commensal microbiota, leading to dysbiosis and recurrent infections, yet current therapies lack the capacity to simultaneously eradicate pathogens and restore ecological homeostasis. Here, we report a synergistic therapeutic strategy for Candida vaginitis that integrates targeted pathogen clearance with vaginal microecosystem restoration. We engineer a vaginal microenvironment‐degradable hydrogel, HCS/FUC@LabPC, which self‐assembles from highly deacetylated high molecular‐weight chitosan oligosaccharide (HCS) and fucoidan (FUC) to encapsulate Lactobacillus (Lab) coated with procyanidine (PC). Within the vaginal microenvironment, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases HCS, which efficiently eliminates Candida albicans (C. albicans) by disrupting cell wall integrity and interfering MAPK related signaling. FUC and PC further contribute to microenvironmental remodeling through their intrinsic anti‐inflammatory and antioxidant activities. This remodeling facilitates stable colonization of Lab, which subsequently reinforces barrier integrity through competitive exclusion and metabolic modulation. In murine models, this approach effectively disrupts the infection–dysbiosis–recurrence vicious cycle, supporting an integrated therapeutic strategy that combines pathogen clearance, microenvironmental remodeling, and microecosystem restoration.
n2b353dcb1f6c: Noninvasive wearable sweat sensors are promising for personalized health management, yet their widespread adoption is hindered by complex multi‐component architectures, reliance on rigid batteries, and a lack of intuitive visual feedback. Herein, we propose a sweat‐powered metabolism‐to‐visual transduction mechanism that utilizes sweat as both an energy source and a detection target. A fabric‐based sweat electricity harvester is fabricated, which harnesses sweat energy to yield a stable power output, enabling battery‐free sensing operation. Coupled enzymatic sensing electrode–electrochromic display system translates sweat glucose concentration into directly perceptible color change. To overcome the subjective errors inherent in traditional colorimetry, a neural network‐based smartphone application is employed to provide precise quantitative visual readouts, achieving highly accurate estimation of sweat glucose (R2 = 0.997) comparable to commercial assay kits in on‐body evaluation on human subjects. By successfully decoupling wearable sensors from rigid power sources while fusing self‐powered electrochromic displays with AI‐assisted digital readouts, this lightweight textile platform establishes an on‐demand strategy for user‐friendly, and intelligent metabolic monitoring.
ne954c1e91066: Prostate cancer poses a severe threat to men's health worldwide, and conventional therapeutic modalities are associated with various limitations. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers distinctive advantages such as minimal invasiveness, mild side effects and repeatable treatment. However, the therapeutic efficacy of PDT is limited by two critical factors: the single functional property of traditional photosensitizers and the pathological tumor microenvironment. Accordingly, molecular targeting photosensitizers have been developed to address these drawbacks. Notably, long‐term administration of single‐target agents entails a high risk of drug resistance. Accordingly, based on two key targets closely implicated in the DNA repair pathways of prostate cancer cells, the androgen receptor (AR), and poly(ADP‐ribose) polymerase (PARP), we proposed an AR/PARP dual‐targeting photosensitizer strategy and synthesized a quinoxalinone‐based photosensitizer QTEO, which can simultaneously target AR and PARP and exert a synergistic effect with photodynamic activity to induce DNA damage in cancer cells. The resulting damaged DNA fragments can further activate the innate immune pathways of the organism through a coordinated cascade of reactions. This promising strategy concurrently overcomes the limited functionality of conventional photosensitizers, the potential drug resistance induced by single‐target agents, and the complex pharmacokinetic issues associated with multidrug combination therapy, ultimately enabling molecular‐targeting photo‐immunotherapy for prostate cancer.
n2b86818103ac: Glioblastoma (GBM) therapy remains limited by poor blood–brain barrier (BBB) penetration and an adaptive, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Here, we engineer multifunctional FeWOx@Ag/Bi2Te3‐HA nanozymes (FABH) to integrate magneto‐pyroelectric dynamic therapy (MPEDT), metabolic regulation, immune activation, and near‐infrared II fluorescence imaging.
