Notably, the ligand functions as an organo-mediator to assist alkyl halide activation and prevent the over-reduction of substrates. This protocol is distinguished by its broad substrate scope, scalability, and mild reaction conditions.
n2c136e03ac1b: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) are generally considered C1-selective in CO2/CO electroreduction, as spatially isolated sites cannot efficiently sustain adjacent CO-derived intermediates required for C─C coupling. Here we show that this selectivity bias is not intrinsic to atomically dispersed Cu, but depends on single-atom site density. Across a series of Cu–N3O catalysts with different Cu site densities, increasing site density drives a clear selectivity crossover from H2 and CH4 formation to C2+ products. The total C2+ Faradaic efficiency (FE) rises from 9.6% on the low-density to 78.1% on the high-density at 1 bar CO, and further reaches 87.7% at 7 bar CO, whereas the low-density remains C1-selective. In situ attenuated-total-reflection surface enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that dense Cu single atoms sustain a larger *COatop population and simultaneously shift interfacial water from strongly hydrogen-bonded species towards free-water-rich configurations. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that higher site density stabilizes CO-containing surface states and lowers the barrier of the acetate-forming pathway. These findings identify a CO-rich and proton-accessible interfacial state that favors C─C coupling over C1 hydrogenation, establishing site density as a structural descriptor for multicarbon electrosynthesis on single-atom catalysts.
n5037ea9f1f9d: Sluggish charge dynamics and poor *NO polarization at active sites hinder the efficiency of photocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia (PcNRA). To address these issues, an atomic-level regulation strategy synergizing facet engineering with axial coordination was developed. Specifically, isolated Cu sites were anchored onto an electron-rich, ultrathin BiVO4 substrate exposing (040) facets. Functionalized ligands featuring distinct donor heteroatoms (S, N, O) were then systematically introduced, yielding a series of single-atom catalysts (S/N/O-Cu/BVO) with tailored axial microenvironments. A comprehensive methodology combining multidimensional spectroscopy and computational chemistry was established to verify this single-atom axial coordination. Detailed analyses of characteristic binding energies and absorption edge shifts via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and synchrotron X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) identified localized coordination field effects. Crucially, these effects are distinct from conventional electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI), providing spectroscopic confirmation of successful axial ligand incorporation and guiding the prediction of their configurations. Building upon these spectral findings, density functional theory (DFT) models were constructed and optimized, conclusively validating the asymmetric axial coordination configurations within the system, specifically Cu-S2O1, Cu-N2O1, and Cu-O4. Catalytic evaluations demonstrated that S-Cu/BVO achieves the highest ammonia yield at 435 μmol·h–1·g–1. In-situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations elucidated the multidimensional synergistic mechanism driving this enhanced activity: (1) The prominently exposed (040) facets act as an interfacial electron sink, efficiently directing photogenerated electrons toward the Cu sites; (2) The axial S ligands reconstruct the electronic structure of the Cu centers via strong orbital coupling, thereby improving effective orbital overlap with nitrate; (3) The resulting asymmetric Cu-NO-S bridging configuration polarizes the critical *NO intermediate, substantially lowering the kinetic barrier for the rate-determining step.
nb4ac1e412542: The article explores the catalytic potential of the emerging class of Janus-type di-N-heterocyclic carbenes that have attracted attention in recent times. The article details different aspects of these Janus-type di-N-heterocyclic carbenes particularly from their classifications, expansion in synthesis approaches, to finally their utility in different homogeneous transformations.
n2515ce2b234a: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has revealed many possible Li-induced interfacial reactions in solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but most in situ studies form Li|electrolyte interfaces through non-electrochemical Li deposition, including evaporation, sputtering, or electron-beam-induced deposition. These routes may introduce additional energy that activates reaction pathways not accessed during electrochemical Li plating. Here, we use lab-based operando XPS to directly evaluate oxide solid-state electrolyte stability during electrochemical Li formation. Using this approach, we find sharply different responses for two representative oxide SSEs: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2–x(PO4)3 (LATP) is reduced upon Li plating, forming a Li+/Ti3+-rich mixed-conducting interphase that partially relaxes through coupled ionic–electronic redistribution, whereas garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) shows no spectroscopically resolvable Zr or La reduction. This work represents the first direct operando XPS evaluation of SSE stability against electrochemically plated Li metal.
n80c758399425: Management of disparate chronic epithelial diseases relies on fragmented site-specific protocols yet remains hindered by common pathological barriers and sustained inflammation. Herein, we developed a top-down strategy to exfoliate short nanofibrils from Antheraea pernyi silk fibers featuring inherent Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD) motifs, followed by in situ growth of Au nanoparticles. The resulting platform (Au@ASFs) achieved superior spatial adaptability via catalytic oxygen propulsion, navigating across barriers to reach deep-seated lesions. Once localized, Au@ASFs provided phase-spanning multifunctional therapy through near-infrared (NIR)-triggered photothermal sterilization. Through RGD–integrin interactions, they also promoted hemostasis and M2 macrophage polarization to resolve persistent inflammation while enhancing fibroblast migration, angiogenesis, and neuronal differentiation. In vivo, Au@ASFs (+NIR) significantly improved closure of infected diabetic oral ulcers from 43.1 to 95.5% by day 7 and restored colon length in ulcerative colitis from 66.3 to 97.7% of healthy controls. In infected diabetic wounds, Au@ASFs (+NIR) increased closure from 63.8 to 89.1% by day 14. Transcriptomic analysis of wound tissues revealed reprogramming through suppressed NF-κB inflammatory signaling, activated Wnt5a/GSK-3β signaling for neuronal differentiation, and modulated PI3K-Akt signaling for tissue regeneration. Collectively, Au@ASF (+NIR) consistently resolves chronic epithelial diseases across disparate anatomical sites, establishing a unified drug-free paradigm that transcends site-specific constraints.
n6bfe06cebdf4: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is driven by amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation and a cascade of interconnected neurotoxic events, including oxidative stress, glutamate excitotoxicity, calcium dysregulation, and impaired neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling. To address the multifactorial nature of AD pathology, chiral d- or l-cysteine-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) nanoparticles are developed as a multitarget nanotherapeutic platform. Both enantiomers effectively inhibit Aβ aggregation, scavenge reactive oxygen species, reduce extracellular glutamate levels, and attenuate calcium dysregulation. In parallel, d/l-Cys-COFs rescue compromised neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling, as evidenced by normalized expression of neuropeptide Y and brain-derived neurotrophic factor. In transgenic AD mice, d/l-Cys-COF treatment significantly improves memory and cognitive performance. Notably, the d-enantiomer affords superior neuroprotection through enhanced suppression of pathological intracellular calcium overload, whereas restoration of neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling remains chirality-independent. These findings identify chirality as a key design element for multitarget nanotherapeutics against AD, with enantioselective efficacy arising primarily from differential regulation of calcium dysregulation and shared restoration of neuroactive signaling contributing to the overall therapeutic benefit.
nc14d1c48363d: Giant optical nonlinearities enable advanced materials control and bridge exotic light-matter phenomena to next-generation photonics. However, materials exhibiting strong higher-order optical nonlinearity beyond the second order are typically rare. Here, we report the discovery of a giant and ultrafast second-harmonic generation (SHG) in self-assembled polar skyrmions under mid-infrared excitations. The transient SHG intensity exhibits a distinctive power dependence originating from higher-order nonlinearity. More generally, we show that large higher-order nonlinearity emerges across diverse domain structures in polar superlattices. Phase-field simulations demonstrate a strong and periodic local permittivity variation within each polar texture at equilibrium, and further confirm the fast polarization oscillation in polar skyrmions with mid-infrared excitations. This intense local permittivity modulation can satisfy epsilon-near-zero conditions, unlocking dramatically enhanced nonlinear optical responses without photonic engineering. Consequently, the self-assembled polar topologies with strong inherent optical nonlinearity could establish a platform for quantum information processing and high-speed optical communications.
n9cadf3617cd8: Weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels are emerging as a versatile platform for ion transport and separation, desalination, and energy applications. However, a predictive understanding of how dynamic charge regulation at the nanoscopic scale influences ionic mobility in these polymer networks remains elusive. Here, using large-scale molecular simulations, we dissect the coupled mechanisms governing small-ion transport in weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels, and reveal how charge density, competitive binding, and dynamic charge regulation jointly control ion mobility. By systematically isolating these effects, we uncover a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence of ion self-diffusion on hydrogel pKa and salt concentration for multivalent ions. Strikingly, allowing the hydrogel backbone to dynamically regulate its charge eliminates this nonmonotonicity and leads to dramatic enhancements in ion mobility, with diffusion coefficients increasing by more than a factor of 2 for trivalent ions. We attribute this effect to a protonation-assisted hopping mechanism that continuously remodels the local electrostatic landscape, providing an additional molecular-scale pathway for ion unbinding beyond translational escape and accelerating ion-pair kinetics without affecting the fraction of free ions. Our results demonstrate that dynamic nanoscale charge regulation can decouple ion mobility from equilibrium binding strength, offering a powerful design lever unavailable in fixed-charge materials. Building upon these insights, we propose simple molecular design principles for next-generation ion-conducting hydrogels and suggest alternative strategies for nanostructured membranes, energy materials, and biologically inspired charge-adaptive soft matter.
ncf528759a6ea: The deterministic realization of quantum light sources operating at telecom wavelengths is essential for long-distance fiber-based quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. In this work, we demonstrate that telecom O-band emission can be achieved from site-controlled InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots (QDs). Our concept utilizes a buried AlAs/AlOx stressor layer with the unique feature of inducing a well-defined and controllable tensile strain field at the growth surface, enabling both site-selective nucleation at the mesa’s centers and a redshift of QD emission to the ∼1.3 μm wavelength range. This concept not only eliminates the need for strain-reducing layers (SRLs), which are known to degrade optical coherence, but also provides spatial control and spectral tunability. The grown telecom QDs show single-photon emission with g(2)(0) = (5.0 ± 1.0) × 10–2 at 4 K and (2.8 ± 0.3) × 10–1 at 77 K, demonstrating the quantum nature and thermal stability of the emitters. The emission characteristics of complex excitonic states are analyzed using 8-band k·p and configuration-interaction modeling, which quantitatively reproduces the experimental observations. Finally, we present a theory-supported strategy to further redshift the emission toward the center of the O-band and beyond by employing a multiburied stressor approach. This combined framework of experiment and theory establishes the buried stressor concept as a scalable route toward highly coherent, position-controlled O-band quantum emitters compatible with scalable photonic integration.
n2d3fc4f248f9: Enantioselective chiroptical sensing is gaining traction across various applications. However, intrinsic molecular chiroptical responses are weak, and existing amplification approaches add synthesis, manufacturing, or operational complexity that limits sensitivity and scalability. Here, we present an enantioselective sensing paradigm merging adsorption-driven chirality induction with large-scale optical transduction in twisted stacks of aligned carbon nanotube (CNT) films. Chiral molecules adsorb onto CNTs to form chiroptically active composites that are macroscopically assembled by alignment and rotational stacking, yielding large ultraviolet circular dichroism (CD). We resolve enantiomer handedness and quantify concentration in single-enantiomer aqueous solutions using a single sensor without lithography, hotspot delivery, or a paired opposite-handed reference. We achieve high sensitivity with estimated sub-μM minimum detectable concentrations for glucose and provide a proof-of-concept demonstration with alanine. Neither analyte-only solution shows detectable CD under the present measurement conditions. We demonstrate Langmuir-type adsorption behavior using molecular dynamics simulations and reproduce experimental results using optical simulations. This platform provides a foundation for future development toward cost-effective in situ enantiomer monitoring in aqueous environments.
nd51d3b5660cb: In this work, we report the synthesis of highly active non-noble metal catalysts with controlled nanoparticle size and dispersion through a new catalyst preparation strategy combining the continuous-flow synthesis of...
n7b345d81f501: The results demonstrate that aqueous NH 3 can be thermocatalytically decomposed to H 2 and N 2 at these comparatively mild temperatures.
n8a4a4ea5188b: 5-Hydroxy-2(5 H )-furanone (HFO) emerges as a versatile bio-based platform chemical, combining renewable accessibility, rich multifunctional reactivity, asymmetric synthesis potential, and routes to high-value chemicals and sustainable materials alike.
ne7d878d963e8: Icosahedral carboranes have extensive applications owing to their unique properties. This review summarizes advances in the mechanistic study of transition metal-catalyzed carborane cage B–H activation and functionalization.
n7b2d3ede544f: Vanadium-based thiophosphates in the MPQ3/M2P2Q6 family provide an unusual platform for coupling mixed-metal valence, metal vacancies, and 2D magnetism, but access to phase-pure multimetal solid solutions with verified chemical homogeneity remains limited. Here, we show that multication alloying provides a route to incorporating V into layered thiophosphates while retaining the mixed-valent, vacancy-containing character of V2−xP2S6. This approach yields Fe1.25V0.6P2S6, Ni1.25V0.6P2S6, Co1.25V0.6P2S6, and high-entropy V-containing compositions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (scXRD) and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping confirm formation of layered single-phase alloys and chemical uniformity both across the surface and through the flake thickness. Optical measurements show semiconducting band gaps spanning ∼1.33−1.66 eV, while temperature-dependent transport reveals markedly enhanced conductivity and low activation energies (∼0.2−0.3 eV) relative to conventional divalent TM2P2S6 analogs. Oxidation-state mapping indicates robust mixed-valent V2+/V3+ character consistent with defect-assisted hopping and self-doping linked to vanadium vacancies, likely causing enhanced conductivity. Magnetic measurements further show composition-dependent behavior, consistent with magnetic frustration and glassy components in Fe1.25V0.6P2S6 and (VMnFeCoNi)2P2S6, highlighting the role of multimetal disorder in shaping exchange interactions. Together, these results establish a route to phase-pure, conductive V-containing thiophosphate alloys and expand the tunable design space for coupled transport and magnetism in layered chalcophosphates.
n110c822b7b03: Two Zn(II)-based mixed-ligand metal−organic frameworks (MOFs) were synthesised using solvothermal methods and fully characterized (SCXRD, PXRD, TGA, DSC, FTIR, HSM). The MOFs are formulated as [Zn2(NDC)2(AzPy)2]n˙n(DMF)3 (ZNA150-DMF) and [Zn(NDC)(AzPy)0.5]n˙n(DMF)0.5 (ZNA90-DMF), where NDC2− = 2,6-naphthalene dicarboxylate, AzPy = 4,4′-azopyridine and DMF = N,N′-dimethylformamide, and are synthesized at 150 °C and 90 °C, respectively. Single crystal X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed that ZNA150-DMF and ZNA90-DMF are non-interpenetrated and triply interpenetrated, respectively. Both MOFs are highly flexible, displaying large changes in their unit cell parameters and void space features upon desolvation with the void space of both desolvated forms (ZNA150-act and ZNA90-act) consisting of isolated voids, thus leading to transient porosity, where these isolated pockets temporarily connect into channels to facilitate sorption. ZNA90-act carbon dioxide sorption isotherms have inflection points indicating a pressure-sustained structural change, as proven by variable-pressure single crystal and powder X-ray diffraction studies on ZNA90-act immersed in a CO2 gas environment. Variable-temperature single crystal X-ray diffraction studies on both activated MOFs, in the absence of gas, show that these are highly flexible, displaying colossal thermal expansion properties with changes in void space features. These changes tend towards what was observed for ZNA90-act under CO2 pressure, thus possibly linking flexible MOF behavior under the two sets of conditions.
na063f64bb8cf: Copper nanoparticles (Cu NPs) have a broad applicability, yet their synthesis is sensitive to subtle changes in reaction parameters. This sensitivity, combined with the time- and resource-intensive nature of experimental optimization, poses a major challenge in achieving reproducible and size-controlled synthesis. While machine learning (ML) shows promise in materials research, its application is often limited by scarcity of large high-quality experimental data sets. This study explores ML to predict the DLS-derived hydrodynamic diameter of Cu NPs from microwave-assisted polyol synthesis using a small data set of 25 in-house performed syntheses. Latin hypercube sampling is used to efficiently cover the parameter space while creating the experimental data set. Ensemble regression models successfully predict hydrodynamic diameters with good predictive performance given the limited data set. Since quantitative regression requires a unique DLS-derived hydrodynamic diameter, the regression model is restricted to monomodal DLS distributions, while a complementary classification model identifies synthesis conditions for which quantitative prediction is applicable. Using equivalent out-of-sample validation (OOB and LOOCV), the ML and DoE models showed comparable generalization (MAE = 40.92 and 40.46 nm, respectively). The final ensemble model achieved an R2 of 0.74, an MAE of 23.81 nm, compared to an R2 of 0.60, an MAE of 33.54 nm for the DoE model, while retaining the complete synthesis parameter space, making it better suited for synthesis guidance. Additionally, classification models using both random forests and large language models (LLMs) are evaluated to distinguish between large and small particles. These classification models exhibited only modest predictive performance, indicating that this small data set is insufficient to fully exploit the capabilities of complex LLMs. Overall, this study demonstrates that carefully curated small data sets, paired with robust classical ML, can effectively support the synthesis of Cu NPs and highlights that for lab-scale studies, complex models like LLMs may offer limited benefits. The validation experiments further indicate the potential of ML guided synthesis to improve the efficiency of experimental optimization and reduce resource consumption.
neb882bc2452f: Transition metal (TM) dissolution from the cathode and deposition on the anode in lithium−ion batteries is a key degradation mechanism, yet its spatial distribution in commercial cylindrical automotive-grade cells remains insufficiently understood. In this study on lithium−ion cells 18650 with a NMC811/graphite technology, we reveal a pronounced radial inhomogeneity in cathode metal deposition on the anode, with significantly higher accumulation in the inner windings of the jelly roll compared to the outer regions, identifying a critical vulnerability in the cell design while operating in overvoltage conditions. Spatially resolved near-edge edge X-ray absorption fine structure measurements further highlight this geometry dependence, revealing a higher fraction of Ni4+ in the inner windings, whereas the outer regions are dominated by Ni2+. This radial gradient correlates with intrinsic geometric characteristics of cylindrical cells, where the smaller bending radius in the inner windings may plausibly contribute to elevated mechanical stress, higher compressive pressure, and reduced heat dissipation in the cell core. The findings directly link cell geometry to both the extent and chemical state of TM deposition, proving its central role in degradation processes.
n5d32910bbb3b: Defect passivation and crystallization regulation are critical for achieving efficient and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, developing a single additive capable of simultaneously optimizing energy-level alignment, suppressing ion migration,...
n3366e6e80a3f: Cost-effective Li2ZrCl6 halides with regulated configurational complexity combine rapid lithium-ion conduction with ultralow electronic conductivity and superior oxidative stability. A robust zirconium oxychloride cathode-electrolyte interphase is formed during cycling, enabling 4.4 V all-solid-state LiNi0.85Co0.1Mn0.05O2 batteries to operate for up to 3,700 cycles.
n2948bef3ea14: Why does corrosion attack specific sites under some conditions but spread uniformly under others? Liang et al. combine real-time nanoscale imaging with atomistic simulations to show that corrosion reflects a competition between local structural heterogeneity and thermodynamic driving force. Near equilibrium, strained regions preferentially corrode and promote localized pitting; far from equilibrium, stronger driving forces overwhelm these local differences and produce rapid, uniform corrosion. The findings provide a framework for understanding and controlling localized material degradation.
n167c83bc2fce: Stable α-FAPbI3 is promising for high-performance X-ray imaging but is difficult to produce without alloying. Here, polymer coordination with PVP enables stable, alloying-free α-FAPbI3 thick films by controlling crystallization and lattice strain. The resulting detectors combine high sensitivity, low-dose operation, and fast response, enabling high-resolution, real-time X-ray imaging.
nbae76d4a1ad5: Photodetection and neuromorphic computing promises sensing at the edge, yet most optoelectronic synapses lack spectral breadth or scalable silicon integration. Here we report a dual-gate synaptic transistor integrating colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) with a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) channel in a complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible platform. This architecture synergistically combines the SOI channel for efficient charge transport and signal amplification with the CQD layer serving a dual role as a broadband absorber (300–1700 nm) and a charge-trap medium. The device exhibits a responsivity of 639 A W–1 and specific detectivity exceeding 3 × 1012 Jones at 1550 nm, parallelly emulating short- and long-term plasticity, multilevel conductance tuning, and highly programmable synaptic dynamics. The top gate enables reversible potentiation and depression, and self-powered operation supports low-power sensing and light-driven learning. We demonstrate system-level utility in a synaptic array that achieves pattern recognition with peak accuracy exceeding 96%, establishing a pathway to silicon-integrated, energy-efficient neuromorphic vision.
n926424c53b61: Control and switching of electrical resistance in semiconductors are important for high-performance electronic devices. Here, we realize giant resistance switching in nonequilibrium (Pb1–xSnx)Se films through a reversible structural transition between three-dimensional (3D) rock-salt (RS)-type and two-dimensional (2D) GeS-type phases. The solid-solution films were fabricated by reactive solid-phase epitaxy of SnSe/PbSe bilayers followed by rapid thermal quenching. Se-flux annealing of the PbSe template suppressed Pb precipitation, enabling chemically homogeneous, single-phase nonequilibrium RS-type films up to x = 0.58. Increasing the Sn content from x = 0.43 to 0.58 systematically increased the 2D–3D structural transition temperature and enhanced the resistance switching ratio to 4.9 × 106, far exceeding those of representative transition-metal oxide thin films (∼102–104). The giant resistance switching originates from the nearly complete transformation (∼98%) of the conductive 3D phase into the high-resistance 2D phase. These results establish crystal-dimensionality switching as a promising new mechanism for high-performance electronic switching devices.
n4fc61f4ffe16: The bottom-up construction of functional matter from individually positioned atoms and molecules requires deterministic control over capture, transport, and assembly on surfaces. Although atomic manipulation is well established, extending comparable control to molecules remains challenging due to their complex internal degrees of freedom and surface interactions. Here, we demonstrate controlled single-molecule transport and assembly at liquid nitrogen temperatures using a scanning tunneling microscope. We designed a molecule with an intrinsic electric dipole moment, enabling efficient noncontact manipulation via electrostatic coupling to the tip. This strategy allows stable long-range translation and the programmable formation of defined dimers and larger assemblies. Systematic mapping of the operational parameter space, supported by first-principles calculations, identifies an electrostatic driving mechanism governing motion. Our approach shifts molecular nanomachine research from demonstrations under extreme cryogenic conditions to positional control under experimentally more accessible temperatures, establishing a practical platform for programmable molecular-scale engineering.
n4e2a28b7b9df: Selector-only memory (SOM), which integrates threshold switching and data storage within a chalcogenide layer, is a promising high-density memory technology, yet the regulation of memory characteristics and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that programming current (Ip) regulates the competition between composition-driven and trap-associated switching processes in amorphous In2Te3 devices. Decreasing Ip from 10–2 to 10–4 A reversibly changes the positive-read threshold voltage (Vth) ordering from Vth, SET > Vth, RESET, yielding an inverted memory window of up to 1.53 V, to Vth, SET < Vth, RESET, with a conventional memory window of ∼0.5 V. Cross-sectional energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy reveals state-dependent In/Te redistribution at high Ip, consistent with composition-mediated modulation of conductive pathways. At low Ip, atomic redistribution is suppressed and trap-associated transport modulation is enhanced, with extracted trap depths of 0.51 eV (SET) and 0.63 eV (RESET), establishing Ip as a means of modifying SOM memory characteristics without complex engineering.
n96da882cf35f: Structural deformation of crystal lattices has emerged as a powerful pathway to engineer and boost electronic properties through lattice geometry. However, realizing ultrafine structural modulations remains challenging without external strain imposed by substrates, prestrain, or artificial patterning. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy, we show that the cleaving process spontaneously induces nanoscale wiggling in 1T′-WTe2 without such external strain sources. Furthermore, scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals pronounced electronic reconstruction and spatially resolved spectral modulations between the top and valley regions of the wiggling. Combined with first-principles calculations, our results show that this wiggling substantially modifies the local electronic structure relative to the unstrained flat region, suggesting electronic structure reconstruction driven by spontaneous lattice deformation. These findings establish spontaneous nanoscale wiggling as a self-formed structural modulation for local electronic-structure engineering in strain-sensitive low-symmetry layered materials.
ncb9bb6ea46e2: Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) moiré bilayers have realized a wide range of strongly correlated and topological phenomena. The physics in these materials is often sensitive to the interlayer stacking order. Polarization-resolved optical second harmonic generation (SHG) is the most used technique for stacking order characterization but unverified for most heterobilayers. Here we calibrate the optical SHG for angle-aligned MoTe2/WSe2 bilayers by the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). We directly compare the transport and magnetic properties and the electronic phase diagram for two distinct stacking orders. With the calibrated stacking order assignment, we clarify the interpretation of earlier results, including the nature of the Chern insulator, mechanism of an electric-field-tuned metal–insulator transition at half band filling, and the Kondo lattice physics. Our work provides a consistent picture of the relation between the stacking order and the electronic properties of MoTe2/WSe2 moiré bilayers.
n3e1139421df5: Regioselective esterification remains challenging, particularly when multiple alcohol groups with similar reactivity are present. Now it has been shown that aldehyde dehydrogenases can be engineered into oxidative ester synthases with programmable alcohol selectivity, enabling controlled ester bond formation through active-site remodelling.
n6d736a7dfb83: Enantioselective dual catalysis represents a powerful strategy for the preparation of functionally dense optically active compounds. Photocatalysis, paired with organocatalysis, undeniably represents a popular choice that takes advantage of radical and polar reactivity for crafting challenging bonds. Despite the interest in this methodology, the detailed analysis of the effects governing selectivity between the two catalytic cycles has not been extensively studied. Herein, we report a data-driven mechanistic study campaign to disclose the factors that influence the enantioselectivity of a photo-organocatalytic alkylation of indoles. Data science tools were used to generate a virtual library of potential substrates, thus ensuring the selection of a statistically diverse training set. Subsequent multivariate linear regression (MLR) analysis led to the identification of substrate electronic features as the key factor affecting the stereochemical outcome. Moreover, comprehensive mechanistic experiments unveiled the key role of the in situ generated oxindole intermediate that connects the two catalytic cycles in determining the observed selectivity. These findings lay the foundation for developing asymmetric dual catalytic transformations of synthetic relevance and provide a general platform for interrogating other complex catalytic systems.
n24becfd2d7f7: Quaternary stereocenters on densely functionalized furanoside frameworks are challenging to construct with high chemo-, regio-, and stereocontrol, especially in the presence of nitrogen-containing motifs and multiple downstream diversification handles. Here, we disclose a sequence-programmed three-component radical carboamination of reverse exo-glycals that provides modular access to C4-quaternary furanosides through a distinct radical retrosynthetic logic. In this photoredox process, an N-centered radical adds to an electron-rich reverse exo-glycal to form a pseudo-anomeric radical, which is then intercepted by a Giese acceptor, enabling concomitant C–N and C–C bond formation in a single step. The protocol accommodates diverse N-radical precursors and electron-deficient alkenes, is further extendable to distinct pyranose- and furanose-derived reverse exo-glycals, supports late-stage glyco-functionalization of structurally complex molecules, and furnishes a spiro-glycosyl donor on preparative scale. Subsequent Vorbrüggen glycosylation enables divergent entry to structurally distinct spironucleosides. Preliminary biological profiling of these compounds reveals a modest antiviral signal against influenza A (PR8) at 50 μM, supporting the utility of this platform for probing underexplored spironucleoside chemical space. Mechanistic experiments support the proposed photoredox-mediated radical relay, while DFT studies provide a plausible basis for the contrasting reactivity of representative N-radical precursors. Collectively, this work offers a concise and programmable strategy for the synthesis of quaternary-center furanosides and their downstream spirocyclic derivatives from readily available carbohydrate feedstocks.
n2bc15a697016: Bio-oil derived from lignocellulosic biomass represents an alternative to fossil fuels as an energy source and chemical feedstock. Fast pyrolysis of lignocellulosic biomass yields a rich mixture of oxygenated organic species with low energy density and low stability, which can be electrochemically upgraded to increase energy density and stability and produce value-added chemicals. Here, we focus on electrocatalytic hydrotreatment of furfural (FF) and 4-propylphenol (4-PP), two constituents of raw bio-oil. In a binary mixture, the presence of FF has been shown to inhibit the reduction of 4-PP. The underlying mechanisms of these competing reactions are probed using density functional theory (DFT) and experimental electrochemical deposition techniques. The binding energies of FF and 4-PP, as well as their respective reduction products and associated reaction thermodynamics, are examined comparatively on multiple facets of single-crystal platinum and ruthenium catalysts. FF is shown to bind competitively compared to 4-PP, particularly on Pt(111) and Ru(0001), and hydrogenation products such as tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol (THFA) and 4-propylcyclohexanol (4-PCOL) were found to bind less strongly to the surfaces than the reactants. FF reduction side products, including dimers furoin (FUI) and hydrofuroin (HF), were also found to bind competitively with 4-PP. No thermodynamic barriers were observed for FF hydrogenation to THFA, whereas 4-PCOL formation is favored on Pt facets, and propylcyclohexane (PC) formation is favored on Ru. The presence of barriers to 4-PP hydrogenation indicates that FF hydrogenation is thermodynamically favored on Pt and Ru. Further, limiting potential calculations suggest that the FF reduction pathways are generally favorable around 0 V vs. RHE. In contrast, the 4-PP reduction pathways require a more cathodic bias, achieved at potentials less than -0.1 V vs. RHE. The adsorption behavior of FF-derived reduction products on polycrystalline Pt is experimentally validated using a Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM). Such experiments yield estimates of aqueous-phase free energies of adsorption, which are compared with computational results that are correlated to the aqueous phase. Overall, the DFT model results suggest that the observed inhibition of 4-PP by FF is due to competitive adsorption and favorable FF reaction thermodynamics.
ne5f768710e1b: Formamidinium lead iodide (α-FAPbI3) perovskite, despite its ideal bandgap, requires high-temperature (≥150 °C) annealing for the δ-to-α phase transformation, hindering its application in low-temperature processed inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), particularly on flexible substrates. Herein, we demonstrate that the alicyclic Lewis base caprolactam (CPL) effectively drives the complete δ-to-α phase transformation of FAPbI3 at a reduced temperature of 100 °C. Experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that CPL lowers the phase transition energy barrier and retards crystallization kinetics via strong Pb2+ coordination and controlled desorption. This strategy yields highly crystalline, fully phase-converted α-FAPbI3 films with improved morphology, reduced defect densities, and enhanced optoelectronic properties. Consequently, CPL-modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.64% with good operational stability. The low-temperature processability also enables high-performance flexible PSCs with a PCE of 23.73%. This work presents an additive engineering approach for realizing efficient and stable α-FAPbI3 PSCs through low-temperature manufacturing.
nea02888a1208: Ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) metal halide perovskite solar cells are essential for multi-junction solar cells with higher power conversion efficiency (PCE) potentials. In this work, we report the dual functions of 5-iodoisophthalic acid (I-BDC) to suppress phase segregation and uncoordinated Pb2+ related defects to enhance UWBG perovskite cell performance and stability. An I-BDC incorporated 1.95 eV perovskite film exhibited stable photoluminescence after 120 min of illumination. The best I-BDC cell achieved a certified reverse scan PCE of 16.5%, the highest for 1.95 eV perovskite cells to date. These UWBG perovskite solar cells are the most stable reported to date, with one encapsulated device retaining 90% of its initial PCE after 500 h of maximum power point tracking at ∼40 °C and another retaining 95% of its initial PCE after 206 thermal cycles (–40 ↔ 85 °C), passing the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 61215 testing protocols at the cell level.
n712c6d476bae: High-energy batteries require cathodes with greater capacity and specific energy. Ni-rich-layered oxides approach the performance limit of LiNiO2 (LNO), yet its practical use is hindered by severe chemomechanical degradation. Near 4.2 V, the H2-H3/H4 transition drives substantial c-axis contraction, volume shrinkage, O1 formation, oxygen loss, and rapid capacity decay. Here, we show that only 5% cobalt-free complex concentrated doping stabilizes LNO without sacrificing energy density. The modified LNO reduces c-axis strain from 7.4 to 2.1%, exhibits near-zero-strain behavior, and delivers 258 mAh•g–1 and 973 Wh•kg–1. In pouch cells, it retains 80% capacity after 1800 cycles and shows markedly improved thermal stability. These results demonstrate that complex-concentrated doping at low dopant loading can suppress strain and phase transformations at the full-Ni limit, providing a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing high-energy intercalation electrodes while preserving their intrinsic capacity and specific energy during prolonged electrochemical cycling.
n230e941a234c: In this work, we report an innovative interface engineering strategy combining bidirectional chemical anchoring and electronic bridging via a 2D reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and MXene conductive network. This hierarchical 2D structure suppresses the aggregation and stacking of single-layer MXene nanosheets while mutually compensating for individual charge transport limitations. Specifically, the abundant functional groups passivate interfacial defects (Pb2+ and I–) and bond with the PCBM layer via coordination, hydrogen bonding and π–π interactions. This synergistic architecture lowers the electron energy offset. Consequently, PSCs incorporating the rGO-MXene interlayer achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.96% (certified 25.05%) and retain 96.43% of initial efficiency after 1000 h in ambient air. Furthermore, 10 × 10 cm2 large-area PSM yields a high PCE of 20.25%, maintaining 96.05% of initial efficiency under maximum power point tracking for 963 h.
n71e7113fddbe: Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites with multiquantum-well structures hold great potential for light-emitting diodes (LEDs) due to their cascaded energy funnels, yet their performance is hampered by defect-rich low-n phases and disordered crystallization. Here, we present a phase-homogenization strategy that combines a self-adaptive solvent by doping ethyl acetate (EA) with dimethyl phosphonate (DPP), which simultaneously modulates the polarity and evaporation kinetics of EA, guiding the crystal growth and phase distribution of quasi-2D perovskites. The strong coordination of DPP with Pb2+ also passivates deep-level traps, thereby drastically reducing nonradiative low-n-phase recombination. We further use the bridging molecules to enhance perovskite/transport layer interfaces by incorporating sodium 4-amino-1-naphthalenesulfonate tetrahydrate (SANT) into the PEDOT/PSS hole transport layer, which weakens PEDOT–PSS electrostatic attraction, enhancing conductivity while reducing acid-induced corrosion of the ITO electrode and perovskite film. SANT also templates perovskite nucleation via its functional groups, promoting ordered crystallite growth. Overall, the resulting green-emitting quasi-2D perovskite LEDs achieve a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 32.81% (average 30.74%) and a luminance of 44338 cd m–2, with a lower surface temperature during operation. Moreover, the devices exhibit a 10-fold enhancement in operational stability compared to the control counterparts. Our findings provide a strategy for combining crystallization control and interface passivation in quasi-2D PeLEDs.
nda6c3061d507: Many applications for shape-controlled metal nanoparticles require their immobilization on a surface, creating a need for development of direct substrate-based synthesis routes for increasingly complex materials. Colloidal chemical syntheses for shape-controlled nanoparticles are common, but transferring insight from synthesis in solution to growth on a substrate requires accounting for significant differences in reagent diffusion between these two growth environments─a nontrivial challenge. In the present work, we establish fundamental principles for rationally adapting reaction parameters from colloidal syntheses to electrodeposition such that the growth of nanoparticles on the electrode proceeds under comparable reagent diffusion conditions to those that drive shape direction during colloidal growth. To demonstrate these principles, we successfully translate reaction conditions from colloidal synthesis to electrodeposition for a series of dilute bimetallic (silver) gold nanoparticles whose shapes are controlled by surface deposition of silver: concave cubes, octahedra, rhombic dodecahedra, truncated ditetragonal prisms, and tetrahexahedra. By comparing open-circuit potential measurements of the colloidal syntheses with chronopotentiometry measurements from galvanostatic electrodeposition, we determine the adjustments required to establish ideal growth kinetics for each electrodeposition. We identify specific synthetic handles─mode of mass transport, surfactant concentration, applied current density, and secondary metal concentration─required to modulate reagent transport to the electrode surface, as well as the direction they must be modified so that the relative rates of silver and gold ion reduction mimic colloidal growth. These generalizable synthetic parameters for controlling reagent diffusion and concentrations near the electrode surface open possibilities for the electrodeposition of complex multimetallic and shaped nanomaterials.
na1b5b1534ba4: The morphology and microenvironment of ion-conducting polymers (ionomers) on the catalyst electrode surface critically govern the CO2 electrocatalytic performance. Herein, we report a dual-reconstruction strategy that synergistically tailors the surface structure of the Nafion ionomer using positively charged molecules and solvent effect. By combining a low-dielectric-constant solvent (isopropanol) with arginine cations, the optimized electrode achieves an 83.6% Faradaic efficiency for multicarbon (C2+) products at a high current density of –500 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH. Based on experimental characterization and MD simulations, we propose a structural model in which the Nafion side chains are oriented away from both the catalyst surface and the electrolyte phase. In situ spectroscopic analyses, theoretical calculation, and experimental evidence suggest that this structural reorganization disrupts the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network, suppresses the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, improves effective gaseous CO2 accessibility, and facilitates C–C coupling along an energetically favorable *OC–COH pathway. This work provides valuable insights into microenvironment engineering of ionomer–catalyst interfaces for efficient CO2 electrolysis.
n5331d089401a: Polyolefin hydrocracking over Brønsted acidic ZSM-5 produces light hydrocarbons with narrow product distributions, but further increases in propane and butane selectivity are required to improve process economics and sustainability. Here, we examined the effect of various metal and metal oxide dopants, namely Pt, Pt-Sn, SnOx, ZnOx, and GaOx, on ZSM-5-mediated polyolefin hydrocracking and identified GaOx as a selective promoter for light gas formation. Incorporation of gallium oxide (3 wt % Ga) was shown to increase propane selectivity from 40 c-wt %, achieved over ZSM-5, to near 60 c-wt %, reaching a combined propane and butane selectivity of 85 c-wt %, while maintaining solids conversion. To elucidate the role of gallium oxide, we used ex situ and operando characterization techniques to probe acidity, local coordination environment, and the spatial distribution of GaOx species. Extra-framework gallium oxide introduced via incipient wetness impregnation reduced the measured acid site density from 1275 to 911 μmol g–1, decreased the Brønsted/Lewis acid site ratio, and formed a high-coverage GaOx layer on the external surface of the zeolite. Operando experiments show that Ga is present in both Ga3+ and Ga1+ under reaction conditions. Attempts to disperse gallium oxide through reductive pretreatments led to an increase in the Lewis acid site concentration and a 10 c-wt % decrease in propane selectivity, highlighting the importance of the specific location, structural, and acidic configurations. Systematic variation of impregnation methods to control location and dispersion revealed a synergistic interaction between gallium oxide and zeolite acid sites, with propane selectivity strongly influenced by spatial proximity of GaOx to acid sites. Furthermore, vapor-phase flow reactions with a model compound demonstrated a decrease in intermediate product formation compared to the zeolite alone. The optimized catalyst was validated across diverse polyolefin substrates and resulted in similar increases to propane selectivity, yielding >80 c-wt % combined C3–C4 selectivity across the range of polyolefin substrates.
n5473a6afe684: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) requires anode catalysts that sustain acidic oxygen evolution in practical stacks with minimal noble-metal content. Cobalt spinel oxides are cost-attractive but dissolve rapidly in acid as cobalt sites over-oxidize under anodic bias. Here we show that incorporation of d10-configured p-block cations (Sb, Ge, In, and Ga) into Co3O4 stabilizes cobalt sites by promoting robust heterometallic Co–O–M interactions. Density functional theory predicts dopant-driven charge redistribution that suppresses over-oxidation of octahedral Co while maintaining favorable binding of oxygen intermediates. Operando Co K-edge X-ray absorption and time-resolved dissolution measurements confirm reduced oxidation-state dynamics and cobalt loss, whereas a d-block d10 control (Zn) shows no such stabilization. In a PEMWE single cell at 80 °C, Sb/Co3O4 reaches >3500 mA cm–2 at 2.0 V and operates for >1000 h at 250 mA cm–2. This work establishes p-block d10 incorporation as a general route to iridium-free PEMWE anodes.
n2b243381fb6b: Developing robust multi-junction tandem photovoltaics remains constrained by the instability of mixed-halide perovskite subcells, given their dominating contribution to overall power output. Integrating near-infrared (NIR) PbS quantum dots (QDs) with FAPbBr3 and crystalline silicon (c-Si) broadens spectrum utilization while improving overall operational stability by reducing the perovskite power contribution. However, enlarged (100) facets and the trade-off between film thickness and quality limit efficient NIR photon harvesting. Herein, a Lewis-basic dihydrazide molecule achieves universal passivation across diverse PbS QD facets via synergistic lead chelation and hydrogen-bonding interactions. Consequently, 0.8 eV PbS QD solar cells with a 685 nm-thick active layer achieve a short-circuit current density of 41.31 mA cm–2 and a 1100-nm-filtered efficiency of 1.80%. The resulting FAPbBr3/c-Si/PbS triple-junction tandems achieve a promising efficiency of 31.04%, with the perovskite subcell contributing 30.4% of the total power output, demonstrating a well-matched operational lifetime. This work offers a strategic framework for efficient multi-junction tandem photovoltaics.
n9de84a3dfdc1: Pronounced heterogeneity and adaptability of tumors inherently curtail monotherapeutic efficacy, necessitating rationally integrated multimodal regimens that enable precise intervention, overcome resistance, and eradicate heterogeneous cell populations within the complex tumor microenvironment (TME). All-in-one mitochondria-targeted “nanomissiles” were created by emodin (Em)-Fe3+-gated, doxorubicin (DOX)-loaded PCN-600(FeIII) (denoted as DOX@ME) nanoparticles for synergistic multimodal tumor therapy integrating ferroptosis, photodynamic therapy (PDT), mild photothermal therapy (MPTT), and chemotherapy. DOX@ME achieved on-demand release of DOX in response to the TME [such as low pH, glutathione (GSH), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and adenosine-5′-triphosphate (ATP)] and near-infrared laser, via the disassembly of the Em-Fe3+ gating films and/or the degradation of the PCN-600(FeIII) nanocarriers. Under both 660 and 808 nm laser irradiation, DOX@ME effectively triggered apoptosis via chemotherapy, PDT, and MPTT while robustly accelerating reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, GSH depletion, glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) downregulation, and lipid peroxide (LPO) accumulation to enhance ferroptosis. Moreover, DOX@ME could alleviate thermotolerance by depleting intracellular ATP and downregulating protective heat shock protein 70 to boost the curative efficacy of MPTT. DOX@ME exhibited excellent antitumor efficacy and good biocompatibility and biosafety in A549 tumor-bearing nude mice. Collectively, DOX@ME demonstrates robust clinical translational potential for precision cancer therapy.
n04443ced010c: Effective glioblastoma therapy requires simultaneous solutions to poor blood–brain barrier (BBB) penetration, insufficient tumor-selective killing, and treatment-related systemic toxicity. We hypothesized that a BBB-penetrating nanoplatform capable of generating distinct H2S exposures in tumor and normal tissues could enhance antitumor efficacy while mitigating doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity. Here, DOX-loaded metastable molybdenum disulfide nanoflowers functionalized with an I6P8 peptide (DOX@MSI) were developed. After BBB transport and tumor accumulation, the acidic, H2O2-rich, and GSH-rich microenvironment accelerates nanoplatform degradation, promoting GSH depletion and enhanced H2S/DOX release. High local H2S upregulates xCT, while H2S/DOX-mediated mitochondrial inhibition suppresses NADPH regeneration, synergistically triggering disulfidptosis. Meanwhile, H2S suppresses the JAK2/STAT3/IDO axis, alleviating DOX-induced immunosuppression and enhancing immunogenic cell death and T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity. In contrast, slower degradation under physiological conditions enables sustained low-level H2S release, reducing the level of oxidative stress and ERK-associated apoptosis in cardiomyocytes. Together with NIR-enhanced photothermal therapy, DOX@MSI suppresses orthotopic glioblastoma while reducing cardiac injury, thereby integrating tumor-selective multimodal therapy with active organ protection.
n91d7aa2aa5b5: Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) self-assemble into cholesteric structures that enable sustainable photonic films, but controlling their pitch, domain morphology, and angular color response remains challenging. Here, we investigate how salt concentration and sonication dose jointly regulate the evaporation-induced self-assembly of CNC suspensions. Across 24 dish-cast films, polarized optical microscopy, time-lapse imaging, rheology, electron microscopy, and angle-resolved spectroscopy reveal that these processing parameters affect not only the cholesteric pitch but also tactoid nucleation, transport, coalescence, and the onset of kinetic arrest. Increasing NaCl concentration generally blue-shifts the photonic response, whereas sonication red-shifts it by fragmenting CNC bundles, with the magnitude of this effect decreasing as ionic content increases. At intermediate ionic content, low sonication doses produce extended cholesteric domains with comparatively narrow spectral responses, while the abundance of focal conic domains (FCDs) increases with sonication dose, culminating in FCD-rich films at moderate sonication. Refined parameter scans show that FCDs form within a finite processing window. Time-lapse imaging shows that FCDs appear abruptly after tactoid growth and coalescence, as macroscopic motion becomes strongly restricted during late-stage evaporation. Concentration- and residence-time-dependent rheology further demonstrates that the material response evolves throughout the assembly pathway. The FCD-rich film retains a narrow local reflection band while exhibiting the smallest angular displacement of the reflection maximum among the films examined. These findings show that salt and sonication regulate the kinetic accessibility of elastically driven focal conic structures, providing a route to tune domain morphology, spectral bandwidth, and iridescence in CNC photonic films.
n0db9f0de878d: Interlayer sliding in two-dimensional (2D) materials is generally assumed to be weakly anisotropic, even as low-symmetry layered crystals with strongly direction-dependent properties continue to emerge. Here we adopt a mechanics-guided conformal probe design that enables quantitative measurement of crystallographically resolved interlayer friction between anisotropic 2D materials. Using Ta2NiSe5 as a model system, we demonstrate pronounced interlayer friction anisotropy approaching 2 orders of magnitude, substantially larger than its moderate in-plane friction anisotropy and the values reported for high-symmetry layered materials. Atomic-resolution lateral force mapping reveals a hierarchical friction landscape composed of atomic lattice corrugation and twist-induced moiré modulation, with the moiré wavelength evolving systematically with relative misorientation. These results show that interlayer friction in low-symmetry 2D materials is governed by a multiscale, orientation-dependent potential energy landscape and constitutes an independent mechanical degree of freedom. The conformal probe platform provides a general route to probe and engineer direction-selective interlayer mechanics in van der Waals systems.
nf3c5c05acfd8: Delayed emission, a long-lived nonexponential photoluminescence tail, is widely observed in quantum dots (QDs), but its microscopic origin and relationship with blinking and the quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE) remain unclear. Here, we combine single-QD spectroscopy, time-gated photon analysis, and Monte Carlo simulations across CsPbX3 perovskite, CdSe-based, and InP-based QDs to identify a potential mechanism. Delayed emission correlates with band-edge carrier-trapping blinking, but is weak in QDs dominated by trion-mediated Auger blinking, suggesting delayed emission is not universally tied to charge-separated states. Delayed photons originate from nanosecond-scale carrier trapping and detrapping at nonradiative recombination centers: transiently trapped carriers return to the band edge and recombine radiatively. Time-gated analysis distinguishes this process from QCSE-driven intensity-lifetime fluctuations on slower blinking time scales. Furthermore, we demonstrate that delayed photons compromise the single-photon purity at a fixed excitation repetition rate. These findings establish a general framework of delayed emission in QDs.
nca8fa3e693a1: Uncontrolled Zn nucleation and growth at the electrode–electrolyte interface limit the reversibility and lifetime of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Nanoparticle (NP)-based anode protective layers are widely used to regulate Zn deposition, yet precise control over the exposed zincophilic facets of individual NPs remains challenging. Here, we show a facet-geometry engineering strategy based on threefold-symmetric Te nanoparticles (TF–Te NPs) to modulate Zn plating/stripping during cycling. The TF–Te NPs present a high density of zincophilic facets, while their threefold symmetric geometry spatially clusters nucleation sites within nanoscale proximity, promoting uniform Zn deposition and accelerating interfacial kinetics. As a result, TF–Te NP-modified Zn anodes exhibit reduced nucleation overpotentials, improved rate capability, and enhanced cycling stability. Our work establishes a direct link between NP geometry, facet-dependent zincophilicity, and Zn deposition behavior, offering a strategy for engineering NP protective layers across a broad range of aqueous batteries.
n2836f018169d: Carbonic anhydrase (CA) catalyzes CO2 hydration with turnover frequencies approaching 106 s–1, but native enzymes lack stability under conditions typical of industrial carbon capture. Small-molecule zinc mimics can be more stable under harsh conditions, but product inhibition by bicarbonate limits efficiency. A general framework for predicting turnover across ligand scaffolds has remained elusive. We report the analysis, by experiment and computation, of speciation and catalytic activity of zinc complexes as CA mimics. A literature data set of twelve Zn-ligand complexes was constructed, and the binding free energy (ΔGbind) of bicarbonate to zinc was calculated by DFT with DLPNO-CCSD(T) refinement. ΔGbind strongly correlates with the intrinsic rate constants of these Zn-ligand complexes for CO2 hydration with R2 = 0.90 at pH 9, 25 °C, and saturated CO2 (1 atm). By comparison, combining the commonly used descriptors ΣE(2), qZn, and %Vburied resulted in R2 = 0.74. Examining additional Zn catalysts (for example, the coordination species [ZnL4(OH)]+, where L is 1-methylimidazole) revealed that chemical speciation must be accounted for to describe the observed dependence of catalytic activity on ligand stoichiometry. Furthermore, accurate ranking of catalytic activity for several of the modified cyclens considered requires accounting for steric congestion (%Vburied), as ΔGbind alone does not capture active-site occlusion. These results define a transferable framework that integrates ΔGbind, speciation, and steric properties to enable the design of Zn-based CO2 hydration catalysts.
n26f49d4084d9: The ever-escalating accumulation of atmospheric CO2 and the growing demand for renewable energy conversion and storage have intensified research into solar-driven CO2 utilization technologies. Photothermal catalytic CO2 hydrogenation to methane has emerged as a promising approach for simultaneous carbon resource recycling and solar energy conversion, synergistically integrating the merits of photocatalysis and thermocatalysis. However, achieving high activity, selectivity, and long-term durability concurrently remains a central challenge, demanding precise control over photothermal conversion efficiency, charge transfer, and mass transport. Rational structural regulation spanning multiple length scales, from individual atoms to clusters, nanoparticles, and macroscopic reactors, is pivotal to overcoming such limitations. This review systematically summarizes research progress from a multiscale catalytic system design perspective, covering single atoms, nanoclusters, nanoparticles, supports, and macroscopic reactors. At each scale, the corresponding structure–activity relationships are analyzed, and the modulation mechanisms of active sites, photothermal effects, charge migration, and mass transport are elaborated. On this basis, we critically evaluate the advantages and bottlenecks of current research and put forward design guidelines and future development directions for next-generation high-performance catalytic systems. This review aims to provide both theoretical insights and practical references for the rational design of advanced photothermal CO2 methanation catalysts.
n2b35c9880e74: Ammonia decomposition provides a promising route for on-demand hydrogen production, but conventional thermocatalytic systems are constrained by severe kinetic limitations at low temperatures, limiting their compatibility with low-grade heat utilization. Herein, we develop an electric-field-assisted oxygen-vacancy engineering strategy to promote low-temperature NH3 decomposition over Ru/CeO2 catalysts. Ru/CeO2 catalysts with tunable oxygen-vacancy concentrations were prepared via a pre-impregnation and solid-state grinding method. Structural and spectroscopic characterizations reveal that oxygen vacancies intrinsically strengthen Ru–CeO2–x interfacial electronic interactions, promote charge redistribution, and generate relatively electron-enriched Ru sites. More importantly, the applied electric field further amplifies this vacancy-mediated interfacial regulation and facilitates H-species transfer/removal. The optimized Ru/CeO2-OV3 EF catalyst achieves 35.3% NH3 conversion at 150 °C under a high GHSV of 30,000 mL gcat–1 h–1 and exhibits an electric-field-assisted apparent activation energy of only 12.28 kJ mol–1. In situ DRIFTS, TPD measurements, impedance analysis, and DFT calculations collectively suggest that defect-associated O sites near oxygen vacancies provide favorable accommodation sites for migrated H species, while the electric field promotes interfacial polarization and accelerates H transfer from Ru sites to the CeO2–x surface. This synergistic effect reduces H coverage on Ru active centers, regenerates available Ru sites for sustained NH3 activation, and enables stable low-temperature operation. This work clarifies how an external electric field amplifies oxygen-vacancy-mediated interfacial electron/H transfer and provides a rational strategy for efficient low-temperature hydrogen production from ammonia.
nc20a192143aa: Chemical fixation of CO2 with CH3OH into value-added chemicals, such as dimethyl carbonate (DMC), plays a crucial role in carbon neutrality and resource recycling. However, its efficiency is limited by the ineffective synergistic activation of CO2 and CH3OH. Here, we employ a strategy to construct CeO2-CePO4 heterojunctions by phosphate-functionalized CeO2, introducing an asymmetric Ceδ+-O-P structure for CO2 and CH3OH activation. The prepared Ce0.8P0.2Oσ catalyst achieves a CH3OH conversion of 28.6% with nearly 100% DMC selectivity and retains its performance for 300 h during continuous DMC synthesis at 140 °C. Experimental characterization supports the formation of local Ceδ+-O-P sites in the catalyst. DFT calculations based on one selected idealized strained model containing a specific local Ceδ+-O-P site show a distinct Bader charge for Ce–O–P and Ce–O–Ce coordinated oxygen atoms within this model. Within the same model, the local Ceδ+-O-P site is associated with elongation of the C–O bond in CH3O* and a lower energy barrier for its dissociation into *CH3 and *O, providing a model-specific interpretation of the enhanced DMC yield. This work develops a design strategy for asymmetric catalytic site via composite oxide heterojunctions engineered for CO2 and CH3OH activation, exhibiting great potential for large-scale continuous CO2 chemical fixation to high-value-added chemicals.
nddaa440b2141: Valence dynamics of transition metals are central to oxygen evolution reaction (OER) mechanisms, yet in situ spectroscopic studies capturing these dynamics within amorphous catalysts remain limited. Here, we present in situ X-ray spectroscopy of amorphous catalysts, where CoBi exhibits higher OER performance compared to CoPi. While our data shows successive valence changes toward high-valent states in both catalysts, distinct initial electro-structural states dictate the intermediate evolution. Co(III) dominates in both catalysts at open-circuit potential, yet the Co(III)–O–Co(III) bridge structure observed in CoBi is absent in CoPi. Under active OER, Co(IV) species are identified as distinguishable spectral intensities; these are assigned to highly hybridized low-spin (LS) Co(IV) with reduced electron–electron repulsion, as validated by resonant inelastic X-ray spectroscopy (RIXS) analysis of Li0.75CoO2. Density functional theory supports the conversion from tetrahedral (Td) Co(II) to octahedral (Oh) Co(III) and suggests that factors other than thermodynamic pathways are likely responsible for the performance gap. The lower formal oxidation, larger Co–O length, smaller Co–O–Co angle, prominent pre-edge dipole character and absent oxo-bridging in CoPi suggest a kinetically inefficient Co(IV) state. These findings demonstrate that the initial electro-structure strongly influences the formation of productive high-valent active species and the resulting OER activity.
ne230db331c05: Solar-driven conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals provides an effective pathway for carbon resource utilization. However, the sluggish kinetics of CO2 reduction and the reliance on sacrificial electron donors limit its practical viability. Herein, we present a bifunctional photocatalyst consisting of spatially separated Ag2S and Au cocatalysts anchored on hollow CdS (Ag2S-Au/CdSH), which enables efficient concurrent CO2 photoreduction to CO and selective oxidation of aryl alcohols to benzaldehyde in a sacrificial-agent-free system. The rational integration of dual-active sites induces oriented charge flow, significantly enhancing photogenerated carrier separation and utilization, as evidenced by ultrafast spectroscopy showing extended electron lifetimes. This synergistic architecture delivers markedly higher production rates of 1.2 mmol g–1 h–1 for CO and 2.5 mmol g–1 h–1 for benzaldehyde, representing approximately 8-fold and 5-fold enhancements over pristine CdS, respectively. Comprehensive in situ spectroscopic studies combined with density functional theory calculations elucidate the distinct roles: Au sites strengthen CO2 adsorption and stabilize intermediates for reduction, while Ag2S promotes alcohol dehydrogenation. This synergistic dual-site architecture maximizes redox efficiency by matching reaction potentials and minimizing carrier recombination. This work provides mechanistic insights into catalyst design for integrated CO2 valorization and biomass upgrading, providing a basis for efficient chemical production.
n334c79cb8698: The selective oxyfunctionalization of C(sp3)–H bonds remains a central challenge in chemical synthesis. Although oxygenases and peroxygenases provide biocatalytic alternatives to metal-based chemical methods, their practical use is constrained by costly cofactor regeneration, toxic co-substrates, or limited selectivity. Molybdenum (Mo)-dependent alkyl dehydrogenases circumvent these limitations by employing water, rather than O2 or H2O2, as the oxygen source for hydroxylation in conjunction with an electron acceptor. Here, we combine enzymatic, structural, and computational analyses to characterize a Mo-dependent p-cymene dehydrogenase (pCDH) from an anaerobic hydrocarbon-degrading bacterium. Isolated pCDH selectively hydroxylates a variety of benzylic and allylic C(sp3)–H bonds. A 2.0 Å cryo-EM structure of the heterotrimeric enzyme in complex with p-cymene captures key states of the catalytic cycle. Structure-guided QM/MM modelling and docking rationalize the substrate scope and radical mechanism. These results identify water-dependent Mo-dehydrogenases as promising catalysts for selective C(sp3)–H oxyfunctionalization.
n80df4c9d9ab6: Efficient H2 dissociation and subsequent spillover of active hydrogen species are critical factors for achieving high activity in CO2 hydrogenation reactions. Herein, we constructed a well-designed and highly dispersed Cu–In bimetallic catalyst supported on CeO2. This catalyst enables the spatial separation of plasmonic enhancement, H2 activation, and CO2 conversion sites, thereby significantly improving H2 dissociation capability and H-spillover efficiency. Comprehensive investigations using multiple transient characterizations, together with in situ/operando spectroscopy, reveal that the three components are tightly coupled through H-spillover, electron transfer, and interfacial interactions. Specifically, the Ce sites on the CeO2 surface serve as the active centers for CO2 conversion via a redox mechanism, while the available indirect but consistent evidence suggests that In species likely act as the primary H2 dissociation sites, promoting the reduction of Cu species and the regeneration of oxygen vacancies on the CeO2 surface through H-spillover. Meanwhile, the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect of Cu significantly enhances the light absorption and photothermal conversion efficiency of the catalyst. The photoexcited LSPR electrons generated by Cu are further transferred to the In species and CeO2 surface, thereby facilitating H2 dissociation and the redox cycling of Ce sites. Such a “functional separation–synergistic enhancement” strategy effectively improves the catalytic activity, and the optimal catalyst achieves a CO yield of 230.1 mmol gcat–1 h–1 W–1 cm2 under 1.5 W cm–2 light irradiation at the surface temperature of 300 °C, significantly outperforming both the corresponding dark reaction and the monometallic Cu/CeO2 and In/CeO2 counterparts. This work provides important design principles and mechanistic insights for constructing highly active CO2 hydrogenation catalytic systems by enhancing H2 dissociation and H-spillover processes.
nb868a2c8a215: LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.
n615084cc7254: Hot carriers (HC) offer a potential route to surpass conventional efficiency limits in solar cells. Generated after light absorption, these high-energy carriers can significantly boost device performance if extracted before dissipating energy as heat. Although HC cooling has been studied in tin-based perovskites, interpreting these dynamics is challenging because high-energy, high-fluence pump pulses required to generate HCs have shallow penetration depths, confining excitation near the surface. In tin-based perovskites, surface properties differ from the bulk, and surface defects may strongly contribute to the optical response. Here, by using pump-push-probe ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, we photo-excite the semiconductor thin film with a low-energy pump, in a photon density range typical for solar cell operation, making relevant the bulk electronic properties, and selectively re-excite the photo-carriers only once they cool down, enabling direct tracking of HC relaxation in the relevant spectral region while minimizing surface contributions. We track the cooling process in FA0.85Cs0.15SnI3 (FA = Formamidinium) as a benchmark sample and extend the analysis to single-cation FA+, MA+ (MA = methylammonium), and Cs+ tin perovskites. Across all compositions, and at different doping densities, we find cooling timescales in the 150–600 fs time range. These results highlight the central role of phonon-mediated interactions and show that ultrafast cooling fundamentally limits hot carrier extraction in tin halide perovskites.
n472b3f592c93: Sodium-metal batteries present a more abundant alternative to lithium-based batteries, with high theoretical capacity and comparable reduction potential. Ether electrolytes perform well in sodium-metal batteries under continuous cycling and are presumed to have a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, the solubility of sodium SEI components is a cause for concern, and SEI evolution during calendar aging is not commonly studied for the ether sodium-metal system. In this work, SEI mass formation and dissolution are quantitatively measured for NaPF6 in diglyme. For varying potential hold levels, significant SEI dissolution is observed, from 55 to 76% of the originally formed SEI. Characterization shows that in addition to organic component dissolution, inorganic salts such as NaF and NaxPOyFz are unstable in SEI during open circuit rest. This instability results in continuous corrosion of sodium metal during calendar aging, highlighting an important understanding and concern of SEI stability in sodium-metal batteries.
n352917b010cd: Fast Na+ transport and durable interfacial stability remain challenging for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries. To address these issues, we developed a synergistic solvation-interphase regulation strategy by integrating methyl propanoate (MP) with a combined VC/NaDFOB additive pair. MP modifies the Na+ solvation sheath and facilitates Na+ desolvation, while VC and NaDFOB cooperatively generate a mechanically robust hybrid organicinorganic interphase. This coupled regulation enables enhanced ion transport and interfacial stability over a broad temperature range. The EC/EMC/MP + VC/NaDFOB electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.52 mS cm–1 at –40 ̊C and an increased Na+ transference number. Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells retain 96.5% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% at room temperature. At –20 ̊C, the cells deliver 69.4 mAh g–1 for over 900 cycles, corresponding to 82% of their room-temperature capacity. This work establishes a practical solvation-interphase regulation approach for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries.
n626efefab170: NMR chemical shifts are plainly transformed into machine learning features that have rational and intuitive chemical meaning. A small number of these features are used to predict molecular reactivity (via the HOMO-LUMO energy gap), resulting in a model that is not reliant on a priori knowledge of chemical structure or charge.
n6e245f30a071: This review discusses transferrable lessons and parameters from solution-based COF syntheses and small molecule mechanochemistry for the mechanochemical syntheses of imine and imine-derived COFs.
n81ff3f33c787: The development of ferroelectric materials relies on cation engineering of pure oxide systems. However, the discovery of new polar frameworks in pure oxides has become increasingly difficult because of their chemical and structural limitations. We report an approach to realize ferroelectricity in the n = 1 Ruddlesden−Popper (RP) family (A2BX4), a structure that is typically nonpolar in the oxide form because of its high crystalline symmetry. To stabilize the polar order in this rigid framework, we utilized anion engineering, specifically the partial substitution of O2− with F−. Although traditional topochemical fluorination requires a stable crystalline parent oxide, the parent n = 1 oxide Pb2MO4 (M = Fe, Co, Ni) is thermodynamically unstable and cannot be synthesized as a crystalline template. A low-temperature fluorination method using amorphous oxide film precursors was used to overcome this challenge. c-Axis-oriented epitaxial thin films of metastable Pb2M(O,F)4 were obtained, because a stable parent crystal was not required. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and electrical measurements (P−E) hysteresis and positive-up-negative-down (PUND) measurements confirmed that these layered oxyfluorides exhibited clear and switchable ferroelectricity. This behavior probably originates from the strong O/F anisotropy, which forces significant off-center cation displacements within the single perovskite layers. Thus, amorphous-based low-temperature fluorination provides a universal route for exploring novel functional materials across various mixed-anion systems.
n4d11072d1704: Lithium-conducting fluoride garnets exhibit ionic conductivities of ∼10–10 S cm–1, far below those of their oxide counterparts. Here, we investigate the origin of this poor transport in Na3Ga2Li3F12 and Na3Al2Li3F12 through a combination of structural characterization and first-principles calculations. Both compounds are highly ordered, with no significant antisite disorder, and exhibit intrinsic ionic conductivities of ∼2 × 10–11 S cm–1 at 100 °C. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal low Li-ion migration barriers (0.16 to 0.29 eV), indicating that the fluoride garnet framework does not inherently restrict Li-ion diffusion. However, the formation energies for lithium Frenkel and Schottky defect pairs are high (1.9 to 2.4 eV), indicating that the intrinsic concentrations of mobile Li-ion defects are negligibly small. These results establish that the low conductivity of stoichiometric fluoride garnets arises from high defect-formation energies, rather than high migration barriers.
nafc6148501c9: Reversible-deactivation radical photopolymerization (photoRDRP) enables precise spatiotemporal control of polymer architectures. Because of embedded active chain ends, photoRDRP offers straightforward reactivation and chain extension, providing unmatched flexibility for fine-tuning structural, mechanical, and physicochemical properties for targeted applications.
